title.zh: 卷一百八十三 列傳第一百三十三: 外戚
title.en: Volume 183 Biographies 133: Families of Imperial Consorts
title.raw: 卷一百八十三 列傳第一百三十三: 外戚 Volume 183 Biographies 133: Families of Imperial Consorts

meta.sourceNote: Body replaced from Wikisource raw text after ChineseNotes scrape due to glyph/encoding artifacts.

sentences.zh: 《語》曰：「無求生以害仁，有殺身以成仁。」

translations.literal: The Analects says: "Do not seek life in a way that harms humaneness; there is sacrificing one's body to fulfill humaneness.
translations.idiomatic: The Analects says, "One must not preserve one's life at the cost of benevolence, but may give one's life to complete benevolence.

sentences.zh: 孟軻曰：「生亦我所欲，義亦我所欲，舍生而取義可也。」

translations.literal: Mencius said: "Life is also what I desire; righteousness is also what I desire. If I cannot have both, I will abandon life and take righteousness."
translations.idiomatic: Mencius said, "Life is something I want, and righteousness is something I want too. If I cannot have both, I would rather surrender life and hold to righteousness."

sentences.zh: 古之德行君子，動必由禮，守之以仁，造次顛沛，不愆於素。

translations.literal: The virtuous gentlemen of antiquity in their conduct always followed ritual; they kept to benevolence; in haste and in hardship they did not depart from their constant nature.
translations.idiomatic: Men of virtue in ancient times acted always according to ritual and upheld benevolence; whether rushed or in distress, they never strayed from who they were.

sentences.zh: 有若仲由之結纓，鉏麑之觸樹，紀信之蹈火，豫讓之斬衣，此所謂殺身成仁，臨難不茍者也！

translations.literal: There were such as Zhong You tying his cap-cord, Chu Ni striking the tree, Ji Xin treading the fire, and Yu Rang cutting his garment—this is what is called sacrificing the body to fulfill benevolence, facing hardship without compromise!
translations.idiomatic: Zhong You binding his cap-strings, Chu Ni ramming the tree, Ji Xin walking into the flames, Yu Rang slashing his robe—these are the very men who "gave their lives to complete benevolence" and would not bend when disaster struck!

sentences.zh: 然受刑一代，顧瞻七族。

translations.literal: Yet when one receives punishment in a generation, one must look back upon seven clans.
translations.idiomatic: Yet to suffer capital punishment in one's own time is to bring ruin upon seven generations of kin.

sentences.zh: 不犯難者，有終身之利；

translations.literal: Those who do not court danger have profit for a lifetime;
translations.idiomatic: He who never risks his neck enjoys lifelong advantage;

sentences.zh: 隨市道者，獲當世之榮。

translations.literal: Those who follow the ways of the marketplace gain glory in the present age.
translations.idiomatic: while he who drifts with the crowd wins honor in his own day.

sentences.zh: 茍非氣義不群，貞剛絕俗，安能碎所重之支體，徇他人之義哉！

translations.literal: Unless one is uncongenial through valor and righteousness, upright and firm and removed from the vulgar, how could one shatter the body one holds dear and yield to another's sense of duty!
translations.idiomatic: Unless a man's spirit set him apart through loyalty and courage, his integrity absolute and far from the common run, how could he tear apart the body he treasured for the sake of someone else's cause!

sentences.zh: 則由、麑、信、讓之徒，君人者常宜血祀，況自有其臣乎！

translations.literal: Then such men as You, Ni, Xin, and Rang—a ruler should regularly offer them blood sacrifice; how much more when they are one's own subjects!
translations.idiomatic: Men like Zhong You, Chu Ni, Ji Xin, and Yu Rang ought to receive blood offerings from any lord—and how much more when they were his own officers!

sentences.zh: 即如安金藏剖腹以明皇嗣，段秀實挺笏而擊元凶，張巡、姚摐之守城，杲卿、真卿之罵賊，又愈於金藏。

translations.literal: Then again, such as An Jinzang, who cut open his belly to prove the imperial heir; Duan Xiushi, who raised his baton to strike the chief rebel; Zhang Xun and Yao Gun in defending cities; Gao Qing and Yan Zhenqing in reviling the rebels—these surpass Jinzang.
translations.idiomatic: And later figures surpassed even them—An Jinzang disemboweling himself to vindicate the heir, Duan Xiushi striking the rebel leader with his tablet, Zhang Xun and Yao Gun holding their cities, Yan Gaoqing and Yan Zhenqing cursing the invaders.

sentences.zh: 秀實等各見本傳。

translations.literal: Xiushi and the others are each treated in their original biographies.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Xiushi and the rest each have full accounts elsewhere in these annals.

sentences.zh: 今采夏侯端、李悽已下，附於此篇。

translations.literal: Now we have gathered Xiahou Duan, Li Chong, and those below them, and appended them to this chapter.
translations.idiomatic: Here we have selected Xiahou Duan, Li Chong, and the men who follow, and set their lives down in this chapter.

sentences.zh: 夏侯端夏侯端，壽州壽春人，梁尚書左僕射詳之孫也。

translations.literal: Xiahou Duan. Xiahou Duan was a native of Shouchun in Shou Prefecture, grandson of Xiang, Left Vice Director of the Secretariat of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Xiahou Duan was a native of Shouchun in Shou Prefecture and grandson of Xiang, who had served Liang as Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 仕隋為大理司直，高祖龍潛時，與其結交。

translations.literal: He served the Sui as a direct clerk in the Court of Judicial Review, and when Gaozu was still in obscurity they became friends.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Sui he was a direct clerk in the Court of Judicial Review; while Gaozu was still in private life, the two became close friends.

sentences.zh: 大業中，高祖帥師於河東討捕，乃請端為副。

translations.literal: In the Daye era, when Gaozu commanded troops at Hedong on punitive campaigns, Duan requested to serve as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daye reign, when Gaozu led troops from Hedong on pacification campaigns, Duan asked to serve as his second-in-command.

sentences.zh: 時煬帝幸江都，盜賊日滋。

translations.literal: At that time the Yang emperor was at Jiangdu, and bandits grew daily.
translations.idiomatic: The Yang emperor was then at Jiangdu, and banditry spread day by day.

sentences.zh: 端頗知玄象，善相人，說高祖曰：「金玉床搖動，此帝座不安。

translations.literal: Duan was well versed in celestial signs and skilled at reading faces. He told Gaozu: "The golden jade bed stirs—this means the imperial throne is unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: Duan knew celestial omens well and was skilled at physiognomy. He told Gaozu, "When the golden jade bed trembles, the imperial seat is unsettled.

sentences.zh: 參墟得歲，必有真人起於實沈之次。

translations.literal: When Shen and Xu receive the year's influence, a true man will surely arise in the quarter of Shi Chen.
translations.idiomatic: When Shen and Xu receive the year's influence, a true lord will surely rise in the quarter of Shi Chen.

sentences.zh: 天下方亂，能安之者，其在明公。

translations.literal: The realm is in turmoil; he who can pacify it—will it not be Your Lordship?
translations.idiomatic: The realm is in chaos; he who can pacify it—will it not be you, my lord?

sentences.zh: 但主上曉察，情多猜忍，切忌諸李，強者先誅，全才既死，明公豈非其次？

translations.literal: But the sovereign is sharp-sighted, much given to suspicion and cruelty; you must beware of all the Lis. The strong are executed first; when every able man is dead, will Your Lordship not be next?
translations.idiomatic: But the sovereign is sharp-eyed, suspicious and cruel; he is destroying every Li. The strongest are killed first—when all able men are gone, will you not be next?

sentences.zh: 若早為計，則應天福；

translations.literal: If you plan early, you will match Heaven's blessing;
translations.idiomatic: If you act in time, you will answer Heaven's mandate;

sentences.zh: 不然者，則誅矣！」

translations.literal: otherwise you will be put to death!
translations.idiomatic: otherwise you will be executed!

sentences.zh: 高祖深然其言。

translations.literal: Gaozu deeply agreed with his words.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was deeply persuaded by what he said.

sentences.zh: 及義師起，端在河東，為吏所捕，送於長安，囚之。

translations.literal: When the righteous army rose, Duan was at Hedong; officials arrested him and sent him to Chang'an, where he was imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: When the righteous army rose, Duan was at Hedong; officials seized him, sent him to Chang'an, and imprisoned him.

sentences.zh: 高祖入京城，釋之。

translations.literal: When Gaozu entered the capital, he released him.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu entered the capital, he set Duan free.

sentences.zh: 引入臥內，與語極歡，授秘書監。

translations.literal: He brought him into his bedchamber and talked with great delight, appointing him Director of the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: He brought him into his private chamber and spoke with him at great length in high spirits, then appointed him Director of the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 屬李密為王世充所破，以眾來降，關東之地，未有所屬。

translations.literal: When Li Mi was broken by Wang Shichong and came to surrender with his forces, the lands east of the Pass still had no master.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Mi was defeated by Wang Shichong and came over with his army, the lands east of the Pass still had no acknowledged ruler.

sentences.zh: 端固請往招諭之，乃加大將軍，持節為河南道招慰使。

translations.literal: Duan firmly requested to go recruit and reassure them; he was additionally made Grand General and given credentials as Pacification Commissioner for the Henan Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Duan pressed hard to go win them over; he was made Grand General and given credentials as Pacification Commissioner for the Henan Circuit.

sentences.zh: 至黎陽，李勣發兵送之，自澶水濟河，傳檄郡縣，東至於海，南至於淮，二十餘州，並遣使送款。

translations.literal: Reaching Liyang, Li Ji dispatched troops to escort him; he crossed the River from the Cang waters and issued proclamations through the commanderies and counties. East to the sea and south to the Huai, more than twenty prefectures all sent envoys to submit.
translations.idiomatic: At Liyang, Li Ji sent troops to escort him; he crossed the Yellow River from the Cang ford and issued proclamations through the commanderies and counties. From the sea in the east to the Huai in the south, more than twenty prefectures sent envoys to pledge allegiance.

sentences.zh: 行次譙州，會亳州刺史丁叔則及汴州刺史王要漢並以所部降於世充，路遂隔絕。

translations.literal: Stopping at Qiao Prefecture, he found that Qiao Prefect Ding Shize and Bian Prefect Wang Yaohan had both led their districts to surrender to Shichong, so the road was cut off.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Qiao Prefecture, he learned that Bo Prefect Ding Shize and Bian Prefect Wang Yaohan had both surrendered their districts to Shichong, cutting off his route.

sentences.zh: 端素得眾心，所從二千人，雖糧盡，不忍委去。

translations.literal: Duan had always won men's hearts; his two thousand followers, though food was gone, could not bear to leave him.
translations.idiomatic: Duan had long won men's hearts; though provisions were gone, his two thousand followers could not bring themselves to abandon him.

sentences.zh: 端知事必不濟，乃坐澤中，盡殺私馬，以會軍士。

translations.literal: Knowing success was impossible, he sat in a marsh, slaughtered all private horses, and shared them with the troops.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that the mission could not succeed, he halted in a marsh, slaughtered every private horse, and shared the meat with his men.

sentences.zh: 因歔欷曰：「今王師已敗，諸處並沒，卿等土壤，悉皆從偽，特以共事之情，未能見委。

translations.literal: Sighing he said: "Now the royal army has been defeated; everywhere is lost. Your homelands have all gone over to the pretender. Only because we have served together have I not been abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: He sighed and said, "The royal army is defeated and every district is lost. Your homelands have all submitted to the pretender. Only our time together keeps you from leaving me.

sentences.zh: 然我奉王命，不可從。

translations.literal: Yet I bear the king's commission and cannot follow them.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I hold the king's commission and cannot go over.

sentences.zh: 卿有妻子，無宜效我。

translations.literal: You have wives and children—you ought not to die as I shall.
translations.idiomatic: You have wives and children—you should not die as I must.

sentences.zh: 可斬吾首，持歸於賊，必獲富貴。」

translations.literal: You may cut off my head and carry it to the enemy; you will surely win riches.
translations.idiomatic: Cut off my head and carry it to the enemy—you will surely win wealth and rank.

sentences.zh: 眾皆流涕。

translations.literal: All wept.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone wept.

sentences.zh: 端又曰：「卿不忍見殺，吾當自刎。」

translations.literal: Duan said again: "If you cannot bear to kill me, I shall cut my own throat.
translations.idiomatic: Duan said again, "If you cannot bear to kill me, I will cut my own throat.

sentences.zh: 眾士抱持之，皆曰：「公於唐家，非有親屬，但以忠義之故，不辭於死。

translations.literal: The soldiers seized him, saying: "You have no kin in the house of Tang; it is solely for loyalty and righteousness that you will not shrink from death.
translations.idiomatic: The men seized him, crying, "You have no kin in the house of Tang; it is loyalty and righteousness alone that make you refuse to shrink from death.

sentences.zh: 諸人與公共事，經涉艱危，豈有害公而取富貴！」

translations.literal: We have shared your service through hardship—how could we harm you for wealth!
translations.idiomatic: We have shared hardship with you—how could we harm you for wealth and rank!

sentences.zh: 復與同進。

translations.literal: They pressed on together again.
translations.idiomatic: They pressed on together again.

sentences.zh: 潛行五日，餒死者十三四；

translations.literal: After marching five days in secret, a third or fourth had died of hunger;
translations.idiomatic: They marched in secret for five days, and a third or fourth of the men died of hunger;

sentences.zh: 又為賊所擊，奔潰相失者大半。

translations.literal: they were again struck by rebels and more than half scattered in flight.
translations.idiomatic: then rebels struck them again and more than half scattered in flight.

sentences.zh: 端唯與三十餘人東走，采生瑩豆而食之。

translations.literal: Duan had only thirty-odd men left going east, gathering wild beans and edible greens to eat.
translations.idiomatic: Duan had only thirty-odd men left heading east, gathering wild beans and edible greens to survive.

sentences.zh: 猶持節與之俱臥起，謂眾人曰：「平生不知死地乃在此中。

translations.literal: He still held his credentials and slept and rose with the men, telling them: "I never knew the land of death lay here.
translations.idiomatic: He still carried his credentials and slept and rose with them, telling the men, "I never knew the land of death was here.

sentences.zh: 我受國恩，所以然耳，今卿等何乃相伴死乎！

translations.literal: I received the state's grace—that is why it is so. Why then do you share death with me!
translations.idiomatic: I received the state's grace—that is why I am here. Why should you die with me!

sentences.zh: 可散投賊，猶全性命。

translations.literal: Scatter and join the enemy; you may yet save your lives.
translations.idiomatic: Scatter and join the rebels—you may yet save your lives.

sentences.zh: 吾當抱此一節，與之俱殞。」

translations.literal: I will clasp this seal alone and perish with it.
translations.idiomatic: I will keep this seal to my breast and die with it.

sentences.zh: 眾又不去。

translations.literal: The men would not leave.
translations.idiomatic: The men would not leave him.

sentences.zh: 屬李公逸為唐守杞州，聞而勒兵迎館之。

translations.literal: When Li Gongyi, Tang loyalist at Qi Prefecture, heard of it he led troops out to receive and lodge him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gongyi was holding Qi Prefecture for Tang; when he heard of Duan's plight he led troops out to receive and shelter him.

sentences.zh: 於時河南之地，皆入世充，唯公逸感端之義，獨堅守不下。

translations.literal: At that time all Henan had fallen to Shichong; only Gongyi, moved by Duan's righteousness, held his city and would not submit.
translations.idiomatic: By then all of Henan had submitted to Shichong; only Gongyi, moved by Duan's example, held his city and refused to yield.

sentences.zh: 世充遣使召端，解衣遺之。

translations.literal: Shichong sent envoys to summon Duan, sending clothes as gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong sent envoys to summon Duan and presented him with gifts of clothing.

sentences.zh: 禮甚厚，仍送除書，以端為淮南郡公、吏部尚書。

translations.literal: The courtesy was very great; they also brought an appointment making Duan Duke of Huainan and Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: The courtesy was lavish; they also brought an appointment naming him Duke of Huainan and Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 端對其使者曰：「夏侯端天子大使，豈受王世充之官！

translations.literal: Duan told the envoys: "Xiahou Duan is the Son of Heaven's grand envoy—how should he take office from Wang Shichong!
translations.idiomatic: Duan told the envoys, "Xiahou Duan is the Son of Heaven's grand envoy—how could he accept office from Wang Shichong!

sentences.zh: 自非斬我頭將往見汝，何容身茍活而屈於賊乎！」

translations.literal: Unless you carry off my head to show him, how could I keep my body alive and bow to the rebel!
translations.idiomatic: Unless you carry off my head to show him, how could I keep my body alive and bow to a rebel!

sentences.zh: 遂焚其書，拔刀斬其所遺衣服。

translations.literal: He burned their letter and drew his sword to slash the clothes they had brought.
translations.idiomatic: He burned their letter, drew his sword, and slashed the clothes they had brought.

sentences.zh: 因發路西歸，解節旄懷之，取竿加刃，從間道得至宜陽。

translations.literal: Then he set out west; he took off the seal-tassels and hid them in his breast, fixed a blade to a pole, and by secret paths reached Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Then he set out west, hid the seal-tassels in his breast, fixed a blade to a pole, and by secret paths reached Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 初，山中險峻，先無蹊徑，但冒履榛梗，晝夜兼行，從者三十二人，或墜崖溺水、遇猛獸而死又半，其餘至者，皆鬢髮禿落，形貌枯瘠。

translations.literal: At first the mountains were perilous with no path; they forced their way through thorns day and night. Of thirty-two followers, some fell from cliffs, drowned, or were killed by wild beasts—half again were lost; the rest who arrived had hair fallen out and faces wasted.
translations.idiomatic: At first the mountains were trackless and steep; they forced their way through thorns day and night. Of thirty-two followers, some fell from cliffs, drowned, or were killed by wild beasts—half were lost again; those who arrived had hair fallen out and faces gaunt with hunger.

sentences.zh: 端馳驛奉見，但謝無功，殊不自言艱苦。

translations.literal: Duan rode post-haste to an audience and thanked the emperor only for failing; he said nothing at all of his hardships.
translations.idiomatic: Duan rode post-haste to audience and apologized only for failing; he said nothing of his hardships.

sentences.zh: 高祖憫之，復以為秘書監。

translations.literal: Gaozu pitied him and made him Director of the Palace Library again.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu pitied him and again appointed him Director of the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 俄出為梓州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon after he went out as Prefect of Zizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he was sent out as Prefect of Zizhou.

sentences.zh: 所得料錢，皆散施孤寡。

translations.literal: The stipends he received he gave entirely to orphans and the destitute.
translations.idiomatic: Every stipend he received he gave away to orphans and the destitute.

sentences.zh: 病卒。

translations.literal: He died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He died of illness.

sentences.zh: 劉感劉感，岐州鳳泉人，後魏司徒高昌王豐生之孫也。

translations.literal: Liu Gan. Liu Gan was a native of Fengquan in Qi Prefecture, grandson of Fengsheng, Prince of Gaochang and Minister over the Masses of Later Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Gan was a native of Fengquan in Qi Prefecture and grandson of Fengsheng, Prince of Gaochang and Minister over the Masses of Northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 武德初，以驃騎將軍鎮涇州。

translations.literal: In early Wude he was made General of Agile Cavalry and defended Jing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In early Wude he was made General of Agile Cavalry and stationed at Jing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 薛仁杲率眾圍之。

translations.literal: Xue Rengao led masses to besiege him.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Rengao led a host to besiege the city.

sentences.zh: 感嬰城拒守，城中糧盡，遂殺所乘馬以分將士，感一無所啖，唯煮馬骨取汁，和木屑食之。

translations.literal: Gan closed the city and resisted; when grain was exhausted he killed his own horse to divide among the officers and men. Gan ate nothing himself—only boiled the horse bones for broth and mixed it with wood shavings to eat.
translations.idiomatic: Gan shut the gates and held out; when grain ran out he killed his own horse to share among the troops. He ate nothing himself—only boiled the horse bones for broth and mixed it with wood shavings.

sentences.zh: 城垂陷者數矣。

translations.literal: The city nearly fell many times.
translations.idiomatic: The city nearly fell many times.

sentences.zh: 長平王叔良援兵至，仁杲解圍而去。

translations.literal: Prince of Changping, Shuliang, arrived with rescue troops and Rengao lifted the siege and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Changping, Shuliang, arrived with relief troops and Rengao lifted the siege and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 感與叔良出戰，為賊所擒。

translations.literal: Gan and Shuliang went out to fight and were captured by the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Gan and Shuliang went out to fight and were captured.

sentences.zh: 仁杲復圍涇州，令感語城中云：「援軍已敗，徒守孤城，何益也！

translations.literal: Rengao again besieged Jing and made Gan address the city: "The relief army is defeated; what use to hold a lone city!
translations.idiomatic: Rengao again besieged Jing and made Gan call to the city, "The relief army is defeated—what use is there in holding a lone city!

sentences.zh: 宜早出降，以全家室。」

translations.literal: You should surrender early to save your families.
translations.idiomatic: Surrender at once and save your families.

sentences.zh: 感許之。

translations.literal: Gan agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Gan agreed.

sentences.zh: 及至城下，大呼曰：「逆賊饑餓，亡在朝夕！

translations.literal: When he reached the foot of the wall he shouted loudly: "The rebels are starving; destruction is only days away!
translations.idiomatic: When he reached the foot of the wall he shouted, "The rebels are starving—ruin is only days away!

sentences.zh: 秦王率數十萬眾，四面俱集，城中勿憂，各宜自勉，以全忠節！」

translations.literal: The Prince of Qin leads hundreds of thousands; they are gathering on every side. Do not worry within the walls—each of you should steel yourselves and preserve loyalty unto death!
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qin leads hundreds of thousands and is closing in on every side. Do not despair—steel yourselves and hold to loyalty unto death!

sentences.zh: 仁杲大怒，執感於城邊，埋腳至膝，馳騎射殺之，至死聲色逾厲。

translations.literal: Rengao was furious, seized him at the wall, buried him to the knees, and had horsemen ride shooting at him until death; to the end his voice and bearing grew fiercer.
translations.idiomatic: Rengao was furious; he seized Gan at the wall, buried him to the knees, and had horsemen ride past shooting at him until he died—his voice and bearing fiercer to the last.

sentences.zh: 賊平，高祖購得其屍，祭以少牢，贈瀛州刺史，封平原郡公，謚曰忠壯。

translations.literal: When the rebels were pacified, Gaozu bought back his corpse, sacrificed to it with a lesser victim, made him Prefect of Ying, enfeoffed him as Duke of Pingyuan, and gave the posthumous title Zhongzhuang (Loyal and Stalwart).
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels were crushed, Gaozu bought back his body, sacrificed to it with a lesser victim, made him Prefect of Ying, enfeoffed him as Duke of Pingyuan, and gave him the posthumous title Loyal and Stalwart.

sentences.zh: 令其子襲官爵，並賜田宅。

translations.literal: He ordered his son to inherit rank and offices and granted him fields and houses.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Gan's son to inherit his rank and offices and granted him fields and houses.

sentences.zh: 常達常達，陜人也。

translations.literal: Chang Da. Chang Da was a man of Shan.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Da was a native of Shan.

sentences.zh: 初仕隋為鷹揚郎將，數從高祖征伐，甚蒙親待。

translations.literal: He first served the Sui as an Eagle-Flying Captain and often followed Gaozu on campaigns, receiving very close favor.
translations.idiomatic: He first served the Sui as an Eagle-Flying Captain and often followed Gaozu on campaign, enjoying his close favor.

sentences.zh: 及義兵起，達在霍邑，從宋老生來拒戰。

translations.literal: When the righteous army rose, Da was at Huoyi and came with Song Laosheng to resist the fight.
translations.idiomatic: When the righteous army rose, Da was at Huoyi and came with Song Laosheng to resist.

sentences.zh: 老生敗，達懼，自匿不出。

translations.literal: Laosheng was defeated; in fear Da hid himself and did not come out.
translations.idiomatic: Laosheng was defeated; in fear Da hid himself and did not emerge.

sentences.zh: 高祖謂達已死，令人閱屍求之。

translations.literal: Gaozu thought Da was already dead and had men search the corpses for him.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu thought Da was dead and had men search the corpses for him.

sentences.zh: 及達奉見，高祖大悅，以為統軍。

translations.literal: When Da came to an audience Gaozu was greatly pleased and made him army commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Da presented himself, Gaozu was overjoyed and made him army commander.

sentences.zh: 武德初，拜隴州刺史。

translations.literal: In early Wude he was appointed Prefect of Long.
translations.idiomatic: In early Wude he was appointed Prefect of Long.

sentences.zh: 時薛舉屢攻之，不能克，乃遣其將仵士政以數百人偽降達。

translations.literal: At that time Xue Ju repeatedly attacked but could not take the city; he sent his general Wu Shizheng with several hundred men to feign surrender to Da.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Ju attacked repeatedly but could not take the city; he sent his general Wu Shizheng with several hundred men to feign surrender.

sentences.zh: 達不之測，厚加撫接。

translations.literal: Da could not discern it and treated them warmly.
translations.idiomatic: Da could not see through the ruse and treated them warmly.

sentences.zh: 士政伺隙以其徒劫達，擁城中二千人而叛，牽達以見於舉。

translations.literal: Shizheng seized his chance and with his men seized Da, holding the city's two thousand men in revolt, and led Da before Ju.
translations.idiomatic: Shizheng seized his chance, seized Da with his men, rallied the city's two thousand troops in revolt, and led Da before Ju.

sentences.zh: 達詞色抗厲，不為之屈。

translations.literal: Da's words and bearing were defiant; he would not submit.
translations.idiomatic: Da's words and bearing were defiant; he would not yield.

sentences.zh: 舉指其妻謂達曰：「識皇后否？」

translations.literal: Ju pointed at his wife and said to Da, "Do you recognize the empress?
translations.idiomatic: Ju pointed at his wife and said to Da, "Do you recognize the empress?

sentences.zh: 達曰：「正是癭老嫗，何足可識！」

translations.literal: Da said, "She is just that goitered old hag—why should she be worth recognizing!
translations.idiomatic: Da said, "She is just that goitered old hag—why should she be worth recognizing!

sentences.zh: 竟釋之。

translations.literal: Ju released him in the end.
translations.idiomatic: Ju released him in the end.

sentences.zh: 有賊帥張貴謂達曰：「汝識我否？」

translations.literal: A rebel chief Zhang Gui said to Da, "Do you know me?
translations.idiomatic: A rebel chief Zhang Gui said to Da, "Do you know me?

sentences.zh: 答曰：「汝逃死奴。」

translations.literal: He answered, "You are a runaway slave condemned to death."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "You are a runaway slave condemned to death."

sentences.zh: 瞋目視之，貴怒，拔刀將斫達。

translations.literal: Staring at him with bulging eyes, Gui in anger drew his sword to hack Da down.
translations.idiomatic: Staring at him with bulging eyes, Gui drew his sword in anger to strike Da down.

sentences.zh: 人救之，獲免。

translations.literal: Men rescued him and he escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Others restrained him and Da was spared.

sentences.zh: 及仁杲平，高祖見達，謂曰：「卿之忠節，便可求之古人。」

translations.literal: When Rengao was pacified Gaozu saw Da and said, "Your loyalty and firmness—such could be sought among the ancients.
translations.idiomatic: When Rengao was pacified Gaozu saw Da and said, "Your loyalty and steadfastness are the equal of the ancients.

sentences.zh: 命起居舍人令狐德棻曰：「劉感、常達，須載之史策也。」

translations.literal: He told the recorder Linghu Defen, "Liu Gan and Chang Da must be entered in the historical records."
translations.idiomatic: He told the recorder Linghu Defen, "Liu Gan and Chang Da must be entered in the historical records."

sentences.zh: 執仵士政，撲殺之。

translations.literal: They seized Wu Shizheng and beat him to death.
translations.idiomatic: They seized Wu Shizheng and beat him to death.

sentences.zh: 賜達布帛三百段，復拜隴州刺史，卒。

translations.literal: They gave Da three hundred bolts of silk and cloth and again appointed him Prefect of Long; he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: They gave Da three hundred bolts of silk and cloth, again appointed him Prefect of Long, and he died in office.

sentences.zh: 羅士信羅士信，齊州歷城人也。

translations.literal: Luo Shixin—Luo Shixin was a man of Licheng in Qi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Shixin was a native of Licheng in Qi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 大業中，長白山賊王簿、左才相、孟讓來寇齊郡，通守張須陀率兵討擊。

translations.literal: In the Daye era, the bandits of Mount Changbai—Wang Bo, Zuo Caixiang, and Meng Rang—came to raid Qi Commandery; Commissioner Zhang Xutuo led troops to attack and suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daye reign, the Mount Changbai bandits Wang Bo, Zuo Caixiang, and Meng Rang raided Qi Commandery, and Commissioner Zhang Xutuo led troops against them.

sentences.zh: 士信年始十四，固請自效。

translations.literal: Shixin was only fourteen years old; he firmly requested to offer his own service.
translations.idiomatic: Shixin was only fourteen, yet he begged insistently to be allowed to serve.

sentences.zh: 須陀謂曰：「汝形容未勝衣甲，何可入陣！」

translations.literal: Xutuo said to him, "Your frame cannot yet bear armor—how could you enter the battle line!
translations.idiomatic: Xutuo told him, "Your body is not yet strong enough for armor—how can you go into battle!

sentences.zh: 士信怒，重著二甲，左右雙鞬而上馬，須陀壯而從之。

translations.literal: Shixin grew angry, put on two suits of armor, slung a pair of quivers left and right, mounted his horse, and Xutuo, admiring his spirit, allowed him to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Shixin donned double armor, strapped quivers to both sides, mounted, and Xutuo, impressed by his mettle, let him come along.

sentences.zh: 擊賊濰水之上。

translations.literal: They attacked the bandits on the Wei River.
translations.idiomatic: They engaged the bandits along the Wei River.

sentences.zh: 陣才列，士信馳至賊所，刺倒數人，斬一人首，擲於空中，用槍承之，戴以略陣。

translations.literal: The formation had barely been drawn up when Shixin galloped to where the bandits stood, stabbed several men down, cut off one man's head, tossed it into the air, caught it on his spear, and wore it as he rode around the formation.
translations.idiomatic: Hardly had the line formed when Shixin charged into the enemy ranks, felled several men, severed one head, tossed it skyward, caught it on his spear, and paraded it before the array.

sentences.zh: 賊眾愕然，無敢逼者；

translations.literal: The bandit masses were stunned; none dared press close.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits stood dumbfounded; not one dared advance.

sentences.zh: 須陀因而奮擊，賊眾大潰。

translations.literal: Xutuo thereupon struck with renewed force, and the bandit masses broke in great rout.
translations.idiomatic: Xutuo pressed the advantage, and the bandits broke and fled in utter disorder.

sentences.zh: 士信逐北，每殺一人，輒劓其鼻而懷之；

translations.literal: Shixin pursued the fleeing foe; each time he killed a man, he cut off the nose and kept it on his person.
translations.idiomatic: Shixin chased down the retreating enemy, and for every man he killed he sliced off the nose and carried it with him.

sentences.zh: 及還，則驗鼻以表殺賊之多少也。

translations.literal: When he returned, he checked the noses to show how many bandits he had killed.
translations.idiomatic: Back in camp, he counted the noses to prove how many enemies he had slain.

sentences.zh: 須陀甚加嘆賞，以所乘馬遺之，引置左右。

translations.literal: Xutuo greatly praised and rewarded him, gave him the horse he himself rode, and kept him at his side.
translations.idiomatic: Xutuo was deeply impressed, gave him his own mount, and kept him close at hand.

sentences.zh: 每戰，須陀先登，士信為副。

translations.literal: In every battle, Xutuo would be first up; Shixin served as his second.
translations.idiomatic: In every fight Xutuo led the charge, with Shixin right behind him.

sentences.zh: 煬帝遣使慰喻之，又令畫工寫須陀、士信戰陣之圖，上於內史。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang sent envoys to comfort and commend them, and also ordered painters to depict Xutuo and Shixin in battle, submitting the pictures to the Inner Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang dispatched envoys to praise them and had artists paint scenes of Xutuo and Shixin in battle, which were sent up to the Inner Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 及須陀為李密所殺，士信隨裴仁基率眾歸於密，署為總管。

translations.literal: When Xutuo was killed by Li Mi, Shixin followed Pei Renji in leading the masses to submit to Mi, who appointed him general commander.
translations.idiomatic: After Xutuo was killed by Li Mi, Shixin followed Pei Renji and brought their forces over to Mi, who made him a general commander.

sentences.zh: 使統所部，隨密擊王世充。

translations.literal: He was made to command his own forces and followed Mi in attacking Wang Shichong.
translations.idiomatic: He was put in charge of his own troops and joined Mi in the assault on Wang Shichong.

sentences.zh: 敗，士信躍馬突進，身中數矢，乃陷於世充軍。

translations.literal: When they were defeated, Shixin leapt his horse and charged forward; he was struck by several arrows and finally fell into Shichong's army.
translations.idiomatic: When the battle was lost, Shixin spurred his horse forward in a desperate charge, took several arrows, and was finally overrun by Shichong's troops.

sentences.zh: 世充知其驍勇，厚禮之，與同寢食。

translations.literal: Shichong, knowing his fierce bravery, treated him with lavish honor and ate and slept with him.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong, recognizing his valor, showered him with honors and shared his meals and quarters.

sentences.zh: 後世充破李密，得密將邴元真等，盡拜為將軍，不復專重之。

translations.literal: Later, when Shichong defeated Li Mi and obtained Mi's generals Bing Yuanzhen and others, he all appointed them as generals and no longer singled Shixin out for special favor.
translations.idiomatic: Later, after Shichong crushed Li Mi and took Mi's generals Bing Yuanzhen and the rest, he made them all commanders and no longer treated Shixin with special distinction.

sentences.zh: 士信恥與為伍，率所部千餘人奔於谷州。

translations.literal: Shixin was ashamed to be their companion; he led his troops of more than a thousand men and fled to Gu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed to stand among them, Shixin led more than a thousand of his men and fled to Gu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 高祖以為陜州道行軍總管，使圖世充。

translations.literal: Gaozu appointed him route-army commander of the Shaanzhou Circuit and sent him to besiege Shichong.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu made him route-army commander on the Shaanzhou circuit and ordered him to move against Wang Shichong.

sentences.zh: 及大軍至洛陽，士信以兵圍世充千金堡。

translations.literal: When the great army reached Luoyang, Shixin used his troops to surround Shichong's Qianjin Fort.
translations.idiomatic: When the main force reached Luoyang, Shixin laid siege to Shichong's Qianjin Fort.

sentences.zh: 中有大罵之者，士信怒，夜遣百餘人將嬰兒數十至於堡下，詐言「從東都來投羅總管」。

translations.literal: Someone inside loudly cursed him; Shixin grew angry and by night sent more than a hundred men with several dozen infants to the foot of the fort, falsely saying, "We have come from the Eastern Capital to surrender to Commander Luo."
translations.idiomatic: When someone inside hurled abuse at him, Shixin flew into a rage and by night sent a hundred-odd men carrying several dozen infants to the foot of the fort, pretending they had fled the Eastern Capital to join Commander Luo.

sentences.zh: 因令嬰兒啼噪，既而佯驚曰：「此千金堡，吾輩錯矣！」

translations.literal: He then had the infants cry and wail; afterward he feigned alarm and said, "This is Qianjin Fort—we have gone wrong!
translations.idiomatic: He set the infants wailing, then pretended to panic and cried, "This is Qianjin Fort—we've come to the wrong place!

sentences.zh: 忽然而去。

translations.literal: Suddenly they departed.
translations.idiomatic: Then they abruptly withdrew.

sentences.zh: 堡中謂是東都逃人，遽出兵追之。

translations.literal: Those in the fort took them for fugitives from the Eastern Capital and hurriedly sent troops out in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison assumed they were refugees from the Eastern Capital and rushed troops out in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 士信伏兵於路，俟其開門，奮擊大破之，殺無遺類。

translations.literal: Shixin had hid troops along the road; when they opened the gate he struck with fury and utterly defeated them, killing every last man.
translations.idiomatic: Shixin had men lying in ambush along the road; as soon as the gate opened he fell upon them and wiped out the garrison to the last man.

sentences.zh: 世充平，擢授絳州總管，封剡國公。

translations.literal: When Shichong was pacified, Shixin was promoted and appointed Prefect of Jiang Prefecture and enfeoffed as Duke of Shan.
translations.idiomatic: After Shichong's defeat, Shixin was promoted to Prefect of Jiang and enfeoffed as Duke of Shan.

sentences.zh: 尋從太宗擊劉黑闥於河北，有洺水人以城來降，遣士信入城據守。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he followed Taizong in attacking Liu Heita in Hebei; men of Ming city came over with the city in surrender, and he sent Shixin to enter the city and hold it.
translations.idiomatic: He soon followed Taizong against Liu Heita in Hebei; when the people of Ming surrendered their city, Taizong sent Shixin in to hold it.

sentences.zh: 賊悉眾攻之甚急，遇雨雪，大軍不得救，經數日，城陷，為賊所擒。

translations.literal: The bandits gathered all their forces and attacked with extreme urgency; rain and snow fell, the great army could not rescue him, and after several days the city fell and he was captured by the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels threw their full strength against the city; rain and snow blocked relief, and after several days the walls fell and Shixin was taken.

sentences.zh: 黑闥聞其勇，意欲活之；

translations.literal: Heita, hearing of his bravery, wished to keep him alive.
translations.idiomatic: Heita, impressed by his courage, wanted to spare his life.

sentences.zh: 士信詞色不屈，遂遇害，年二十。

translations.literal: Shixin's words and bearing were unyielding; he was thereupon killed, aged twenty.
translations.idiomatic: Shixin refused to yield in word or bearing, and was put to death at the age of twenty.

sentences.zh: 太宗聞而傷惜，購得其屍，葬之，謚曰勇。

translations.literal: When Taizong heard of it he grieved; he ransomed and recovered his corpse, buried him, and gave him the posthumous title Courageous.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong mourned the loss, paid to recover his body, gave him burial, and posthumously titled him Courageous.

sentences.zh: 士信初為裴仁基所禮，嘗感其知己之恩，及東都平，遂以家財收斂，葬於北邙。

translations.literal: At first Shixin had been treated with courtesy by Pei Renji and had felt gratitude for his recognition; when the Eastern Capital was pacified, he used his family's wealth to gather and bury Renji on Northern Mount Mang.
translations.idiomatic: Shixin had once been honored by Pei Renji and never forgot that debt; when the Eastern Capital fell, he spent his family's fortune to recover Renji's remains and bury them on Northern Mount Mang.

sentences.zh: 又云：「我死後，當葬此墓側。」

translations.literal: He also said, "After my death, bury me beside this tomb.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "When I die, lay me to rest beside this grave.

sentences.zh: 及卒，果就仁基左而托葬焉。

translations.literal: When he died, it was indeed to Renji's left that he was laid to rest.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, he was buried as he had wished, at Renji's left hand.

sentences.zh: 呂子臧呂子臧，蒲州河東人也。

translations.literal: Lü Zizang—Lü Zizang was a man of Hedong in Pu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Zizang was a native of Hedong in Pu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 大業末，為南陽郡丞。

translations.literal: At the end of the Daye reign he served as assistant prefect of Nanyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Daye era he served as assistant prefect of Nanyang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 高祖克京師，遣馬元規撫慰山南，子臧堅守不下，元規遣使諷諭之，前後數輩，皆為子臧所殺。

translations.literal: When Gaozu captured the capital he dispatched Ma Yuangui to soothe and reassure the regions south of the mountains; Zizang held firm and would not surrender. Yuangui sent envoys to persuade him, several parties in succession, and Zizang killed them all.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the capital he sent Ma Yuangui to pacify the country south of the mountains, but Zizang held out and refused to submit. Yuangui sent envoy after envoy to win him over, and Zizang killed every one.

sentences.zh: 及煬帝被殺，高祖又遣其婿薛君倩賫手詔諭旨，子臧乃為煬帝發喪成禮。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang was killed, Gaozu again sent his son-in-law Xue Junqian bearing an imperial letter to convey his intent, and only then did Zizang perform the full rites of mourning for Emperor Yang.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Yang was killed, Gaozu sent his son-in-law Xue Junqian with an imperial letter, and only then did Zizang observe the full mourning rites for the late emperor.

sentences.zh: 而後歸國，拜鄧州刺史，封南陽郡公。

translations.literal: Afterward he submitted to the realm; he was appointed Prefect of Deng and enfeoffed as Duke of Nanyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He then submitted to the Tang and was appointed Prefect of Deng and enfeoffed as Duke of Nanyang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 時朱粲新敗，子臧率所部數千人，與元規並力將擊之。

translations.literal: At that time Zhu Can had just been defeated; Zizang led several thousand of his own troops and joined Yuangui in a combined effort to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Can had just suffered a defeat, and Zizang led several thousand of his own men to join Yuangui in a joint strike.

sentences.zh: 謂元規曰：「朱粲新破之後，上下危懼，一戰可擒。

translations.literal: He said to Yuangui, "After Zhu Can's fresh defeat, his men high and low are fearful and alarmed—one battle will take him.
translations.idiomatic: He told Yuangui, "Zhu Can's men are still shaken from defeat; one hard fight and we can take him.

sentences.zh: 若更遷延，部眾稍集，力強食盡，必死戰於我，為患不細也。」

translations.literal: If we delay further, his troops will gradually gather, his strength grow, and his food run out; he will surely fight to the death against us, and the harm will not be slight.
translations.idiomatic: If we wait, his forces will regroup, grow stronger, and run out of food—and then they will fight us to the death. The damage will be far from small.

sentences.zh: 元規不納，子臧請以本兵獨戰，又不許。

translations.literal: Yuangui did not accept this; Zizang requested to fight alone with his own troops, and again permission was denied.
translations.idiomatic: Yuangui refused to listen; when Zizang asked to fight with his own troops alone, he was again denied.

sentences.zh: 俄而粲眾大至，元規懼，退保南陽。

translations.literal: Before long Can's masses arrived in strength; Yuangui grew afraid and withdrew to hold Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Zhu Can's army arrived in force; Yuangui panicked and fell back to defend Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 子臧謂元規曰：「言不見納，以至於此，老夫今坐公死矣！」

translations.literal: Zizang said to Yuangui, "My words went unheard, and we have come to this—this old man will now sit here and die on your account!
translations.idiomatic: Zizang said to Yuangui, "You would not heed me, and now we are here—this old man will die sitting here because of you!

sentences.zh: 粲果率兵圍之，遇霖雨，城壁皆壞，所親者知城必陷，固勸其降。

translations.literal: Can indeed led troops to surround them; constant rains fell and the walls all collapsed; those close to him knew the city must fall and firmly urged him to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Can duly besieged the city; weeks of rain ruined the walls, and those closest to Zizang, seeing the fall was inevitable, pressed him to surrender.

sentences.zh: 子臧曰：「安有天子方伯降賊者乎！」

translations.literal: Zizang said, "How could there be an imperial regional governor who surrenders to bandits!
translations.idiomatic: Zizang said, "What imperial governor ever surrendered to bandits!

sentences.zh: 於是率其麾下，赴敵而死。

translations.literal: Thereupon he led his followers to meet the enemy and died.
translations.idiomatic: He then led his men out to face the enemy and was killed.

sentences.zh: 俄而城陷，元規亦遇害。

translations.literal: Before long the city fell, and Yuangui was also killed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the city fell, and Yuangui was killed as well.

sentences.zh: 張道源張道源，并州祁人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Daoyuan—Zhang Daoyuan was a man of Qi in Bing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Daoyuan was a native of Qi in Bing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 年十五，父死，居喪以孝行稱，縣令郭湛改其所居為復禮鄉至孝裏。

translations.literal: At fifteen his father died; in mourning he was famed for filial conduct, and the magistrate Guo Zhan changed the place where he lived to Fuli Village in the Lane of Utmost Filiality.
translations.idiomatic: When he was fifteen his father died; his mourning conduct won wide praise for filial piety, and Magistrate Guo Zhan renamed his neighborhood Fuli Village, Lane of Utmost Filiality.

sentences.zh: 道源嘗與友人客遊，友人病，中宵而卒，道源恐驚擾主人，遂共屍臥，達曙方哭，親步營送，至其本鄉里。

translations.literal: Daoyuan once traveled as a guest with a friend; the friend fell ill and died in the middle of the night. Daoyuan, fearing to startle and disturb the host, lay beside the corpse until dawn before weeping; he personally walked to make arrangements for the funeral and saw it delivered to the friend's native village.
translations.idiomatic: Once, while traveling with a friend, the friend fell ill and died at midnight. Not wanting to alarm their host, Daoyuan lay beside the body until dawn before he wept; then he personally saw to the funeral and walked the remains home to the friend's native place.

sentences.zh: 高祖舉義，召授大將軍府戶曹參軍。

translations.literal: When Gaozu raised the righteous banner he was summoned and appointed Army Registrar of Household Affairs in the Grand General's Office.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu raised his banner of revolt, Daoyuan was summoned and appointed registrar of household affairs in the Grand General's Office.

sentences.zh: 及平京城，遣道源撫慰山東，燕、趙之地爭來款附。

translations.literal: When the capital was pacified he dispatched Daoyuan to soothe and reassure Shandong; the lands of Yan and Zhao vied to come over in submission.
translations.idiomatic: After the capital was taken, Gaozu sent Daoyuan to pacify Shandong, and the regions of Yan and Zhao rushed to submit.

sentences.zh: 高祖下書褒美，累封范陽郡公，後拜大理卿。

translations.literal: Gaozu issued a letter of praise; Daoyuan was repeatedly enfeoffed as Duke of Fanyang Commandery and later appointed Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu issued a commendation, repeatedly raised him to Duke of Fanyang Commandery, and later made him Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 時何稠、士澄有罪，家口籍沒，仍以賜之。

translations.literal: At that time He Chou and Shi Cheng were guilty of crimes; their households were confiscated and registered, and were then given to him as gifts.
translations.idiomatic: At the time He Chou and Shi Cheng were condemned; their families were confiscated and then bestowed on Daoyuan.

sentences.zh: 道源嘆曰：「人有否泰，蓋亦是常。

translations.literal: Daoyuan sighed and said, "Men have adversity and prosperity—this too is constant.
translations.idiomatic: Daoyuan sighed and said, "Fortune and misfortune come to every man—that is only natural.

sentences.zh: 安可因己之泰，利人之否，取其子女以為僕妾，豈近仁者之心乎！」

translations.literal: How can one, in one's own time of prosperity, profit from another's adversity and take his sons and daughters as servants and concubines—does this approach the heart of the humane man!
translations.idiomatic: How can I, in my own good fortune, profit from another's ruin and take his sons and daughters as servants and concubines—is that the way of a humane man!

sentences.zh: 皆舍之，一無所取。

translations.literal: He released them all and took nothing.
translations.idiomatic: He set them all free and accepted nothing.

sentences.zh: 尋轉太僕卿，後歷相州都督。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to Minister of the Stud and later served in succession as Governor of Xiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Minister of the Stud and later served as Governor of Xiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 武德七年卒官，贈工部尚書，謚曰節。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Wude he died in office; he was posthumously made Minister of Works and given the posthumous title Upright.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office in the seventh year of Wude, was posthumously made Minister of Works, and given the posthumous title Upright.

sentences.zh: 道源雖歷職九卿，身死日，唯有粟石兩，高祖深異之，賜其家帛三百段。

translations.literal: Though Daoyuan had held office among the Nine Ministers, on the day of his death he possessed only two piculs of grain; Gaozu was deeply struck by this and bestowed three hundred bolts of silk on his family.
translations.idiomatic: Though Daoyuan had risen to one of the Nine Ministers, he left behind only two piculs of grain when he died; Gaozu was deeply moved and gave his family three hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 族子 楚金楚金，少有志行，事親以孝聞。

translations.literal: A clansman, Chu Jin—Chu Jin in youth had ambition and conduct; in serving his parents he was known for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: His clansman Chu Jin was ambitious and principled from youth and was known for filial devotion to his parents.

sentences.zh: 初，與兄越石同預鄉貢進士，州司將罷越石而薦楚金，辭曰：「以順則越石長，以才則楚金不如。」

translations.literal: At first he and his elder brother Yueshi together entered the provincial examination for Presented Scholars; the prefectural office was about to drop Yueshi and recommend Chu Jin, but he declined, saying, "By seniority Yueshi is the elder; by talent Chu Jin is not his equal.
translations.idiomatic: Early on he and his elder brother Yueshi both sat for the provincial Presented Scholar examination; when the prefecture was about to drop Yueshi and recommend Chu Jin instead, he refused, saying, "By age Yueshi is my elder; by ability I am his inferior.

sentences.zh: 固請俱退。

translations.literal: He firmly requested that both withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: He insisted that both of them withdraw.

sentences.zh: 時李勣為都督，嘆曰：「貢士本求才行，相推如此，何嫌雙居也。」

translations.literal: At that time Li Ji was governor; he sighed and said, "Presented Scholars are sought for ability and conduct—when they defer to one another like this, what objection is there to both succeeding?
translations.idiomatic: Li Ji was then governor; he marveled and said, "The examination seeks men of talent and character—when brothers yield to each other like this, why not let both pass?

sentences.zh: 乃俱薦擢第。

translations.literal: Thereupon both were recommended and passed the examination.
translations.idiomatic: He then recommended them both, and both passed.

sentences.zh: 楚金，高宗時累遷刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: Chu Jin, during the reign of Emperor Gaozong, was repeatedly promoted to Vice Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Gaozong, Chu Jin rose through repeated promotions to Vice Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 儀鳳年，有妖星見，楚金上疏，極言得失。

translations.literal: In the Yifeng era an inauspicious star appeared; Chu Jin submitted a memorial thoroughly setting forth what was gained and lost.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yifeng era an ominous star appeared; Chu Jin memorialized the throne with a frank assessment of what the court was doing right and wrong.

sentences.zh: 高宗優納，賜帛二百段。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong graciously accepted it and bestowed two hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong received it favorably and rewarded him with two hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 則天臨朝，歷位吏部侍郎、秋官尚書，賜爵南陽侯。

translations.literal: When Wu Zetian held court, he rose through the posts of Vice Minister of Personnel and Minister of Punishments, and was granted the title Marquis of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Zetian took power, he served as Vice Minister of Personnel and Minister of Punishments and was ennobled as Marquis of Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 為酷吏周興所陷，配流嶺表，竟卒於徙所。

translations.literal: He was entrapped by the cruel official Zhou Xing, exiled to the region south of the Five Ridges, and finally died at the place of banishment.
translations.idiomatic: He was framed by the cruel official Zhou Xing, banished to the far south beyond the Five Ridges, and died in exile.

sentences.zh: 著《翰苑》三十卷、《紳誡》三卷，並傳於時。

translations.literal: He authored thirty fascicles of Hanlin and three fascicles of Admonitions for Officials, both of which circulated in his time.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote thirty fascicles of Hanlin and three fascicles of Admonitions for Officials, both widely read in his day.

sentences.zh: 李公逸李公逸，汴梁雍丘人也。

translations.literal: Li Gongyi—Li Gongyi was a man of Yongqiu in Bianliang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gongyi was a native of Yongqiu in Bianliang.

sentences.zh: 隋末，與族弟善行以義勇為人所附。

translations.literal: At the end of the Sui, he and his clansman Shanxing, men of righteous courage, were followed by the people.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Sui he and his clansman Shanxing, both men of righteous courage, gathered a following.

sentences.zh: 初歸王世充，知其必敗，遣間使請降。

translations.literal: At first he submitted to Wang Shichong; knowing Shichong would surely fall, he sent secret envoys to request surrender.
translations.idiomatic: He first served Wang Shichong, but seeing that Shichong was doomed, he sent secret envoys to offer his surrender to Tang.

sentences.zh: 高祖因以雍丘置杞州，拜為總管，封陽夏郡公。

translations.literal: Gaozu thereupon established Qi Prefecture at Yongqiu, appointed him general commander, and enfeoffed him as Duke of Yangxia Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu established Qi Prefecture at Yongqiu, made him general commander, and enfeoffed him as Duke of Yangxia Commandery.

sentences.zh: 又以善行為杞州刺史。

translations.literal: He also made Shanxing Prefect of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: He also appointed Shanxing Prefect of Qi.

sentences.zh: 世充遣其從弟辨率眾攻之，公逸遣使請援。

translations.literal: Shichong sent his younger cousin Bian at the head of troops to attack him; Gongyi sent envoys to request aid.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong sent his cousin Bian with an army against him, and Gongyi dispatched envoys to plead for relief.

sentences.zh: 高祖以其懸隔賊境，未即出兵。

translations.literal: Gaozu, because he was separated and cut off amid the bandit territory, did not immediately send out troops.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu, seeing that the city lay deep in enemy-held territory, did not send troops at once.

sentences.zh: 公逸乃留善行居守，自入朝請援，行至襄城，為世充伊州刺史張殷所獲，送於洛陽。

translations.literal: Gongyi thereupon left Shanxing to hold the defense and himself entered court to request aid; when he reached Xiangcheng he was seized by Shichong's Prefect of Yi, Zhang Yin, and sent to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Gongyi left Shanxing to hold the city and went himself to court to ask for aid; at Xiangcheng he was captured by Shichong's Prefect of Yi, Zhang Yin, and sent to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 世充謂曰：「卿越鄭臣唐，其說安在？」

translations.literal: Shichong said to him, "You crossed from a minister of Zheng to a subject of Tang—what is your explanation?
translations.idiomatic: Shichong asked him, "You abandoned Zheng to serve Tang—what excuse do you have?

sentences.zh: 公逸答曰：「我於天下，唯聞有唐。」

translations.literal: Gongyi answered, "In all the realm I have heard only of Tang."
translations.idiomatic: Gongyi replied, "In all the world I know only Tang."

sentences.zh: 世充怒，斬之。

translations.literal: Shichong grew angry and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Shichong had him executed.

sentences.zh: 善行竟沒於賊。

translations.literal: Shanxing in the end perished among the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Shanxing ultimately fell to the enemy.

sentences.zh: 高祖聞而悼惜，封其子為襄邑縣公。

translations.literal: When Gaozu heard of it he mourned and grieved; he enfeoffed Gongyi's son as Duke of Xiangyi County.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu mourned the loss and enfeoffed Gongyi's son as Duke of Xiangyi County.

sentences.zh: 張善相張善相，許州襄城人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Shanxiang—Zhang Shanxiang was a man of Xiangcheng in Xu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shanxiang was a native of Xiangcheng in Xu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 大業末，為里長，每督縣兵，逐小盜，為眾所附，遂據本郡，歸於李密。

translations.literal: At the end of Daye he was headman of his village; he regularly led county troops in pursuit of small bandits, was followed by the masses, and thereupon held his own commandery and submitted to Li Mi.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Daye era he served as village headman, leading county troops against petty bandits; the people rallied to him, and he seized his home commandery and submitted to Li Mi.

sentences.zh: 密敗，以城歸國，高祖授伊州總管。

translations.literal: When Mi was defeated he came over with the city to the realm; Gaozu appointed him general commander of Yi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Mi fell, he surrendered his city to Tang, and Gaozu made him general commander of Yi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 王世充數攻之，善相頻遣使請救。

translations.literal: Wang Shichong repeatedly attacked him; Shanxiang repeatedly sent envoys to request rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shichong attacked again and again, and Shanxiang sent envoy after envoy begging for relief.

sentences.zh: 兵既不赴，城中糧盡，自知必敗，謂僚屬曰：「死當斬吾頭以歸世充。」

translations.literal: When troops did not arrive and grain in the city was exhausted, knowing he must fall, he told his staff, "In death you must cut off my head and take it to Shichong.
translations.idiomatic: When no relief came and the city's grain ran out, seeing defeat was inevitable, he told his officers, "When I die, cut off my head and surrender it to Shichong.

sentences.zh: 眾皆泣曰：「寧與公同死，終不獨生！」

translations.literal: All wept and said, "Better to die with you than live alone!"
translations.idiomatic: They all wept and said, "We would rather die with you than live on alone!"

sentences.zh: 後城陷被擒，送於世充，辭色不撓，罵世充極口，尋被害。

translations.literal: Later the city fell and he was captured; sent to Shichong, his words and bearing were unbowed and he cursed Shichong to his face; soon he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: When the city finally fell he was taken and sent to Shichong; he showed no fear, cursed Shichong to his face, and was soon put to death.

sentences.zh: 高祖嘆曰：「吾負善相，善相不負吾。」

translations.literal: Gaozu sighed and said, "I failed Shanxiang; Shanxiang did not fail me.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu sighed and said, "I let Shanxiang down; Shanxiang never let me down.

sentences.zh: 封其子為襄城郡公。

translations.literal: He enfeoffed Shanxiang's son as Duke of Xiangcheng Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He conferred on Shanxiang's son the title Duke of Xiangcheng Commandery.

sentences.zh: 李玄通李玄通，雍州藍田人。

translations.literal: Li Xuantong—Li Xuantong was a man of Lantian in Yong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xuantong was a native of Lantian in Yong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 仕隋鷹揚郎將。

translations.literal: He served the Sui as an Eagle-and-Messenger Captain.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Sui he served as an Eagle-and-Messenger Captain.

sentences.zh: 義兵入關，率所部歸國，累除定州總管。

translations.literal: When the righteous army entered the passes, he led his troops to submit to the realm and was repeatedly promoted, eventually being appointed general commander of Ding Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebel army entered the passes, he brought his troops over to Tang and rose through successive appointments until he became general commander of Ding Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 劉黑闥反叛，攻之，城陷被擒。

translations.literal: Liu Hei'a rebelled, attacked him, the city fell, and he was captured.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Hei'a rebelled and attacked him, the city fell and he was taken prisoner.

sentences.zh: 黑闥重其才，欲以為大將，玄通嘆息曰：「吾荷朝恩，作籓東夏，孤城無援，遂陷虜庭。

translations.literal: Hei'a valued his talent and wished to make him a great general. Xuantong sighed and said, "I have received the court's grace, served as frontier lord over Eastern Xia; an isolated city without relief—thus I fell into the enemy's camp.
translations.idiomatic: Hei'a admired his ability and wanted to appoint him a great general. Xuantong sighed and said, "I owe the dynasty a debt of favor—I was made its frontier lord in the east, yet my lone city had no help and I fell into the enemy's hands.

sentences.zh: 當守臣節，以忠報國，豈能降誌，輒受賊官。」

translations.literal: One ought to keep a minister's integrity and repay the state with loyalty—how could I lower my resolve and casually accept an office from bandits?
translations.idiomatic: A minister should hold to his duty and repay the realm with loyalty. How could I lower my spirit and take rank from rebels?

sentences.zh: 拒而不受。

translations.literal: He refused and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He refused the offer.

sentences.zh: 故吏有以酒食饋之者，玄通曰：「諸君哀吾困辱，故以酒食來相寬慰，吾當為諸君一醉。」

translations.literal: Former subordinates brought him food and wine. Xuantong said, "You pity my distress and humiliation, so you bring food and wine to comfort me—I shall drink once for you all.
translations.idiomatic: Some of his former officers brought him food and wine. Xuantong said, "You pity my plight and have come to comfort me with a meal—I owe you at least one good drunk.

sentences.zh: 遂與樂飲。

translations.literal: Then he drank merrily with them.
translations.idiomatic: He then drank happily with them.

sentences.zh: 謂守者曰：「吾能舞劍，可借吾刀。」

translations.literal: He said to the guards, "I can perform a sword dance—lend me a blade.
translations.idiomatic: He told his guards, "I know how to dance with a sword—lend me one.

sentences.zh: 守者與之。

translations.literal: The guards gave him one.
translations.idiomatic: The guards handed him a sword.

sentences.zh: 及曲終，太息而言：「大丈夫受國厚恩，鎮撫方面，不能保全所守，亦何面目視息世間哉！」

translations.literal: When the melody ended, he sighed deeply and said, "A great man who has received the state's deep grace, governing a frontier region, yet could not preserve what he was charged to hold—what face has he to draw breath in this world!
translations.idiomatic: When the dance was finished, he sighed and said, "A man who has received the state's great favor and been entrusted with a frontier command, yet could not hold what he was charged to defend—what face has he left to go on living in this world!

sentences.zh: 因潰腹而死。

translations.literal: Thereupon he disemboweled himself and died.
translations.idiomatic: Then he cut open his belly and died.

sentences.zh: 高祖聞而為之流涕，拜其子伏護為大將。

translations.literal: When Gaozu heard of it, he wept for him and appointed his son Fuhu as General-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu heard, he wept and appointed Xuantong's son Fuhu a general-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 敬君弘敬君弘，絳州太平人，齊右僕射顯雋曾孫也。

translations.literal: Jing Junhong—Jing Junhong was a man of Taiping in Jiang Prefecture, a great-grandson of Qi Right Vice Director Xianjun.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Junhong was a native of Taiping in Jiang Prefecture and a great-grandson of Xianjun, Right Vice Director of Qi.

sentences.zh: 武德中，為驃騎將軍，封黔昌縣侯，掌屯營兵於玄武門，加授雲麾將軍。

translations.literal: During Wude he served as General of Agile Cavalry, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Qianchang County, commanded garrison troops at Xuanwu Gate, and was additionally appointed General of Cloud-Banners.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wude era he was made General of Agile Cavalry, enfeoffed as Marquis of Qianchang County, put in charge of the garrison at Xuanwu Gate, and further given the rank of General of Cloud-Banners.

sentences.zh: 隱太子建成之誅也，其餘黨馮立、謝叔方率兵犯玄武門，君弘挺身出戰。

translations.literal: When the Hidden Crown Prince Jiancheng was executed, the remnant followers Feng Li and Xie Shufang led troops to attack Xuanwu Gate; Junhong threw himself forward to fight.
translations.idiomatic: When the Hidden Crown Prince Jiancheng was killed, his remaining partisans Feng Li and Xie Shufang led troops against Xuanwu Gate, and Junhong stepped forward to meet them.

sentences.zh: 其所親止之曰：「事未可知，當且觀變，待兵集，成列而戰，未晚也。」

translations.literal: Those close to him stopped him and said, "The outcome is not yet known—you should watch how things develop first; wait until troops are assembled and fight in formation—it will not be too late.
translations.idiomatic: Those close to him held him back and said, "The outcome is still uncertain. Watch how things unfold, wait until the troops are gathered, and fight in formation—it will not be too late.

sentences.zh: 君弘不從，乃與中郎將呂世衡大呼而進，並遇害。

translations.literal: Junhong would not listen; he and Middle General Lü Shiheng shouted and charged forward, and both were killed.
translations.idiomatic: Junhong refused. He and Middle General Lü Shiheng charged forward with a shout, and both were killed.

sentences.zh: 太宗甚嗟賞之，贈君弘左屯衛大將軍，世衡右驍衛將軍。

translations.literal: Taizong deeply admired them; Junhong was posthumously made General-in-Chief of the Left Garrison Guard, and Shiheng General of the Right Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong greatly admired them. Junhong was posthumously made General-in-Chief of the Left Garrison Guard, and Shiheng General of the Right Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 馮立馮立，同州馮翊人也。

translations.literal: Feng Li—Feng Li was a man of Fuyi in Tong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Li was a native of Fuyi in Tong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 有武藝，略涉書記，隱太子建成引為翊衛車騎將軍，托以心膂。

translations.literal: Skilled in martial arts and with some knowledge of clerical matters, the Hidden Crown Prince Jiancheng recruited him as General of the Winged Guard Chariots and Cavalry and trusted him as a close confidant.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled in arms and had some learning in record-keeping. The Hidden Crown Prince Jiancheng brought him in as General of the Winged Guard Chariots and Cavalry and treated him as a trusted inner companion.

sentences.zh: 建成被誅，其左右多逃散，立嘆曰：「豈有生受其恩而死逃其難！」

translations.literal: When Jiancheng was executed, most of his close followers fled and scattered. Li sighed and said, "How can one live receiving his grace yet flee when he faces disaster!
translations.idiomatic: When Jiancheng was killed, most of his close attendants fled. Li sighed and said, "How can a man accept his lord's favor in life and run from his lord's death!

sentences.zh: 於是率兵犯玄武門，苦戰久之，殺屯營將軍敬君弘。

translations.literal: Thereupon he led troops to attack Xuanwu Gate, fought bitterly for a long time, and killed Garrison General Jing Junhong.
translations.idiomatic: He then led troops against Xuanwu Gate, fought a long and bitter battle, and killed the garrison general Jing Junhong.

sentences.zh: 謂其徒曰：「微以報太子矣！」

translations.literal: He said to his followers, "I have in a small measure repaid the Crown Prince!
translations.idiomatic: He told his men, "I have done what little I could to repay the Crown Prince!

sentences.zh: 遂解兵遁於野。

translations.literal: Then he dispersed his forces and fled into the wilds.
translations.idiomatic: He then dismissed his troops and fled into the countryside.

sentences.zh: 俄而來請罪。

translations.literal: Before long he came to surrender and confess guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he came to surrender and ask for punishment.

sentences.zh: 太宗數之曰：「汝在東宮，潛為間構，阻我骨肉，汝罪一也。

translations.literal: Taizong rebuked him, saying, "In the Eastern Palace you secretly fomented division and blocked me from my kin—your first crime.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong rebuked him, saying, "In the Eastern Palace you secretly sowed discord and came between me and my kin—that is your first crime.

sentences.zh: 昨日復出兵來戰，殺傷我將士，汝罪二也。

translations.literal: Yesterday you again led troops to battle and killed and wounded my officers and soldiers—your second crime.
translations.idiomatic: Yesterday you took the field again, killing and wounding my officers and men—that is your second crime.

sentences.zh: 何以逃死！」

translations.literal: How can you escape death!
translations.idiomatic: How do you expect to escape death!

sentences.zh: 對曰：「出身事主，期之效命，當職之日，無所顧憚。」

translations.literal: He replied, "Having emerged to serve a lord, one expects to give one's life in duty; on the day one holds office, one has nothing to fear.
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Once one enters a lord's service, one expects to give one's life. On the day duty falls to you, there is nothing to hold back.

sentences.zh: 因伏地歔欷，悲不自勝。

translations.literal: Then he prostrated himself, sobbing; grief overwhelmed him.
translations.idiomatic: He prostrated himself and wept until grief overwhelmed him.

sentences.zh: 太宗慰勉之。

translations.literal: Taizong comforted and encouraged him.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong comforted him and urged him on.

sentences.zh: 立歸，謂所親曰：「逢莫大之恩，幸而獲濟，終當以死奉答。」

translations.literal: Li returned and told those close to him, "Having met with boundless grace and by luck been spared, in the end I shall repay it with my life."
translations.idiomatic: When Li went home, he told those close to him, "I have received an immense favor and by luck been spared. In the end I shall repay it with my life."

sentences.zh: 未幾，突厥至便橋。

translations.literal: Not long after, the Turks arrived at Bian Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Turks reached Bian Bridge.

sentences.zh: 立率數百騎與虜戰於咸陽，殺獲甚眾。

translations.literal: Li led several hundred horsemen to fight the barbarians at Xianyang, killing and capturing many.
translations.idiomatic: Li led several hundred horsemen against the invaders at Xianyang and killed or captured a great many of them.

sentences.zh: 太宗聞而嘉嘆，拜廣州都督。

translations.literal: When Taizong heard, he praised and sighed; Li was appointed Governor of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong heard, he praised him warmly and appointed him Governor of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 前後作牧者，多以黷貨為蠻夷所患，由是數怨叛。

translations.literal: Previous governors mostly plagued the barbarians with corrupt exactions, and for this reason they rebelled repeatedly in resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier governors had mostly preyed on the tribes with corrupt exactions, and for that reason the region had rebelled again and again.

sentences.zh: 立到，不營產業，衣食取給而已。

translations.literal: When Li arrived, he did not build up estates; clothing and food were taken only as needed.
translations.idiomatic: When Li took up the post, he built no private fortune and took only enough for food and clothing.

sentences.zh: 嘗至貪泉，嘆曰：「此吳隱之所酌泉也。

translations.literal: Once when he reached the Greedy Spring, he sighed and said, "This is the spring from which Wu Yinzhi drank.
translations.idiomatic: Once, passing the Greedy Spring, he sighed and said, "This is the spring Wu Yinzhi drank from.

sentences.zh: 飲一杯水，何足道哉！

translations.literal: To drink a cup of water—what is there in it!
translations.idiomatic: What is one cup of water, after all!

sentences.zh: 吾當汲而為食，豈止一杯耶，安能易吾性乎！」

translations.literal: I shall draw it and use it for food—not merely a cup! How could it change my nature!
translations.idiomatic: I mean to draw from it for my daily fare—not just one cup! How could it change who I am!

sentences.zh: 遂畢飲而去。

translations.literal: Then he finished drinking and departed.
translations.idiomatic: He drank his fill and went on.

sentences.zh: 在職數年，甚有惠政，卒於官。

translations.literal: In office for several years, he had excellent benevolent administration and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He served several years with excellent benevolent rule and died in office.

sentences.zh: 謝叔方謝叔方，雍州萬年人也。

translations.literal: Xie Shufang—Xie Shufang was a man of Wannian in Yong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Shufang was a native of Wannian in Yong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 初從巢剌王元吉征討，數有戰功，元吉奏授屈咥直府左軍騎。

translations.literal: At first he followed Prince Yuanji of Chao in campaigns and had repeated military merit; Yuanji memorialized to appoint him Left Cavalry Officer of the Qudie Direct Office.
translations.idiomatic: At first he followed Prince Yuanji of Chao on campaign and won repeated distinction in battle; Yuanji memorialized to appoint him Left Cavalry Officer of the Qudie Direct Office.

sentences.zh: 太宗誅隱太子及元吉於玄武門，叔方率府兵與馮立合軍，拒戰於北闕下，殺敬君弘、呂世衡。

translations.literal: When Taizong executed the Hidden Crown Prince and Yuanji at Xuanwu Gate, Shufang led office troops and joined Feng Li's army, resisting battle beneath the North Gate, and killed Jing Junhong and Lü Shiheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong killed the Hidden Crown Prince and Yuanji at Xuanwu Gate, Shufang led his office troops to join Feng Li's force, fought beneath the North Gate, and killed Jing Junhong and Lü Shiheng.

sentences.zh: 太宗兵不振，秦府護軍尉遲敬德傳元吉首以示之，叔方下馬號哭而遁。

translations.literal: Taizong's troops faltered; Qin Prince's Protector-General Yuchi Jingde displayed Yuanji's head to show them; Shufang dismounted, wept loudly, and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong's force faltered until Yuchi Jingde, Protector-General of the Prince of Qin's household, held up Yuanji's head for all to see. Shufang dismounted, wailed, and fled.

sentences.zh: 明日出首，太宗曰：「義士也！」

translations.literal: The next day he turned himself in; Taizong said, "A man of righteousness!
translations.idiomatic: The next day he surrendered himself. Taizong said, "A man of honor!

sentences.zh: 命釋之。

translations.literal: He ordered him released.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered him set free.

sentences.zh: 歷遷西、伊二州刺史，善綏邊鎮，胡戎愛而敬之，如事嚴父。

translations.literal: In successive appointments as Governor of Xi and Yi Prefectures, he was skilled at pacifying frontier garrisons; the Hu and Rong tribes loved and revered him as they would a stern father.
translations.idiomatic: Serving in turn as Governor of Xi and Yi Prefectures, he was skilled at pacifying the frontier garrisons; the Hu and Rong tribes loved and revered him as they would a strict father.

sentences.zh: 貞觀末，累加銀青光祿大夫，歷洪、廣二州都督。

translations.literal: At the end of the Zhenguan era, he was repeatedly promoted to Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with Silver Seal and made Governor of Hong and Guang Prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Zhenguan he rose to Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with Silver Seal and served as Governor of Hong and Guang Prefectures.

sentences.zh: 永徽中卒。

translations.literal: He died in the Yonghui era.
translations.idiomatic: He died during the Yonghui era.

sentences.zh: 王義方王義方，泗州漣水人也。

translations.literal: Wang Yifang—Wang Yifang was a man of Lianshui in Si Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yifang was a native of Lianshui in Si Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 少孤貧，事母甚謹，博通《五經》，而謇傲獨行。

translations.literal: Orphaned and poor in youth, he served his mother with great care, was broadly versed in the Five Classics, and was upright, proud, and independent in conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned and poor as a youth, he cared for his mother with great devotion, mastered the Five Classics, and was upright, proud, and fiercely independent.

sentences.zh: 初舉明經，因詣京師，中路逢徒步者，自雲父為潁上令，聞病篤，倍道將往焉，徒步不前，計無所出。

translations.literal: When he first passed the Classics examination and was on his way to the capital, midway he met a man on foot who said his father was magistrate of Yingshang, that he had heard his illness was critical, and was hurrying day and night to reach him—but on foot he could not advance and had no plan.
translations.idiomatic: When he first passed the Classics examination and set out for the capital, he met a man on foot who said his father was magistrate of Yingshang and was gravely ill; the man was hurrying to reach him but could not go fast enough on foot and had no way forward.

sentences.zh: 義方解所乘馬與之，不告姓名而去。

translations.literal: Yifang gave him the horse he was riding without giving his name and left.
translations.idiomatic: Yifang gave him his own horse without leaving his name and went on.

sentences.zh: 俄授晉王府參軍，直弘文館。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Adjunct of the Prince of Jin's mansion, serving directly in the Hongwen Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed adjutant in the Prince of Jin's household and served on duty at the Hongwen Academy.

sentences.zh: 特進魏徵甚禮之，將以侄女妻之。

translations.literal: Special Advance Wei Zheng treated him with great courtesy and was about to marry his niece to him.
translations.idiomatic: Special Advance Wei Zheng treated him with great respect and planned to give him his niece in marriage.

sentences.zh: 義方竟娶徵之侄女，告人曰：「昔不附宰相之勢，今感知己之言故也。」

translations.literal: Yifang ultimately married Wei Zheng's niece and told people, "Formerly I would not attach myself to a chancellor's power; now I do so because I feel the obligation of a friend's word.
translations.idiomatic: Yifang did marry Wei Zheng's niece and told others, "I once refused to lean on a chancellor's power; now I accept because I honor a friend's word.

sentences.zh: 轉太子校書。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Collator of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made collator to the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 無何，坐與刑部尚書張亮交通，貶為儋州吉安丞。

translations.literal: Before long, for associating with Minister of Punishments Zhang Liang, he was demoted to Assistant Magistrate of Ji'an in Dan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was punished for dealings with Minister of Punishments Zhang Liang and demoted to assistant magistrate of Ji'an in Dan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 行至海南，舟人將以酒脯致祭。

translations.literal: When he reached Hainan, the boatmen were about to offer wine and meats in sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Hainan, the boatmen prepared to offer wine and meat to the spirits of the sea.

sentences.zh: 義方曰：「黍稷非馨，義在明德。」

translations.literal: Yifang said, "Grain offerings are not fragrant; righteousness lies in bright virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Yifang said, "Grain offerings are not what make a sacrifice fragrant; what matters is bright virtue.

sentences.zh: 乃酌水而祭，為文曰：「思帝鄉而北顧，望海浦而南浮。

translations.literal: Then he poured water and offered sacrifice, writing a text that said, "Thinking of the imperial capital I look north; gazing at the sea's shore I float south.
translations.idiomatic: He poured water instead and made an offering, writing a text that said, "I think of the capital and look north; I gaze at the sea's edge and drift south.

sentences.zh: 必也行愆諸己，義負前修。

translations.literal: Surely my conduct's faults lie with myself; in righteousness I fail the sages of old.
translations.idiomatic: Surely the fault lies in my own conduct; in duty I have failed the worthies of old.

sentences.zh: 長鯨擊水，天吳覆舟。

translations.literal: The great whale strikes the water; Tianwu capsizes the boat.
translations.idiomatic: Great whales strike the water; Tianwu overturns the boat.

sentences.zh: 因忠獲戾，以孝見尤。

translations.literal: For loyalty I receive blame; for filial piety I meet reproach.
translations.idiomatic: For loyalty I am punished; for filial piety I am blamed.

sentences.zh: 四維霧廓，千里安流。

translations.literal: The four cardinal principles clear like mist; a thousand leagues flow in peace.
translations.idiomatic: May the four pillars of the realm clear like lifting mist, and a thousand leagues run calm.

sentences.zh: 靈應如響，無作神羞。」

translations.literal: Let spiritual response be like an echo; do not make the gods ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Let the spirits answer as if to a summons, and do not let the gods be shamed.

sentences.zh: 時當盛夏，風濤蒸毒，既而開霽，南渡吉安。

translations.literal: It was then midsummer; wind and waves were steaming and poisonous; soon thereafter the sky cleared, and they crossed south to Ji'an.
translations.idiomatic: It was midsummer, and the wind and waves were fierce and stifling; then the sky cleared, and they crossed south to Ji'an.

sentences.zh: 蠻俗荒梗，義方召諸首領，集生徒，親為講經，行釋奠之禮；

translations.literal: The barbarian customs were wild and stubborn; Yifang summoned the chieftains, gathered students, personally lectured on the classics, and performed the Confucian sacrifice ceremony;
