translations.idiomatic: The tribal customs were crude and stubborn, so Yifang summoned the chieftains, gathered students, lectured on the classics himself, and performed the Confucian sacrifice;

sentences.zh: 清歌吹籥，登降有序，蠻酋大喜。

translations.literal: With clear songs, pipes, and bells, ascending and descending in order, the barbarian chiefs were greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: With clear song, pipes, and bells, and every step of the rite in proper order, the tribal chiefs were delighted.

sentences.zh: ，改授洹水丞。

translations.literal: He was reassigned as Assistant Magistrate of Huanshui.
translations.idiomatic: He was then reassigned as assistant magistrate of Huanshui.

sentences.zh: 時張亮兄子皎，配流在崖州，來依義方而卒。

translations.literal: At that time Zhang Liang's elder brother's son Jiao, sentenced to exile, was in Yazhou; he came to rely on Yifang and died there.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Zhang Liang's nephew Jiao, exiled to Yazhou, came to stay with Yifang and died there.

sentences.zh: 臨終托以妻子及致屍還鄉。

translations.literal: On his deathbed he entrusted his wife and children and the return of his corpse to his native place.
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed he entrusted Yifang with his wife and children and with bringing his body home.

sentences.zh: 義方與皎妻自誓於海神，使奴負柩，令皎妻抱其赤子，乘義方之馬，身獨步從而還。

translations.literal: Yifang and Jiao's wife swore an oath before the Sea God; he had a servant carry the coffin, had Jiao's wife hold their infant, mounted Yifang's horse for them, and himself walked alone following behind to return.
translations.idiomatic: Yifang and Jiao's wife swore an oath before the Sea God. He had a servant carry the coffin, put Jiao's wife and infant on his own horse, and walked the whole way home himself.

sentences.zh: 先之原武葬皎，告祭張亮，送皎妻子歸其家而往洹水。

translations.literal: He first went to Yuanwu to bury Jiao, performed rites to announce it to Zhang Liang, sent Jiao's wife and children home to their family, and then proceeded to Huanshui.
translations.idiomatic: He went first to Yuanwu to bury Jiao, performed rites to notify Zhang Liang, saw Jiao's wife and children safely home, and then went on to Huanshui.

sentences.zh: 轉雲陽丞，擢為著作佐郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Assistant Magistrate of Yunyang and was promoted to Assistant in the Office of Literary Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to assistant magistrate of Yunyang and then promoted to assistant in the Office of Literary Works.

sentences.zh: ，遷侍御史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made an attending censor.

sentences.zh: 時中書侍郎李義府執權用事，婦人淳於氏有美色，坐事系大理，義府悅之，托大理丞畢正義枉法出之。

translations.literal: At that time Vice Director of the Secretariat Li Yifu held power and handled affairs; the woman Lady Chunyu was beautiful and was imprisoned at the Court of Judicial Review for an offense; Yifu was pleased with her and had Vice Director of Judicial Review Bi Zhengyi pervert the law to release her.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Vice Director of the Secretariat Li Yifu held power. Lady Chunyu, a woman of great beauty, had been imprisoned at the Court of Judicial Review for an offense. Yifu desired her and had Vice Director Bi Zhengyi bend the law to set her free.

sentences.zh: 高宗又敕給事中劉仁軌、侍御史張倫重按其事。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong also ordered Remonstrating Attendant Liu Rengui and Attending Censor Zhang Lun to reinvestigate the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong also ordered Remonstrating Attendant Liu Rengui and Attending Censor Zhang Lun to reinvestigate the case.

sentences.zh: 正義自縊。

translations.literal: Zhengyi hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: Bi Zhengyi took his own life.

sentences.zh: 高宗特原義府之罪。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong specially pardoned Yifu's crime.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong specially pardoned Yifu.

sentences.zh: 義方以義府奸蠹害政，將加彈奏，以問其母。

translations.literal: Yifang, because Yifu was treacherous and corrupt and harmed government, was about to submit an impeachment and consulted his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Believing Yifu treacherous and corrupt and a harm to government, Yifang prepared to impeach him and asked his mother's counsel.

sentences.zh: 母曰：「昔王陵母伏劍成子之義，汝能盡忠立名，吾之願也，雖死不恨！」

translations.literal: His mother said, "In old times Wang Ling's mother took sword in hand to complete her son's righteousness; if you can exhaust loyalty and establish your name, that is my wish—even in death I have no regret!
translations.idiomatic: His mother said, "Long ago Wang Ling's mother killed herself with a sword to complete her son's duty. If you can give your full loyalty and make a name for yourself, that is my wish—I would not regret death!

sentences.zh: 義方乃先奏曰：

translations.literal: Yifang then first submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Yifang then submitted a memorial that began:

sentences.zh: 臣聞春鶯鳴於獻歲，蟋蟀吟於始秋，物有微而應時，人有賤而言忠。

translations.literal: I have heard the oriole sings in the year's offering, the cricket chirps at the start of autumn—creatures lowly yet responding to the season; men humble yet speaking in loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that orioles sing at the year's offering and crickets chirp at the start of autumn—lowly creatures answer the season, and humble men may still speak in loyalty.

sentences.zh: 臣去歲冬初，雲陽下縣丞耳。

translations.literal: Last winter at the start I was only Assistant Magistrate of Yunyang County.
translations.idiomatic: Only last winter I was a lowly assistant magistrate in Yunyang County.

sentences.zh: 今春及夏，陛下擢臣著作佐郎，極文學之清選。

translations.literal: This spring and summer Your Majesty promoted me to Assistant in the Office of Literary Works—the utmost refined selection in literary service.
translations.idiomatic: This spring and summer Your Majesty raised me to assistant in the Office of Literary Works—the finest literary appointment in the court.

sentences.zh: 未幾，又拜臣侍御史，濫朝廷之雄職。

translations.literal: Before long, you again appointed me Attending Censor—an exalted office of the court, though I fill it unworthily.
translations.idiomatic: Before long you made me an attending censor—a lofty post at court, though I scarcely deserve it.

sentences.zh: 顧視生涯，隕首非報，唯欲有犯無隱，以廣天聽。

translations.literal: Looking back on my life's path, even losing my head would not repay your grace; I only wish to speak without concealment and broaden Heaven's hearing.
translations.idiomatic: Looking back on what I have become, even my death would not repay your grace; I wish only to speak without concealment and widen what reaches the throne.

sentences.zh: 伏以李義府枉殺寺丞，陛下已赦之，臣不應更有鞫問。

translations.literal: I submit that Li Yifu wrongly killed the Vice Director—in this Your Majesty has already pardoned him, and I ought not to raise further investigation.
translations.idiomatic: I know Li Yifu drove the vice director to his death and that Your Majesty has already pardoned him, so I should not press the matter further.

sentences.zh: 然天子置三公、九卿、二十七大夫、八十一元士，本欲水火相濟，鹽梅相成，然後庶績咸熙，風雨交泰。

translations.literal: Yet the Son of Heaven established the Three Excellencies, Nine Ministers, twenty-seven Great Officers, and eighty-one Founding Officers precisely so that water and fire may complement each other, salt and plums may work together—and only then are all achievements bright and wind and rain harmoniously exchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Son of Heaven created the Three Excellencies, Nine Ministers, twenty-seven Great Officers, and eighty-one Founding Officers so that water and fire might complement each other and salt and plums work in harmony—only then are all tasks accomplished and heaven and earth in concord.

sentences.zh: 亦不可獨是獨非，皆由聖旨。

translations.literal: One also cannot have only right or only wrong, all decided by the sacred will alone.
translations.idiomatic: Right and wrong cannot all be decided by the throne alone.

sentences.zh: 昔唐堯失之於四凶，漢祖失之於陳豨，光武失之於逢萌，魏武失之於張邈。

translations.literal: In the past Emperor Yao lost track of the Four Villains, Emperor Gaozu of Han lost track of Chen Xi, Emperor Guangwu lost track of Feng Meng, and Emperor Wu of Wei lost track of Zhang Miao.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yao once missed the Four Villains; Han Gaozu missed Chen Xi; Emperor Guangwu missed Feng Meng; Cao Cao missed Zhang Miao.

sentences.zh: 此四帝者，英傑之主，然失之於前，得之於後。

translations.literal: These four emperors were heroic and outstanding lords—yet they lost them at first and recovered them afterward.
translations.idiomatic: These four were heroic rulers, yet each lost his man at first and recovered him afterward.

sentences.zh: 今陛下繼聖，撫育萬邦，蠻陬夷落，猶懼疏網。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty succeeds the sages, nurtures all states; even remote barbarian corners still fear the loose net.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty succeeds the sages and nurtures all lands; even distant tribes still fear the loosening of the law.

sentences.zh: 況輦轂咫尺，奸臣肆虐，足使忠臣抗憤，義士扼腕。

translations.literal: How much more when within a bowshot of the imperial carriage a treacherous minister runs rampant—it is enough to make loyal ministers indignant and men of righteousness clutch their wrists.
translations.idiomatic: How much more when, within a bowshot of the throne, a treacherous minister runs wild—enough to fill loyal ministers with outrage and men of honor with clenched fists.

sentences.zh: 縱令正義自縊，彌不可容，便是畏義府之權勢，能殺身以滅口。

translations.literal: Even if Zhengyi hanged himself, this cannot be tolerated—it shows fear of Yifu's power, that he could kill himself to seal his mouth.
translations.idiomatic: Even if Zhengyi hanged himself, this cannot be tolerated—it means men feared Yifu's power so much that he could kill himself to silence the truth.

sentences.zh: 此則生殺之威，上非王出；

translations.literal: This means the power of life and death no longer issues solely from the king;
translations.idiomatic: This means the power of life and death no longer comes from the throne alone;

sentences.zh: 賞罰之柄，下移佞寵。

translations.literal: The handle of reward and punishment has shifted downward to flatterers and favorites.
translations.idiomatic: The power to reward and punish has passed down to flatterers and favorites.

sentences.zh: 臣恐履霜堅冰，積小成大，請重鞫正義死由，雪冤氣於幽泉，誅奸臣於白日。

translations.literal: I fear that treading frost leads to solid ice, that small accumulations grow great; I beg to re-examine the cause of Zhengyi's death, clear wrongful grievance in the dark underworld, and execute the wicked minister in broad daylight.
translations.idiomatic: I fear that frost underfoot becomes solid ice—that small wrongs snowball into great ones. I beg that the cause of Zhengyi's death be reinvestigated, that his grievance be cleared in the grave, and that the treacherous minister be put to death in the light of day.

sentences.zh: 及廷劾義府，曰：

translations.literal: When in court he impeached Yifu, he said:
translations.idiomatic: When he impeached Yifu in open court, he declared:

sentences.zh: 臣聞附下罔上，聖主之所宜誅；

translations.literal: I have heard that fawning on subordinates while deceiving superiors is what a sage ruler should punish;
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that to fawn on those below while deceiving those above is what a sage ruler must punish;

sentences.zh: 心狠貌恭，明時之所必罰。

translations.literal: cruel in heart yet deferential in countenance—in a brilliant age this must be penalized.
translations.idiomatic: ruthless at heart yet humble in bearing—in an enlightened age this must be punished.

sentences.zh: 是以隱賊掩義，不容唐帝之朝；

translations.literal: Therefore hiding villains and covering righteousness cannot be permitted in the court of the Tang emperor;
translations.idiomatic: Thus to harbor villains and cover up righteousness has no place in the court of the Tang emperor;

sentences.zh: 竊幸乘權，終齒漢皇之劍。

translations.literal: those who usurp and seize power by chance shall in the end taste the Han emperor's sword.
translations.idiomatic: those who steal power by fortune shall yet meet the Han emperor's blade.

sentences.zh: 中書侍郎李義府，因緣際會，遂階通顯。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Secretariat Li Yifu, through opportune circumstance, ascended to eminent rank.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yifu, Vice Director of the Secretariat, rose to high office through sheer opportunism.

sentences.zh: 不能盡忠竭節，對揚王休，策蹇勵駑，祗奉皇眷，而反憑附城社，蔽虧日月，請托公行，交遊群小。

translations.literal: He could not exhaust loyalty and devote his integrity, respond to and proclaim the king's blessings, spur a lame horse and encourage a slow nag to reverently serve the imperial favor—yet instead he relied upon the city altars, eclipsed sun and moon, practiced patronage openly, and consorted with petty men.
translations.idiomatic: Instead of giving his full loyalty, answering the throne's grace, and doing his utmost to serve the emperor, he clung to powerful patrons, blocked the light of justice, practiced favoritism openly, and kept company with petty men.

sentences.zh: 貪冶容之美，原有罪之淳於；

translations.literal: Coveting the beauty of a cast woman's allure, he pardoned the guilty Chunyu;
translations.idiomatic: Lustful for a woman's beauty, he freed from guilt the condemned Chunyu;

sentences.zh: 恐漏泄其謀，殞無辜之正義。

translations.literal: fearing his scheme would leak out, he caused the innocent Zhengyi to perish.
translations.idiomatic: and fearing his plot would come to light, he drove the innocent Zhengyi to his death.

sentences.zh: 雖挾山超海之力，望此猶輕；

translations.literal: Even strength that could clasp mountains and cross seas would still be light compared with this;
translations.idiomatic: Even power vast enough to move mountains and cross seas seems small beside this crime;

sentences.zh: 回天轉日之威，方斯更劣。

translations.literal: authority that could turn back heaven and shift the sun would be yet feebler by comparison.
translations.idiomatic: and authority that could reverse heaven and turn back the sun seems weaker still.

sentences.zh: 此而可恕，孰不可容！

translations.literal: If this can be forgiven, what cannot be tolerated!
translations.idiomatic: If this may be forgiven, then nothing is beyond tolerance!

sentences.zh: 金風屆節，玉露啟塗，霜簡與秋典共清，忠臣將鷹鹯並擊。

translations.literal: Golden wind arrives at the season, jade dew opens the path; the frost-scroll shares clarity with autumn's statutes, and loyal ministers will strike together with hawk and falcon.
translations.idiomatic: Now the golden wind of autumn is upon us and the jade dew marks the season's turn; the censor's scroll is as clear as autumn law, and loyal ministers will swoop down like hawks and falcons together.

sentences.zh: 請除君側，少答鴻私，碎首玉階，庶明臣節。

translations.literal: I beg to remove [him from] the ruler's side, briefly answer your vast grace, shatter my head on the jade steps, that I may clarify a minister's integrity.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that he be removed from Your Majesty's side, that I may in some small measure repay your boundless grace—even though my head be broken on the jade steps, so that a minister's duty may be made clear.

sentences.zh: 高宗以義方毀辱大臣，言詞不遜，左遷萊州司戶參軍。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong, because Yifang had insulted a great minister with disrespectful words, demoted him to Registrar of the Revenue Section in Laizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong demoted him to registrar in the revenue section at Laizhou for having publicly shamed a high minister in impertinent language.

sentences.zh: 秩滿，家於昌樂，聚徒教授。

translations.literal: When his term ended, he made his home in Changle and gathered disciples to teach.
translations.idiomatic: When his term expired, he settled in Changle and gathered students to teach.

sentences.zh: 母卒，遂不復仕進。

translations.literal: When his mother died, he never again sought office or advancement.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother's death, he never returned to public life.

sentences.zh: 總章二年卒，年五十五。

translations.literal: He died in the second year of Zongzhang, age fifty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of the Zongzhang era, at fifty-five.

sentences.zh: 撰《筆海》十卷、文集十卷。

translations.literal: He compiled ten juan of Brush Sea and ten juan of collected writings.
translations.idiomatic: He authored ten fascicles of Brush Sea and ten fascicles of collected works.

sentences.zh: 門人何彥光、員半千為義方制師服，三年喪畢而去。

translations.literal: His disciples He Yanguang and Yuan Banqian made mourning garments for Yifang as for a teacher, and when the three-year mourning was completed, they departed.
translations.idiomatic: His disciples He Yanguang and Yuan Banqian wore mourning for him as for a master, and left when the three-year mourning period ended.

sentences.zh: 半千者，齊州全節人也。

translations.literal: Banqian was a man of Quanjie in Qi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Banqian was a native of Quanjie in Qi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 事義方經十餘年，博涉經史，知名河朔。

translations.literal: He served under Yifang for more than ten years, broadly immersed himself in the classics and histories, and became known north of the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: He studied under Yifang for more than ten years, mastered the classics and histories, and won renown north of the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 則天時官至天官侍郎。

translations.literal: In Empress Wu's time he reached the office of Vice Minister of the Celestial Office.
translations.idiomatic: Under Empress Wu he rose to Vice Minister of the Celestial Office.

sentences.zh: 撰《三國春秋》二十卷，行於代。

translations.literal: He compiled twenty juan of Three Kingdoms Spring and Autumn, which circulated in his era.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote twenty fascicles of Three Kingdoms Spring and Autumn, which circulated widely in his time.

sentences.zh: 自有傳。

translations.literal: He has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: He has a separate biography elsewhere in the histories.

sentences.zh: 成三郎成三郎，幽州漁陽人也。

translations.literal: Cheng Sanlang—Cheng Sanlang was a man of Yuyang in You Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Sanlang was a native of Yuyang in You Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 光宅年，為左豹韜衛長上果毅。

translations.literal: In the Guangzhai era, he served as Senior Commander Fruit-and-Bravery in the Left Leopard-Bow Guard.
translations.idiomatic: During the Guangzhai reign he served as a senior commander in the Left Leopard-Bow Guard.

sentences.zh: 李孝逸之討徐敬業，以為前鋒，與賊戰於高郵。

translations.literal: When Li Xiaoyi campaigned against Xu Jingye, [Cheng Sanlang] was made vanguard and fought the rebels at Gaoyou.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Xiaoyi marched against Xu Jingye, Cheng Sanlang was made vanguard and fought the rebels at Gaoyou.

sentences.zh: 軍國敗績，被擒，送於江都。

translations.literal: The army suffered defeat; he was captured and sent to Jiangdu.
translations.idiomatic: The army was routed; he was captured and sent to Jiangdu.

sentences.zh: 賊黨唐之奇紿其眾曰：「此李孝逸也！」

translations.literal: The rebel Tang Zhiqi deceived the crowd, saying, "This is Li Xiaoyi!"
translations.idiomatic: The rebel Tang Zhiqi lied to the crowd: "This is Li Xiaoyi!

sentences.zh: 將斬之。

translations.literal: They were about to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: They were about to execute him.

sentences.zh: 三郎大呼曰：「我，是果毅成三郎，不是將軍李孝逸。

translations.literal: Sanlang cried out loudly: "I am the Commander Fruit-and-Bravery Cheng Sanlang, not General Li Xiaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: Sanlang shouted: "I am Commander Cheng Sanlang—not General Li Xiaoyi.

sentences.zh: 官軍已圍爾數重，破爾在於朝夕。

translations.literal: The imperial army has already surrounded you in many rings; your defeat is a matter of morning and evening.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial army has you surrounded on every side; your defeat is only days away.

sentences.zh: 我死，妻子受榮；

translations.literal: If I die, my wife and children will receive honor;
translations.idiomatic: If I die, my wife and children will receive honors;

sentences.zh: 爾死，家口配沒，終不及我！」

translations.literal: if you die, your household will be seized as slaves—you will never match me!"
translations.idiomatic: if you die, your family will be enslaved and your property confiscated—you will never do as well as I!

sentences.zh: 之奇怒，斬之。

translations.literal: Zhiqi was enraged and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiqi was furious and had him executed.

sentences.zh: 敬業平，贈左監門將軍，謚曰勇。

translations.literal: When Jingye's rebellion was quelled, [Cheng Sanlang] was posthumously granted General of the Left Gate Guards, posthumous title Yong (Brave).
translations.idiomatic: After Xu Jingye's rebellion was suppressed, he was posthumously made General of the Left Gate Guards, with the posthumous title Brave.

sentences.zh: 時曲阿令尹元貞，亦死敬業之難。

translations.literal: At that time Yin Yuanzhen, magistrate of Qu'e, also died in Jingye's uprising.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Yin Yuanzhen, magistrate of Qu'e, also died in the turmoil of Xu Jingye's rebellion.

sentences.zh: 尹元貞尹元貞者，瀛州河間人也。

translations.literal: Yin Yuanzhen—Yin Yuanzhen was a man of Hejian in Ying Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Yuanzhen was a native of Hejian in Ying Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 在曲阿，聞敬業攻陷潤州，率兵赴援。

translations.literal: While at Qu'e, hearing that Jingye had captured Run Prefecture, he led troops to rescue.
translations.idiomatic: While serving as magistrate of Qu'e, upon hearing that Xu Jingye had taken Runzhou, he led troops to the relief.

sentences.zh: 及戰敗，被擒。

translations.literal: When the battle was lost, he was captured.
translations.idiomatic: After the battle was lost, he was taken prisoner.

sentences.zh: 敬業臨以白刃，脅令附己，將加任用。

translations.literal: Jingye put a naked blade to him, coerced him to join his side, and intended to employ him.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jingye threatened him with drawn swords and tried to force him to join his cause, intending to appoint him to office.

sentences.zh: 元貞詞色慷慨，竟不之屈，尋遇害。

translations.literal: Yuanzhen's words and bearing were passionate and resolute; in the end he would not yield, and soon met with murder.
translations.idiomatic: Yin spoke with passion and held firm until the end; he was soon killed.

sentences.zh: 敬業平，贈潤州刺史，謚曰壯。

translations.literal: When Jingye was quelled, [Yin Yuanzhen] was posthumously granted Governor of Run Prefecture, posthumous title Zhuang (Robust).
translations.idiomatic: After the rebellion was crushed, he was posthumously made Governor of Run Prefecture, with the posthumous title Robust.

sentences.zh: 高睿高睿，雍州萬年人，隋尚書左僕射崿孫也。

translations.literal: Gao Rui—Gao Rui was a man of Wannian in Yong Prefecture, grandson of E, Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs of Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Rui was a native of Wannian in Yong Prefecture and grandson of E, Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs under the Sui.

sentences.zh: 父表仁，谷州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Biaoren was Governor of Gu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His father Biaoren served as Governor of Gu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 睿少以明經累除桂州都督，尋加銀青光祿大夫，轉趙州刺史，封平昌縣子。

translations.literal: Rui in youth, through repeated passes in the Classics examination, was repeatedly removed and appointed Governor of Gui Prefecture; soon he was additionally given Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with Silver Seal, transferred to Governor of Zhao Prefecture, and enfeoffed as Viscount of Pingchang.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Rui entered service through the Classics examination and eventually became Governor of Gui Prefecture; he was later promoted to Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with Silver Seal, transferred to Governor of Zhao Prefecture, and ennobled as Viscount of Pingchang.

sentences.zh: 聖歷初，突厥默啜來寇，睿又嬰城固守。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shenli, when the Türk Mo-ch'o came to raid, Rui again closed the city and held fast.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Shenli era, when the Türk khan Mo-ch'o invaded, Gao Rui again barricaded the city and held out.

sentences.zh: 長史唐波若見城圍甚急，遂潛謀應賊。

translations.literal: Chief Administrator Tang Boruo, seeing the siege was very pressing, secretly plotted to join the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Administrator Tang Boruo, seeing the siege tighten, secretly conspired to surrender to the enemy.

sentences.zh: 睿覺之，將自殺，不死，俄而城陷被擒，更令招喻諸縣未降者。

translations.literal: Rui detected it, attempted suicide but did not die; soon the city fell and he was captured, then was made to summon and persuade the counties that had not yet surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Rui discovered the plot and tried to kill himself but failed; the city soon fell and he was captured, then forced to persuade the counties that had not yet surrendered.

sentences.zh: 睿竟不從，遂為所殺。

translations.literal: Rui in the end would not comply and was thereupon killed by them.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Rui refused to obey and was killed.

sentences.zh: 初，賊將至州境。

translations.literal: Initially, when the bandits were about to reach the prefectural borders.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the invaders were approaching the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 或謂睿曰：「突厥所向無前，百姓喪膽；

translations.literal: Someone said to Rui: "The Türks advance unstoppably wherever they go, and the people have lost their courage;
translations.idiomatic: Someone urged Gao Rui: "The Türks sweep all before them, and the people are terrified;

sentences.zh: 明公力不能禦，不若降之。」

translations.literal: Your Excellency's strength cannot resist them; better to surrender."
translations.idiomatic: you cannot hold them off—better to surrender.

sentences.zh: 睿曰：「吾為天子刺史，不戰而降，其罪大矣。」

translations.literal: Rui said: "I am the Son of Heaven's governor; to surrender without fighting—the crime would be great."
translations.idiomatic: Gao Rui replied: "I am the emperor's governor; to surrender without fighting would be a grave crime.

sentences.zh: 則天聞而深嘆息之，贈冬官尚書，謚曰節。

translations.literal: Empress Wu heard and sighed deeply, posthumously granting him Minister of the Court of Winter Construction, posthumous title Jie (Integrity).
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wu heard of it, she sighed deeply and posthumously made him Minister of the Court of Winter Construction, with the posthumous title Integrity.

sentences.zh: 及賊退，唐波若伏誅，家口籍沒。

translations.literal: When the bandits retreated, Tang Boruo was executed according to law, and his household was registered and confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: After the invaders withdrew, Tang Boruo was executed and his family and property were confiscated.

sentences.zh: 因下制曰：「故趙州刺史高睿，狂賊既至，死節不降；

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict was issued, saying: "The late Governor of Zhao Prefecture Gao Rui, when the wild bandits arrived, died holding his integrity and would not surrender;
translations.idiomatic: An edict was then issued: "The late Governor of Zhao Prefecture, Gao Rui, when the invaders came, held to his duty and refused to surrender;

sentences.zh: 長史唐波若，不能固城，相率歸賊。

translations.literal: Chief Administrator Tang Boruo could not hold the city and led others in surrendering to the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Administrator Tang Boruo failed to hold the city and led others in surrendering to the enemy.

sentences.zh: 高睿已加褒柱，波若等身死破家。

translations.literal: Gao Rui has already received posthumous honors; Boruo and the others died and lost their families.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumous honors have already been conferred on Gao Rui, while Boruo and his accomplices died and lost their families.

sentences.zh: 賞罰既行，須敦懲勸，宜頒示天下，咸使知聞。」

translations.literal: Reward and punishment having been carried out, encouragement and warning must be earnestly applied; this should be promulgated throughout the realm so all may know and hear."
translations.idiomatic: Now that reward and punishment have been applied, let encouragement and warning be made clear; this should be proclaimed throughout the realm so that all may know.

sentences.zh: 睿子 仲舒子仲舒，博通經史，尤明《三禮》及詁訓之書。

translations.literal: Rui's son Zhongshu—Zhongshu was thoroughly versed in the classics and histories, especially expert in the Three Rites and books of exegesis.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Rui's son Zhongshu was deeply learned in the classics and histories and especially expert in the Three Rites and works of textual commentary.

sentences.zh: 神龍中，為相王府文學，王甚敬重之。

translations.literal: In the Shenlong era, he served as Literary Scholar in the Princely Household of Xiang; the prince greatly respected him.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shenlong era he served as literary tutor to the Prince of Xiang, who held him in high esteem.

sentences.zh: 開元中，累授中書舍人，侍中宋璟、中書侍郎蘇颋每詢訪故事焉。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan era, he was repeatedly appointed Drafting Secretary; Chief Minister Song Jing and Vice Director of the Secretariat Su Ting often consulted him on precedents.
translations.idiomatic: In the Kaiyuan era he rose to Drafting Secretary; Chief Minister Song Jing and Vice Director Su Ting often consulted him on precedent.

sentences.zh: 附 崔琳時又有中書舍人崔琳，深達政理，璟等亦禮焉。

translations.literal: Appendix: Cui Lin—at that time there was also Drafting Secretary Cui Lin, who deeply understood governance; Jing and the others also treated him with courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Appendix: Cui Lin—at this time Drafting Secretary Cui Lin also deeply understood statecraft, and Song Jing and his colleagues honored him as well.

sentences.zh: 嘗謂人曰：「古事問高仲舒，今事問崔琳，則又何所疑矣！」

translations.literal: He once said to people: "For ancient matters ask Gao Zhongshu; for present matters ask Cui Lin—then what would there be to doubt!"
translations.idiomatic: Someone once said: "Ask Gao Zhongshu about antiquity and Cui Lin about the present—and what doubt can remain?

sentences.zh: 仲舒累遷太子右庶子卒。

translations.literal: Zhongshu was repeatedly promoted to Right Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household and died in that office.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongshu rose to Right Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household, where he died.

sentences.zh: 王同皎王同皎，相州安陽人，陳侍中、駙馬都尉寬之曾孫。

translations.literal: Wang Tongjiao—Wang Tongjiao was a man of Anyang in Xiang Prefecture, great-grandson of Kuanzhi, Attendant-in-Ordinary and Commandant of the Feathered Forest of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tongjiao was a native of Anyang in Xiang Prefecture and great-grandson of Kuanzhi, Attendant-in-Ordinary and Commandant of the Feathered Forest under Chen.

sentences.zh: 其先自瑯邪仕江左，陳亡，徙家河北。

translations.literal: His ancestors from Langya served in the lands south of the Yangzi; when Chen fell, the family moved to Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: His forebears had left Langya to serve in the south; when Chen fell, the family resettled in Hebei.

sentences.zh: 同皎，長安中尚皇太子女定安郡主。

translations.literal: Tongjiao, during the Chang'an era, married the Princess Ding'an, daughter of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chang'an era, Tongjiao married Princess Ding'an, daughter of the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 授朝散大夫，行太子典膳郎。

translations.literal: He was granted Grand Master for Dispersal and acted as Provisioner of the Heir Apparent's Household.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Grand Master for Dispersal and served as provisioner in the heir apparent's household.

sentences.zh: 敬暉等討張易之兄弟也。

translations.literal: This was when Jing Hui and the others campaigned against the Zhang Yizhi brothers.
translations.idiomatic: This was during the campaign by Jing Hui and his allies against the Zhang Yizhi brothers.

sentences.zh: 遣同皎與右羽林將軍李多祚迎太子於東宮，請太子至玄武門指麾將士。

translations.literal: They dispatched Tongjiao together with General of the Right Feathered Forest Li Duozuo to welcome the Crown Prince from the Eastern Palace and asked the Crown Prince to come to the Xuanwu Gate to command the troops.
translations.idiomatic: They sent Tongjiao with General of the Right Feathered Forest Li Duozuo to bring the crown prince from the Eastern Palace and asked him to take command of the troops at the Xuanwu Gate.

sentences.zh: 太子初拒而不許，同皎諷諭切至，太子乃就駕。

translations.literal: At first the Crown Prince refused and would not consent; Tongjiao admonished him with utmost urgency, and the Crown Prince then mounted his carriage.
translations.idiomatic: At first the crown prince refused, but Tongjiao pressed him with urgent persuasion until he finally took his carriage.

sentences.zh: 以功授右千牛將軍，封瑯邪郡公，賜實封五百戶。

translations.literal: For his merit he was granted General of the Right Thousand-Ox Guard, enfeoffed as Duke of Langya Commandery, and given five hundred taxable households.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was made General of the Right Thousand-Ox Guard, ennobled as Duke of Langya, and granted five hundred taxable households.

sentences.zh: 及郡主進封為公主，拜同皎為駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: When the Princess was advanced in rank to full princess, Tongjiao was appointed Commandant of the Feathered Forest.
translations.idiomatic: When the princess was raised in rank, Tongjiao was made Commandant of the Feathered Forest.

sentences.zh: 尋加銀青光祿大夫，遷光祿卿。

translations.literal: Soon he was additionally given Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with Silver Seal and transferred to Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with Silver Seal and transferred to Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: ，同皎以武三思專權任勢，謀為逆亂，乃招集壯士，期以則天靈駕發引，劫殺三思。

translations.literal: Tongjiao, seeing Wu Sansi monopolize power and wield influence, plotted rebellion; he gathered stalwart men and set the time for when Empress Wu's funeral procession would depart, intending to waylay and kill Sansi.
translations.idiomatic: Tongjiao saw that Wu Sansi had seized power and was plotting treason; he gathered strong men and planned to ambush and kill Sansi when Empress Wu's funeral procession set out.

sentences.zh: 同謀人撫州司倉冉祖雍，具以其計密告三思。

translations.literal: A co-conspirator, Warehouse Clerk of Fuzhou Ran Zuyong, fully reported their plan in secret to Sansi.
translations.idiomatic: A co-conspirator, Ran Zuyong, warehouse clerk of Fuzhou, secretly informed Sansi of the entire plot.

sentences.zh: 三思乃遣校書郎李悛上言：「同皎潛謀殺三思後，將擁兵詣闕，廢黜皇后。」

translations.literal: Sansi then dispatched Proofreader Li Jun to submit a memorial, saying: "Tongjiao secretly plotted that after killing Sansi he would lead troops to the palace gates and depose the empress."
translations.idiomatic: Sansi then had proofreader Li Jun submit a memorial claiming that Tongjiao planned, after killing Sansi, to march on the palace with troops and depose the empress.

sentences.zh: 帝然之，遂斬同皎於都亭驛前，籍沒其家。

translations.literal: The emperor approved; Tongjiao was thereupon executed before the Capital Pavilion Post Station, and his household was registered and confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed, and Tongjiao was executed before the Capital Pavilion Post Station; his family and property were confiscated.

sentences.zh: 臨刑神色不變，天下莫不冤之。

translations.literal: Facing execution, his expression did not change; throughout the realm none did not deem it an injustice.
translations.idiomatic: At the moment of execution his composure never broke, and people everywhere regarded his death as a grievous injustice.

sentences.zh: 睿宗即位，令復其官爵。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ruizong ascended the throne, he ordered Tongjiao's offices and titles restored.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ruizong took the throne, he restored Tongjiao's offices and titles.

sentences.zh: 執冉祖雍、李悛，並誅之。

translations.literal: Ran Zuyong and Li Jun were arrested and both executed.
translations.idiomatic: Ran Zuyong and Li Jun were arrested and executed.

sentences.zh: 附 周憬初與同皎葉謀，有武當丞周憬者，壽州壽春人也。

translations.literal: Appendix: Zhou Jing—Zhou Jing at first plotted together with Tongjiao; there was Assistant Magistrate of Wudang Zhou Jing, a man of Shouchun in Shou Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Appendix: Zhou Jing—who had plotted with Tongjiao from the start—was assistant magistrate of Wudang and a native of Shouchun in Shou Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 事既泄，遁於比幹廟中，自刎而死。

translations.literal: When the affair was exposed, he fled to the Temple of Bi Gan and cut his own throat to die.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot was exposed, he fled to the Temple of Bi Gan and killed himself by cutting his throat.

sentences.zh: 臨終，謂左右曰：「比干，古之忠臣也。

translations.literal: At the end, he said to those beside him: "Bi Gan was a loyal minister of antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed he said to those around him: "Bi Gan was a loyal minister of old.

sentences.zh: 倘神道聰明，應知周憬忠而死也。

translations.literal: If the spirit way is discerning, it should know that Zhou Jing died in loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: If the spirits are just, they will know that Zhou Jing died loyal to the throne.

sentences.zh: 韋后亂朝，寵樹邪佞，武三思幹上犯順，虐害忠良，吾知其滅亡不久也！

translations.literal: Empress Wei has thrown the court into disorder, favoring and raising the wicked and flatterers; Wu Sansi has violated superiors and rebelled against order, cruelly harming the loyal and good—I know their destruction will come before long!
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wei has thrown the court into chaos, elevating the wicked; Wu Sansi has defied the throne and slaughtered the loyal—I know their ruin cannot be far off!

sentences.zh: 可懸吾頭於國門，觀其身首異門而出。」

translations.literal: You may hang my head at the state gate and watch his body and head pass out through different gates."
translations.idiomatic: Hang my head at the capital gate—and watch his body and head leave by different gates.

sentences.zh: 其後皆如其言。

translations.literal: Afterwards all came to pass as he had said.
translations.idiomatic: Everything later happened just as he had predicted.

sentences.zh: 蘇安恆蘇安恆，冀州武邑人也。

translations.literal: Su Anheng—Su Anheng was a man of Wuyi in Ji Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Su Anheng was a native of Wuyi in Ji Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 博學，尤明《周禮》及《春秋左氏傳》。

translations.literal: Broadly learned, he was especially expert in the Rites of Zhou and the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: He was broadly learned and especially expert in the Rites of Zhou and the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals.

sentences.zh: ，投匭上疏曰：

translations.literal: , [he] cast [a memorial] into the suggestion box and submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial through the suggestion box, saying:

sentences.zh: 陛下欽聖皇之顧托，受嗣子之推讓，應天順人，二十年矣。

translations.literal: Your Majesty reverently received the late sage emperor's entrustment, accepted the heir's yielding of place, and has accorded with Heaven and followed the people for twenty years now.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty reverently accepted the late emperor's charge, took the throne when the heir yielded it, and has ruled in accord with Heaven and the people's will for twenty years.

sentences.zh: 豈不思虞舜褰裳，周公復辟，良以大禹至聖，成王既長，推位讓國，其道備焉！

translations.literal: Have you not considered how Yu Shun lifted his robe, how the Duke of Zhou restored the throne—indeed because Yu the Great was supremely sage and King Cheng had already grown, yielding rank and yielding the state—the Way was complete therein!
translations.idiomatic: Have you not considered how Shun yielded the throne, how the Duke of Zhou restored King Cheng—how the greatest sages, when the heir had come of age, gave up power and restored rightful rule? Their example is complete!

sentences.zh: 故舜之於禹，是其族親；

translations.literal: Therefore Shun toward Yu was his kinsman by clan;
translations.idiomatic: Shun yielded the throne to Yu, who was his kinsman by clan;

sentences.zh: 旦舉成王，不離叔父。

translations.literal: Dan raised King Cheng, never leaving the role of paternal uncle.
translations.idiomatic: the Duke of Zhou restored King Cheng, never abandoning his role as royal uncle.

sentences.zh: 且族親何如子之愛？

translations.literal: Moreover, how can kinship by clan compare with a father's love for his son?
translations.idiomatic: And how can kinship by clan compare with a father's love for his own son?

sentences.zh: 叔父何如母之恩？

translations.literal: How can a paternal uncle compare with a mother's grace?
translations.idiomatic: And how can an uncle's bond compare with a mother's loving devotion?

sentences.zh: 今太子孝敬是崇，春秋既壯，若使統臨宸極，何異陛下之隧！

translations.literal: Now the Crown Prince holds filial piety and respect as his devotion; his years are already full-grown. If he were made to rule the imperial throne, how would it differ from Your Majesty's own succession!
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince already excels in filial devotion and has come of age. If he ascends the throne, would that not merely continue Your Majesty's own imperial line?

sentences.zh: 陛下年德既尊，寶位將倦，機務殷重，浩蕩心神，何不禪位東宮，自怡聖體！

translations.literal: Your Majesty's years and virtue are already esteemed; the precious throne grows wearying; state affairs are numerous and heavy, overwhelming the imperial heart and spirit—why not abdicate to the Eastern Palace and nourish Your Majesty's sacred person!
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's age and moral stature are venerable, the burden of rule is exhausting, and the press of governance overwhelms body and mind. Why not transfer the throne to the Crown Prince and grant yourself peace?

sentences.zh: 臣聞自昔明王之孝理天下者，不見二姓而俱王也。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that since antiquity, enlightened kings who governed the realm with filial piety never saw two surnames both ruling as kings.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that no enlightened sovereign who ruled through filial virtue ever allowed two royal houses to reign at once.

sentences.zh: 當今梁、定、河內、建昌諸王等，承陛下之廕覆，並得封王，臣恐千秋萬歲之後，於事非便，臣請黜為公侯，任以閑簡。

translations.literal: At present the princes of Liang, Ding, Hennei, Jianchang, and others, receiving Your Majesty's sheltering shade, have all been enfeoffed as kings. Your subject fears that after a thousand autumns and ten thousand years this will prove inconvenient for affairs. Your subject requests they be demoted to dukes and marquises and assigned to idle and simple posts.
translations.idiomatic: The Princes of Liang, Ding, Hennei, Jianchang, and others now enjoy royal rank thanks to Your Majesty's favor. I fear that in generations to come this will prove unwise. I urge that they be reduced to dukes and marquises and given only light, honorary duties.

sentences.zh: 臣又聞陛下有二十餘孫，今無尺土之封，此非長久之計也。

translations.literal: Your subject further hears that Your Majesty has more than twenty grandsons, yet now none receives even a handspan of territory as a fief—this is no plan for the long term.
translations.idiomatic: I also note that Your Majesty has more than twenty grandsons, yet none holds so much as an inch of land. That is no lasting policy.

sentences.zh: 臣請四面都督府及要沖州郡，分土而王之。

translations.literal: Your subject requests that across the frontier military commissions and strategic prefectures and districts, territory be divided and they be made kings.
translations.idiomatic: I propose enfeoffing them as regional princes across the frontier commanderies and key prefectures, each with his own domain.

sentences.zh: 縱今年尚幼小，未嫻養人之術，請擇立師傅，成其孝敬之道，將以夾輔周室，籓屏皇家，使累葉重光，饗祀不輟，斯為美矣，豈不大哉！

translations.literal: Even if they are still young this year and not yet practiced in the art of nurturing people, please select and establish tutors for them, complete their path of filial piety and respect, and thereby have them flank and assist the Zhou house, serve as ramparts and screens for the imperial family, so that generation after generation shines anew and sacrifices never cease—this would be beautiful indeed; is it not grand!
translations.idiomatic: Even if they are still young and untrained in governance, appoint tutors to instill filial virtue, so they may support the imperial house, guard the dynasty, and keep the ancestral rites unbroken for generations—what could be nobler?

sentences.zh: 疏奏，則天召見，賜食慰諭而遣之。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, Zetian summoned him for audience, bestowed food, comforted and instructed him, and sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial reached her, Empress Wu summoned Su Anheng, shared a meal with him, offered reassuring words, and dismissed him.

sentences.zh: 長安二年，又上疏曰：

translations.literal: In the second year of Chang'an, he submitted another memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: In Chang'an 2 (702 CE), he submitted another memorial stating:

sentences.zh: 忠臣不順時而取寵，烈士不惜死而偷生。

translations.literal: A loyal minister does not follow the times to win favor; a man of heroic resolve does not spare death yet cling to life.
translations.idiomatic: A loyal minister does not trim his convictions to win favor; a man of principle does not cling to life at the cost of honor.

sentences.zh: 故君道不明者，忠臣之過歟！

translations.literal: Therefore when the way of the ruler is not clear, is it not the loyal minister's failing!
translations.idiomatic: When the ruler's path grows murky, is that not the loyal minister's duty to speak out!

sentences.zh: 臣道不軌者，烈士之過歟！

translations.literal: When the minister's way is not proper, is it not the man of heroic resolve's failing!
translations.idiomatic: When ministers stray from the right path, is that not where men of courage must act!

sentences.zh: 昔者先皇晏駕，留其顧托，將以萬機殷廣，令陛下兼知其事。

translations.literal: Formerly when the late emperor passed peacefully, he left his final charge, intending because state affairs were numerous and vast to have Your Majesty share in knowing these matters.
translations.idiomatic: When the late Emperor Gaozong died, he entrusted the realm to Your Majesty precisely because the burden of rule was too vast for any one person.

sentences.zh: 雖唐堯、虞舜居其位，而共工、驩兜在其間，陛下骨肉之恩阻，陛下子母之愛忘。

translations.literal: Even though Tang Yao and Yu Shun occupied their thrones, Gong Gong and Huan Dou were among them; Your Majesty's flesh-and-blood affections were blocked, and Your Majesty's love between mother and son was forgotten.
translations.idiomatic: Even Yao and Shun on the throne had villains like Gong Gong and Huan Dou in their courts. Under such influence, Your Majesty's bond with your own kin was severed, and the love between mother and son was cast aside.

sentences.zh: 臣謂聖情以運祚將喪，極斯大節；

translations.literal: Your subject considers that in Your Majesty's sage heart, because the dynastic fortune was about to perish, You exerted this supreme resolve;
translations.idiomatic: I believe Your Majesty, seeing the dynasty near ruin, seized upon this ultimate expedient;

sentences.zh: 天下謂陛下微弱李氏，貪天之功。

translations.literal: The realm considers that Your Majesty weakened the Li house and greedily claimed Heaven's achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the people believe Your Majesty has diminished the Li clan and claimed Heaven's credit for Yourself.

sentences.zh: 何以年在耄倦，而不能復子明辟，使忠言莫進，奸佞成朋，夷狄紛擾，屠害黎庶！

translations.literal: Why, with years already in aged weariness, can You not restore the son and clarify the throne, causing loyal words to fail to advance, flatterers and villains to form factions, barbarians to stir in disorder, and slaughter harm to the common people!
translations.idiomatic: Why, in Your advanced years, do You not restore the throne to Your son, so loyal counsel may be heard, sycophants may be scattered, barbarian unrest checked, and the people spared from slaughter?

sentences.zh: 陛下雖納隍軫念，亦罔能救此生靈。

translations.literal: Even though Your Majesty harbors compassionate concern, still You cannot save these living souls.
translations.idiomatic: Though Your Majesty feels pity for the people, You still cannot save them from suffering.

sentences.zh: 臣聞天下者，神堯、文武之天下也。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that the realm belongs to Divine Yao and King Wen-Wu's realm.
translations.idiomatic: The empire belongs to the house founded by Emperor Gaozu and consolidated by Emperor Taizong.

sentences.zh: 昔有隋失馭，小人道長，群雄駭鹿，四海瞻烏。

translations.literal: Formerly when Sui lost control of the reins, petty men grew long in their way, rival heroes panicked like deer at the hunt, and all within the four seas gazed toward the crow.
translations.idiomatic: When Sui lost the mandate, villains flourished, warlords battled like hunters chasing a deer, and the nation watched to see who would seize power.

sentences.zh: 皇唐親事戎旃，鳳翔參野，削平宇縣，龍踐宸極。

translations.literal: Great Tang personally undertook military banners, phoenixes soared and mingled with the wilds, carved flat the universe within the borders, and the dragon stepped upon the imperial throne.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang house took up arms, rose like a phoenix over the land, conquered the realm, and ascended the imperial throne.

sentences.zh: 歃血為盟，指河為誓，非李氏不王，非功臣不封。

translations.literal: They tasted blood to form alliance, pointed to the river to swear oath—none but the Li house would be king, none but meritorious ministers would be enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: They swore binding oaths by blood and river: only the Li clan could rule, only meritorious subjects could hold noble rank.

sentences.zh: 陛下雖居正統，實唐氏舊基。

translations.literal: Your Majesty although occupies the orthodox succession, in truth it is the old foundation of the Tang house.
translations.idiomatic: Though You hold legitimate rule, it rests upon the Tang dynasty's foundation.

sentences.zh: 故《詩》曰：「惟鵲有巢，唯鳩居之。」

translations.literal: Therefore the Odes says: "Only the magpie had a nest; only the cuckoo dwells in it.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Poetry says: "The magpie built the nest, but the cuckoo lives in it.

sentences.zh: 此言雖小，可以喻大。

translations.literal: This saying although small can serve to parable the large.
translations.idiomatic: Though the image is small, it speaks to a great truth.

sentences.zh: 陛下自坤生德，乘乾作主，豈不以上符天意，下順人心！

translations.literal: Your Majesty from the feminine generated virtue, mounted the masculine to become ruler—should this not above accord with Heaven's intent and below follow the people's hearts!
translations.idiomatic: You rose from woman's station to hold imperial power—surely this should align with Heaven above and the hearts of the people below!

sentences.zh: 東宮昔在諒陰，相王又非長子，陛下恐宗祀中絕，所以應其謳歌。

translations.literal: The Eastern Palace formerly was in mourning white; the Prince of Xiang was moreover not the eldest son—Your Majesty feared the ancestral sacrifices would be cut off midway, therefore You responded to their songs of praise.
translations.idiomatic: When the Crown Prince was in mourning and the Prince of Xiang was not the eldest son, You feared the imperial line would perish and therefore answered the people's call to rule.

sentences.zh: 當今太子追回，年德俱盛，陛下貪其寶位而忘母子深恩。

translations.literal: At present the Crown Prince has been recalled; years and virtue are both flourishing—Your Majesty covets the precious throne and forgets the deep grace between mother and son.
translations.idiomatic: Now the Crown Prince has been restored, mature in years and virtue, yet You cling to the throne and forget the deep bond of mother and son.

sentences.zh: 臣聞京邑翼翼，四方取則。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that the capital city is guarded in majesty, and the four quarters take it as their model.
translations.idiomatic: I know that the capital sets the pattern for the entire realm.

sentences.zh: 陛下蔽太子之元良，枉太子之神器，何以教天下母慈子孝！

translations.literal: Your Majesty obscures the Crown Prince's excellence as heir, wrongs the Crown Prince's divine vessel—how can You teach the realm motherly kindness and filial sonship!
translations.idiomatic: By hiding the Crown Prince's rightful station and depriving him of the throne, how can You teach the empire filial devotion between mother and son!

sentences.zh: 焉能使天下移風易俗焉？

translations.literal: How can You cause the realm to shift customs and change practices?
translations.idiomatic: How then can You expect the realm to reform its morals?

sentences.zh: 惟陛下思之，將何聖顏以見唐家宗廟？

translations.literal: Only may Your Majesty ponder this—with what sage countenance will You face the Tang family's ancestral temple?
translations.idiomatic: Consider, Your Majesty: with what face will You stand before the Tang ancestral shrines?

sentences.zh: 將何誥命以謁大帝墳陵？

translations.literal: With what imperial edict will You visit the Great Emperor's tomb and mound?
translations.idiomatic: With what title will You approach the late Emperor's tomb?

sentences.zh: 陛下何故日夜積憂，不知鐘鳴漏盡？

translations.literal: Your Majesty for what reason day and night accumulates worry, not knowing the bell has struck and the water clock run dry?
translations.idiomatic: Why do You heap up worry day and night, heedless that Your hours are running out?

sentences.zh: 臣愚以天意人事，還歸李家。

translations.literal: Your subject in foolishness considers that Heaven's intent and human affairs should return to the Li house.
translations.idiomatic: In my humble view, both Heaven and the people call for the return of the Li dynasty.

sentences.zh: 陛下雖安天位，殊不知物極則反，器滿則傾。

translations.literal: Your Majesty although peacefully occupies Heaven's throne, yet does not know that things at their extreme then reverse, vessels when full then topple.
translations.idiomatic: Though You sit securely on the throne, You do not see that what rises must fall and what fills must spill.

sentences.zh: 故語曰：「當斷不斷，反受其亂。」

translations.literal: Therefore the saying goes: "When one ought to decide yet does not decide, in turn one receives chaos.
translations.idiomatic: As the proverb warns: "He who hesitates when he should act invites disaster.

sentences.zh: 此之謂也。

translations.literal: This is what it refers to.
translations.idiomatic: That is precisely the danger You face.

sentences.zh: 陛下不如高揖機務，自恬聖躬，命史臣以書之，令樂府以歌之，斯亦太平之盛事也！

translations.literal: Your Majesty would do better to loftily yield the keys of state, tranquilly nourish Your sacred person, command the historiographers to record it, and order the Music Bureau to sing of it—this too would be a grand event of great peace!
translations.idiomatic: Better to surrender the reins of power, tend Your health, and let historians and musicians celebrate Your abdication as an act of peace—what glory that would be!

sentences.zh: 臣聞見過不諫，非忠臣也；

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that seeing fault yet not remonstrating is not a loyal minister;
translations.idiomatic: To see wrong and remain silent is not the act of a loyal minister;

sentences.zh: 畏死不言，非勇士也。

translations.literal: Fearing death yet not speaking is not a brave warrior.
translations.idiomatic: To fear death and hold one's tongue is not the mark of a brave man.

sentences.zh: 臣何惜一朝之命，而不安萬乘之國哉！

translations.literal: Why should Your subject cherish one morning's life, yet not secure the state of ten thousand chariots!
translations.idiomatic: Why should I value one day's life above the stability of the empire?

sentences.zh: 故曰：茍利國家，雖死可矣！

translations.literal: Therefore it is said: if it profits the state, even death is acceptable!
translations.idiomatic: As the maxim runs: if it serves the state, one may face death without regret!

sentences.zh: 願陛下稍輟萬機，詳臣愚見。

translations.literal: May Your Majesty briefly pause the myriad affairs of state and examine your subject's foolish view in detail.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to set aside the press of governance and give earnest heed to my counsel.

sentences.zh: 陛下若以臣為忠，則從諫如流，擇是而用；

translations.literal: If Your Majesty considers your subject loyal, then follow remonstrance like flowing water and select what is right and employ it;
translations.idiomatic: If You judge me loyal, accept my counsel freely and act on what is right;

sentences.zh: 若以臣為不忠，則斬取臣頭，以令天下。

translations.literal: If You consider your subject disloyal, then cut off your subject's head to command the realm.
translations.idiomatic: If You deem me disloyal, take my head and make an example for all the realm.

sentences.zh: 疏奏不納。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted but not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was rejected.

sentences.zh: 明年，御史大夫魏元忠為張易之兄弟所構，安恆又抗疏申理之曰：

translations.literal: The following year, Censor-in-Chief Wei Yuanzhong was framed by the Zhang Yizhi brothers; Anheng again submitted a defiant memorial to argue on his behalf, saying:
translations.idiomatic: The next year, when Censor-in-Chief Wei Yuanzhong was framed by Zhang Yizhi and his brother, Su Anheng submitted another bold memorial in his defense:

sentences.zh: 臣聞明王有含天下之量，有濟天下之心，能進天下之善，除天下之惡。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that an enlightened king has a capacity to embrace all under Heaven, has a heart to rescue all under Heaven, can advance all under Heaven's goodness, and remove all under Heaven's evil.
translations.idiomatic: A wise ruler embraces the world, seeks to save it, promotes what is good, and uproots what is evil.

sentences.zh: 若為君王而不行此四者，則當神冤鬼怒，陰錯陽亂，欲使國家榮泰，其可得乎！

translations.literal: If as ruler one does not practice these four things, then spirits will harbor grievances and ghosts rage, yin and yang will err and fall into chaos—wishing to make the state flourish in glory and peace, can this be attained!
translations.idiomatic: A ruler who neglects these duties invites the wrath of Heaven and chaos in the land—how then can the state prosper?

sentences.zh: 陛下革命之初，勤於庶政，親總萬機，博采謀猷，傍求俊乂，故海內以陛下為納諫之主矣！

translations.literal: At the beginning of Your Majesty's transformation of the mandate, You were diligent in numerous government affairs, personally overseeing myriad state matters, broadly gathering counsel and plans, widely seeking brilliant talent—therefore within the seas they regarded Your Majesty as a ruler who accepts remonstrance!
translations.idiomatic: When You first seized power, You were diligent in governance, personally oversaw affairs, sought wise counsel, and recruited talent—the realm hailed You as a ruler who welcomed honest advice.

sentences.zh: 暮年已來，怠於政教，讒邪結黨，水火成災，百姓不親，五品不遜，故四海之內，以陛下為受佞之主矣！

translations.literal: Since Your later years, You have been slack in government and teaching; slanderers and villains form factions, water and fire become disaster; the hundred surnames are not close, the five ranks are not submissive—therefore within the four seas they regard Your Majesty as a ruler who receives flatterers!
translations.idiomatic: In Your later years You have neglected governance; sycophants have formed factions, disasters have multiplied, the people have grown estranged, and officials have grown insolent—the realm now calls You a ruler who indulges flatterers.

sentences.zh: 當今邪正莫辯，訴訟含冤，豈陛下昔是而今非，蓋居安忘危之失也！

translations.literal: At present the wicked and upright cannot be distinguished; lawsuits hold grievances and injustice—is this not Your Majesty's being right before and wrong now? It is roughly the failure of dwelling in peace and forgetting peril!
translations.idiomatic: Right and wrong can no longer be told apart, and the courts overflow with injustice—is this not the error of growing complacent in security?

sentences.zh: 臣竊見御史大夫、檢校太子右庶子、同鳳閣鸞臺平章事魏元忠，廉直有聞，位居宰輔。

translations.literal: Your subject privately observes Censor-in-Chief, Acting Right Vice Director of the Crown Prince's Household, Fellow of the Phoenix Pavilion and Luan Terrace Wei Yuanzhong—integrity and uprightness are renowned, position is among chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: I speak of Wei Yuanzhong, Censor-in-Chief and chief minister, whose integrity is widely known.

sentences.zh: 履忠正之基者，用元忠為龜鏡；

translations.literal: Those who tread the foundation of loyalty and rectitude take Yuanzhong as tortoise mirror;
translations.idiomatic: Those who walk the path of righteousness hold Yuanzhong up as a mirror;

sentences.zh: 踐邪佞之路者，嫉元忠若仇讎。

translations.literal: Those who tread the path of wicked flattery hate Yuanzhong like mortal enemies.
translations.idiomatic: Those who traffic in corruption hate him as a mortal enemy.

sentences.zh: 麟臺監張易之兄弟，在身無德，於國無功，不逾數年，遂極隆貴。

translations.literal: Director of the Lin Platform Zhang Yizhi and his brothers—in person have no virtue, for the state have no merit; in no more than several years they reached ultimate lofty nobility.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yizhi and his brother, holders of high office, are men of no personal virtue and no public service, yet within a few years they rose to the highest honor.

sentences.zh: 自當飲冰懷懼，酌水思清，夙夜兢兢，以答恩造。

translations.literal: They themselves ought to drink ice and harbor fear, pour water and think of clarity, morning and night be cautious and fearful, to repay the grace that created them.
translations.idiomatic: They ought to have trembled with gratitude, lived in scrupulous fear, and repaid Your favor with loyal service.

sentences.zh: 不謂溪壑其志，豺狼其心，欲指鹿而獻馬，先害忠而損善；

translations.literal: One does not expect their ravines and gullies for ambition, their wolf-like hearts—they wish to point at a deer and present it as a horse, first harming the loyal and damaging the good;
translations.idiomatic: Instead their appetites are bottomless and their hearts wolfish; they would twist truth like the deer-and-horse trick, destroy the loyal and corrupt the good.

sentences.zh: 將斯亂代之法，汙我明君之朝。

translations.literal: They will use these methods of chaotic ages to stain our enlightened ruler's court.
translations.idiomatic: They would import the tactics of a fallen dynasty and defile this enlightened court.

sentences.zh: 自元忠下獄，臣見長安城內，街談巷議，皆以陛下委任奸宄，斥逐賢良，以元忠必無不順之言，以易之必有交亂之意，相逢偶語，人心不安。

translations.literal: Since Yuanzhong entered prison, your subject has seen within Chang'an city, talk in streets and alleys—all consider that Your Majesty entrusted office to treacherous villains, dismissed and drove away the worthy and good; that Yuanzhong certainly had no rebellious words, that Yizhi certainly harbored designs to stir turmoil; meeting by chance they converse in whispers, people's hearts are unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: Since Yuanzhong's imprisonment, I hear throughout Chang'an whispers that You have entrusted villains and cast out the worthy, that Yuanzhong spoke no treason, that Yizhi schemes to sow chaos—and everywhere anxiety spreads.

sentences.zh: 雖有忠臣烈士，空撫髀於私室。

translations.literal: Although there are loyal ministers and heroic resolve men, in vain they stroke their thighs in private chambers.
translations.idiomatic: Even loyal men can only clench their fists in private frustration.

sentences.zh: 而鉗口不敢言者，皆懼易之等威權，恐無辜而受戮，亦徒虛死耳！

translations.literal: Yet those whose mouths are clamped shut and dare not speak—all fear Yizhi and company's aweful power, fear suffering execution though innocent—also would die in vain only!
translations.idiomatic: Those who dare not speak do so from fear of Yizhi's power, knowing that to protest would mean a meaningless death.

sentences.zh: 今賊虜強盛，征斂煩重，以臣言之，萬姓不勝其弊。

translations.literal: Now bandit invaders are strong and flourishing; levies and collections are troublesome and heavy—in your subject's words, the myriad surnames cannot bear their harm.
translations.idiomatic: Barbarian enemies grow strong, taxes grow heavier still, and the people can bear no more.

sentences.zh: 況又聞陛下縱逸讒慝，禁錮良善，賞刑失中，則遐邇生變。

translations.literal: Moreover your subject further hears that Your Majesty indulges and releases slanderous villains, imprisons the worthy and good, rewards and punishments miss the center—then far and near will produce change.
translations.idiomatic: Worse, I hear that You indulge sycophants, imprison the good, and misapply reward and punishment—so unrest stirs near and far.

sentences.zh: 臣恐四夷因之，則窺覘得失，以為邊郡之患；

translations.literal: Your subject fears the four barbarians will thereby take advantage, then spy and observe gains and losses, making it a calamity for frontier districts;
translations.idiomatic: I fear foreign peoples will seize the moment, probing our weakness and threatening the borders;

sentences.zh: 百姓因之，即結聚義兵，以除君側之惡。

translations.literal: The common people thereby will gather righteous troops to remove evil beside the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: the people may rise in righteous armies to purge the evil at Your side.

sentences.zh: 復恐逐鹿之黨，叩關而至；

translations.literal: Your subject further fears parties contending for the realm will knock at the passes and arrive;
translations.idiomatic: I fear rival warlords will storm the gates,

sentences.zh: 亂階之徒，從中相應；

translations.literal: Those who give rise to disorder will respond from within.
translations.idiomatic: and agents of rebellion will answer from within.

sentences.zh: 爭鋒於朱雀門內，問鼎於大明殿前，陛下將何事以謝之？

translations.literal: Contending points of edge within the Vermilion Bird Gate, inquiring of the tripods before the Great Bright Hall—Your Majesty will use what affair to apologize to them?
translations.idiomatic: If battle erupts at the palace gates and rebels seize the throne, what answer will You give?

sentences.zh: 復何方以禦之？

translations.literal: With what direction again will You resist them?
translations.idiomatic: With what means will You defend Yourself?

sentences.zh: 臣今為陛下計，安百姓之心者，莫若收雷電之威，解元忠之網，復其爵位，君臣如初，則天下幸甚！

translations.literal: Your subject now plans for Your Majesty—what settles the common people's hearts, nothing is better than withdrawing thunder-and-lightning awefulness, releasing Yuanzhong from the net, restoring his rank and title, ruler and minister as at first—then the realm would be greatly fortunate!
translations.idiomatic: The surest way to calm the people is to recall Your wrath, free Yuanzhong, restore his rank, and renew harmony between ruler and minister.

sentences.zh: 陛下好生惡殺，縱不能斬佞臣頭以塞人望，臣請奪其榮寵，翦其羽翼，無使權柄在手，驕橫日滋。

translations.literal: Your Majesty loves life and hates killing; even if You cannot cut off the flatterer ministers' heads to satisfy the people's expectation, your subject requests stripping their honor and favor, trimming their wings—do not let power's handle be in their hands, insolence grow daily.
translations.idiomatic: Though Your Majesty abhors bloodshed and cannot execute these men as the people wish, at least strip them of rank and power before their arrogance grows beyond control.

sentences.zh: 專國倍於穰侯，回天過於左悺，則社稷危矣，惟陛下圖之！

translations.literal: Monopolizing the state more than double Marquis Rang, turning back Heaven exceeding Zuo Yan—then altars of soil and grain would be endangered! Only may Your Majesty plan for this!
translations.idiomatic: If they monopolize power as the Marquis of Rang once did, or sway the throne as Zuo Yan did, the dynasty itself will be at risk—I beg Your Majesty to act!

sentences.zh: 臣本微賤，不識元忠、易之，豈此可親而彼可疏？

translations.literal: Your subject by origin is low and humble, does not know and distinguish Yuanzhong and Yizhi—is this one to be close and that one to be distant?
translations.idiomatic: I am a man of no account and know neither Yuanzhong nor Yizhi personally—why would I favor one and attack the other?

sentences.zh: 但恐讒邪長而忠臣絕！

translations.literal: Only fearing slander and wickedness grow long while loyal ministers are cut off!
translations.idiomatic: I speak only because I fear that flatterers will flourish while loyal men are silenced forever.

sentences.zh: 伏願陛下暫垂天鑒，察臣此心，即微臣朝誌得行，夕死無恨！

translations.literal: Prostrate, your subject wishes Your Majesty briefly to let fall Heaven's mirror, inspect your subject's this heart—even if your humble subject's morning ambition is fulfilled, dying at evening would be without regret!
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to look upon my heart with Heaven's clarity—if my counsel is heeded, I would die at dusk without regret.

sentences.zh: 疏奏，易之等大怒，欲遣刺客殺之。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, Yizhi and the others were greatly enraged and wished to dispatch assassins to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, Zhang Yizhi and his allies were furious and tried to send assassins to kill him.

sentences.zh: 賴正諫大夫朱敬則、鳳閣舍人桓彥範、著作郎魏知古等保護以免。

translations.literal: Thanks to Rectifying Remonstrance Grandee Zhu Jingze, Phoenix Pavilion Attendant Huan Yanfan, Compiler Wei Zegu, and others protecting him, he escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: Only the intervention of Zhu Jingze, Huan Yanfan, Wei Zegu, and others saved his life.

sentences.zh: 安恆，神龍初為集藝館內教。

translations.literal: Anheng, at the beginning of Shenlong served as inner instructor in the Hall of Gathered Arts.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Shenlong era, Su Anheng served as a tutor in the Hall of Gathered Arts.

sentences.zh: 節湣太子之殺武三思也，或言安恆預其謀，遂下獄死。

translations.literal: When the Sorrow-Moderating Crown Prince killed Wu Sansi, some said Anheng participated in the plot—thereupon he was imprisoned and died.
translations.idiomatic: When Crown Prince Jiemin killed Wu Sansi, some accused Su Anheng of complicity; he was thrown into prison and executed.

sentences.zh: 睿宗即位，知其冤，下制曰：「故蘇安恆，文學基身，鯁直成操，往年抗疏，忠讜可嘉。

translations.literal: When Ruizong ascended the throne, knowing his injustice, issued an edict saying: "The late Su Anheng—literary learning founded his person, straightforward firmness formed his conduct; in former years he submitted defiant memorials, loyal and forthright, praiseworthy.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ruizong took the throne, learning of the injustice, he issued an edict: "The late Su Anheng built his life on learning and cultivated unyielding integrity. His bold memorials of years past were loyal and admirable.

sentences.zh: 屬回邪擅構，奄從非命，興言軫悼，用惻於懷。

translations.literal: Just as treacherous villains arbitrarily fabricated charges, suddenly he followed untimely death; raising the matter brings compassionate grief, causing sorrow in the heart.
translations.idiomatic: Treacherous men engineered his downfall and cut short his life unjustly—a fact that fills Us with deep sorrow.

sentences.zh: 宜贈寵章，式旌徽烈，可贈諫議大夫。」

translations.literal: Properly to bestow favored insignia, thereby to display meritorious glory—may he be posthumously granted Remonstrance Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: Let honor be conferred to mark his virtue—we posthumously appoint him Remonstrance Grandee.

sentences.zh: 時又有俞文俊、王求禮，亦以直言見稱。

translations.literal: At that time there were also Yu Wenjun and Wang Qiuli, likewise famed for blunt speech.
translations.idiomatic: Two other men of blunt counsel were also remembered: Yu Wenjun and Wang Qiuli.

sentences.zh: 俞文俊俞文俊者，荊州江陵人。

translations.literal: Yu Wenjun—Yu Wenjun was a man of Jiangling in Jing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Wenjun was a native of Jiangling in Jing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 則天載初年，新豐因風雷山移，乃改縣名為慶山，四方畢賀。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zetian's Zai era, in Xinfeng because of wind and thunder a mountain shifted—thereupon the county name was changed to Qingshan [Celebration Mountain], and the four directions all congratulated.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Zai reign era, a mountain shifted in Xinfeng during a thunderstorm; the county was renamed Celebration Mountain, and congratulations poured in from every quarter.

sentences.zh: 文俊詣闕上書曰：「臣聞天氣不和而寒暑並，人氣不知而疣贅生，地氣不和而塠阜出。

translations.literal: Wenjun went to the palace gate and submitted a memorial saying: "Your subject has heard when Heaven's qi is not harmonious then cold and heat occur together; when human qi is not knowing then warts and excrescences grow; when Earth's qi is not harmonious then mounds and knolls emerge.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Wenjun submitted a memorial stating: "When Heaven loses harmony, winter and summer come at once; when the body loses balance, tumors form; when Earth loses harmony, the ground itself heaves upward.

sentences.zh: 今陛下以女主處陽位，反易剛柔，故地氣隔塞而山變為災。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty with a female ruler occupying the yang position, reversing yielding and firm—therefore Earth's qi is blocked and obstructed and mountains transform into disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, a woman holding the throne reserved for men, has inverted the natural order—and so the earth chokes and mountains collapse in warning.

sentences.zh: 陛下謂之慶山，臣以為非慶也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty calls it Celebration Mountain; your subject considers it is not celebration.
translations.idiomatic: You call this Celebration Mountain, but I say it is no cause for celebration.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為宜側身修德，以答天譴。

translations.literal: Your subject in foolishness considers You ought to restrain your person and cultivate virtue to answer Heaven's reprimand.
translations.idiomatic: I urge You to mend Your ways and cultivate virtue to answer Heaven's warning.

sentences.zh: 不然，恐殃禍至矣！」

translations.literal: If not so, I fear calamity and disaster will arrive!
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise, I fear disaster will follow.

sentences.zh: 則天大怒，流於嶺外。

translations.literal: Zetian was greatly enraged and exiled him beyond the mountain ranges.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu was furious and banished him to the far south.

sentences.zh: 後為六道使所殺。

translations.literal: Later he was killed by the Six-Circuit Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was later murdered by a regional commissioner.

sentences.zh: 王求禮王求禮者，許州長社人。

translations.literal: Wang Qiuli—Wang Qiuli was a man of Changshe in Xu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qiuli was a native of Changshe in Xu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 則天時，為左拾遺。

translations.literal: During Zetian's time, he served as Left Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: Under Empress Wu he served as Left Reminder.

sentences.zh: 時武懿宗統兵討契丹，畏愞不敢進。

translations.literal: At that time Wu Yizong commanded troops to campaign against the Khitan, fearful and timid not daring to advance.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Yizong led troops against the Khitan, he was too cowardly to advance.

sentences.zh: 及賊平，懿宗奏滄、瀛等數百家從賊，請誅之。

translations.literal: When the bandits were pacified, Yizong memorialized that several hundred households of Cang, Ying, and others followed the bandits, requesting their execution.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebellion was crushed, he reported that several hundred families from Cangzhou and Yingzhou had joined the enemy and asked that they be put to death.

sentences.zh: 求禮廷折之曰：「此等素無武備，城池不完，遇賊畏懼，茍從之以求生，豈素有背叛之心也！

translations.literal: Qiuli in the court refuted him, saying: "These people by nature have no military preparations; city walls are not complete; encountering bandits they were fearful, grasping to follow them in order to seek life—how could they by nature have had hearts of betrayal!
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qiuli rebuked him in open court: "These people had no arms, their walls were broken, and when the enemy came they submitted out of terror to save their lives—how can You call that treason?

sentences.zh: 懿宗擁強兵數十萬，聞賊輒退，使其滋蔓。

translations.literal: Yizong possessed strong troops numbering several tens of thousands; hearing of bandits he would withdraw each time, causing them to spread and flourish.
translations.idiomatic: Yizong had hundreds of thousands of soldiers at his command, yet he fled at every enemy approach and let the rebellion spread unchecked.

sentences.zh: 又欲移罪於草澤詿誤之人，豈為臣之道！

translations.literal: Furthermore wishing to shift guilt onto grass-and-marsh people deceived and led astray—is this the way of a minister!
translations.idiomatic: Now he would shift blame onto innocent villagers who were misled—is that how an officer serves his sovereign?

sentences.zh: 臣請先斬懿宗，以謝河北。」

translations.literal: Your subject requests first beheading Yizong, to make apology to Hebei."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Yizong be executed first, as reparation to the people of Hebei."

sentences.zh: 懿宗不能答。

translations.literal: Yizong could not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Yizong had no answer.

sentences.zh: 則天遂寬脅從者之罪。

translations.literal: Empress Zetian thereupon relaxed the guilt of those coerced to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zetian then pardoned those who had been forced into collusion.

sentences.zh: 後都城三月雨雪，鳳閣侍郎蘇味道以為瑞雪，率群官表賀。

translations.literal: Later in the capital in the third month snow and rain fell; Vice Minister of Fengge Su Weidao regarded it as auspicious snow, leading the multitude of officials in a memorial of congratulation.
translations.idiomatic: Snow fell on the capital in the third month—a freak late-season storm. Fengge Vice Minister Su Weidao hailed it as an auspicious omen and led the court in offering congratulations.

sentences.zh: 求禮曰：「公為宰相，不能燮理陰陽，非時降雪，又將災而為瑞，誣罔視聽。

translations.literal: Qiuli said: "You serve as chief minister, yet cannot harmonize and govern yin and yang; untimely snowfall falling—you again transform calamity into auspiciousness, deceiving and deluding what eyes and ears receive.
translations.idiomatic: Qiuli said: "As chief minister you should harmonize Heaven and earth, yet untimely snow falls and you call disaster a blessing—you are deceiving the court and the people.

sentences.zh: 若以三月雪為瑞雪，即臘月雷亦為瑞雷耶？」

translations.literal: If taking third-month snow as auspicious snow, then twelfth-month thunder—is it also auspicious thunder?"
translations.idiomatic: If snow in March counts as a blessing, is thunder in the twelfth month a blessing too?"

sentences.zh: 味道不從。

translations.literal: Weidao did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Weidao paid him no heed.

sentences.zh: 求禮累遷左臺殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: Qiuli was repeatedly promoted to Left Platform palace attendant censor.
translations.idiomatic: Qiuli rose through the ranks to become a Left Censorate palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，為衛王掾，病卒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shenlong, he served as aide to the Prince of Wei; he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Shenlong reign he became an aide to the Prince of Wei and died in office.

sentences.zh: 燕欽融燕欽融，洛州偃師人也。

translations.literal: Yan Qinrong—Yan Qinrong was a man of Yanshi in Luozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Qinrong was a native of Yanshi in Luozhou.

sentences.zh: 景龍末，為許州司戶參軍。

translations.literal: At the end of Jinglong, he served as revenue section adjutant of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the late Jinglong era he was appointed revenue clerk of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 時韋庶人干預國政，盛封拜群從子弟。

translations.literal: At the time Consort Wei intervened in state affairs, lavishly enfeoffing and appointing the multitude of her collateral kin and younger relatives.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wei was meddling in affairs of state, showering titles and offices on her kinsmen.

sentences.zh: 又與悖逆庶人及駙馬都尉武延秀、中書令宗楚客等將圖危宗社。

translations.literal: Again together with the rebellious consort, and Cavalry Captain-in-Chief Wu Yanxiu, Secretariat Director Zong Chuke, and others, she was about to plot endangering the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: Together with the treacherous empress, Imperial Son-in-Law Wu Yanxiu, Chief Minister Zong Chuke, and others, she plotted to destroy the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 欽融連上奏其事，庶人大怒，勸中宗召欽融廷見，撲殺之。

translations.literal: Qinrong repeatedly submitted memorials reporting this matter; the consort was greatly angered, urging Zhongzong to summon Qinrong for a court audience and beat him to death.
translations.idiomatic: Qinrong memorialized the court repeatedly; the empress was furious and persuaded Zhongzong to summon him to the throne room and have him beaten to death on the spot.

sentences.zh: 宗楚客又私令執法者加刃，欽融因而致死。

translations.literal: Zong Chuke again privately ordered the law enforcers to add blades; Qinrong thereby died.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Chuke secretly ordered the guards to finish him with edged weapons, and Qinrong was killed.

sentences.zh: 睿宗即位，下制曰：「故許州司戶參軍燕欽融，先陳忠讜，頗列章奏，雖幹非其位，而進不顧身。

translations.literal: When Ruizong took the throne, he issued an edict saying: "The late Revenue Section Adjutant Yan Qinrong of Xuzhou, first offering loyal admonition, repeatedly submitted memorials; though overstepping his station, in advancing he did not consider his person.
