translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ruizong came to the throne, he issued an edict: "The late Yan Qinrong, revenue clerk of Xuzhou, spoke loyal truth to power, memorial after memorial. Though it was not his place, he risked everything to do it.

sentences.zh: 永言奄亡，誠所傷悼，方開諫路，宜慰窀穸。

translations.literal: Ever speaking of his sudden death, this is truly what wounds and grieves us; now opening the path of remonstrance, it is fitting to console his grave mound.
translations.idiomatic: His untimely death is deeply mourned; as we reopen the path of honest counsel, let us honor his tomb and bring his spirit peace.

sentences.zh: 可贈諫議大夫，仍令備禮改葬，特授一子官。」

translations.literal: He may be posthumously granted Remonstrance and Discussion Grand Master; still order full rites for reburial, and specially confer an office on one son."
translations.idiomatic: Grant him the posthumous title Remonstrance Grand Master, give him a proper reburial with full honors, and appoint one of his sons to office."

sentences.zh: 附 郎岌先是，定州人郎岌，亦備陳韋庶人及宗楚客將為逆亂之狀，中宗不納，而韋庶人勸杖殺之。

translations.literal: Appendix: Lang Ji. Earlier, Lang Ji of Dingzhou also fully described the situation of Consort Wei and Zong Chuke about to commit rebellion; Zhongzong did not accept it, and Consort Wei urged beating him to death with staves.
translations.idiomatic: Appendix: Lang Ji. Earlier, a man named Lang Ji from Dingzhou had also warned in detail of Empress Wei's and Zong Chuke's planned treason. Zhongzong ignored him, and the empress had him beaten to death.

sentences.zh: 睿宗即位，追贈諫議大夫。

translations.literal: When Ruizong took the throne, he was posthumously granted Remonstrance and Discussion Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: When Ruizong ascended the throne, Lang Ji too was posthumously named Remonstrance Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 安金藏安金藏，京兆長安人，初為太常工人。

translations.literal: An Jinzang—An Jinzang was a man of Chang'an in Jingzhao; initially he was a Court of Imperial Sacrifices artisan.
translations.idiomatic: An Jinzang was a native of Chang'an in the capital district and originally worked as an artisan in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 載初年，則天稱制，睿宗號為皇嗣。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zai, Empress Zetian assumed regency; Ruizong was titled heir apparent to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of her reign title Zai, Wu Zetian seized power and made Ruizong crown prince in name only.

sentences.zh: 少府監裴匪躬、內侍范雲仙並以私謁皇嗣腰斬。

translations.literal: Court of the Palace Supplies Supervisor Pei Feigong and inner attendant Fan Yunxian were both beheaded at the waist for paying private visits to the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Feigong, director of the Palace Supplies Office, and the inner attendant Fan Yunxian were both cut in half at the waist merely for visiting the crown prince privately.

sentences.zh: 自此公卿已下，並不得見之，唯金藏等工人得在左右。

translations.literal: From this the grand ministers and below all could not see him; only Jinzang and other artisans were permitted at his sides.
translations.idiomatic: From then on no senior official was allowed to see him—only Jinzang and fellow artisans could attend him.

sentences.zh: 或有誣告皇嗣潛有異謀者，則天令來俊臣窮鞫其狀。

translations.literal: When there were those who falsely accused the crown prince of secretly harboring divergent plots, Zetian ordered Lai Junchen to exhaustively interrogate the matter.
translations.idiomatic: When someone falsely accused the crown prince of plotting treason, Wu Zetian put Lai Junchen in charge of a full investigation.

sentences.zh: 左右不勝楚毒，皆欲自誣，唯金藏確然無辭，大呼謂俊臣曰：「公不信金藏之言，請剖心以明皇嗣不反。」

translations.literal: Those at his sides could not bear the torments; all wished to falsely incriminate themselves—only Jinzang steadfastly had no confession, loudly shouting to Junchen: "If you sir do not believe Jinzang's words, I ask to cut open my heart to make clear the crown prince does not rebel."
translations.idiomatic: The prince's attendants broke under torture and were ready to confess to anything, but Jinzang held firm. He shouted at Junchen: "If you will not believe me, I will cut open my chest to prove the crown prince is innocent!"

sentences.zh: 即引佩刀自剖其胸，五藏並出，流血被地，因氣絕而仆。

translations.literal: Immediately drawing his girdle knife he cut open his own chest; the five viscera all came out, blood covering the ground; he thereby ceased breath and fell prostrate.
translations.idiomatic: He drew his belt dagger, split open his chest, and his entrails spilled onto the floor. Blood pooled beneath him and he collapsed, apparently dead.

sentences.zh: 則天聞之，令輿入宮中，遣醫人卻內五藏，以桑白皮為線縫合，傅之藥。

translations.literal: Zetian heard of it, ordered he be carried in a litter into the palace, sent physicians to return the five viscera inside, using mulberry bark as thread to stitch closed, and applying medicine.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Zetian heard what had happened, she had him carried into the palace. Surgeons replaced his entrails, sewed him shut with mulberry-bark thread, and treated the wound.

sentences.zh: 經宿，金藏始甦。

translations.literal: After one night's passage, Jinzang first revived.
translations.idiomatic: After a night he came back to life.

sentences.zh: 則天親臨視之，嘆曰：「吾子不能自明，不如爾之忠也！」

translations.literal: Zetian personally came to view him, sighing and saying: "My son cannot clarify himself—as he is not equal to your loyalty!"
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zetian visited him in person and sighed: "My own son cannot prove his innocence as you have done with your loyalty!"

sentences.zh: 即令俊臣停推，睿宗由是免難。

translations.literal: Immediately ordered Junchen to stop the investigation; Ruizong thereby escaped calamity.
translations.idiomatic: She ordered Junchen to halt the inquiry, and Ruizong was spared.

sentences.zh: 金藏，神龍初喪母，寓葬於都南闕口之北，廬於墓側，躬造石墳石塔，晝夜不息。

translations.literal: Jinzang, at the beginning of Shenlong mourning his mother, provisionally buried her north of the Que Pass south of the capital, built a hut beside the tomb, and personally fashioned stone tomb and stone pagoda, day and night without ceasing.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Shenlong reign, after his mother's death, Jinzang buried her provisionally north of Que Pass south of the capital. He built a hut by the grave and worked day and night carving a stone tomb and pagoda with his own hands.

sentences.zh: 原上舊無水，忽有湧泉自出。

translations.literal: On the plain there had originally been no water; suddenly a gushing spring issued forth of itself.
translations.idiomatic: Though the hill had never had water before, a spring suddenly burst from the ground.

sentences.zh: 又有李樹盛冬開花，犬鹿相狎。

translations.literal: Again there were plum trees blooming in the height of winter; dogs and deer mutually intimate.
translations.idiomatic: Plum trees blossomed in deep winter, and dogs and deer mingled peacefully.

sentences.zh: 本道使盧懷慎上聞，敕旌表其門。

translations.literal: The circuit commissioner Lu Huaishen reported upward; an edict commended and inscribed his gate.
translations.idiomatic: Circuit commissioner Lu Huaishen reported these portents to the throne, and the emperor ordered an honorific plaque for Jinzang's household.

sentences.zh: 景雲中，累遷右武衛中郎將。

translations.literal: During Jingyun, he was repeatedly promoted to Right Martial Guard middle-ranking general.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jingyun era he rose to become a captain in the Right Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 玄宗即位，追思金藏忠節，下制褒美，擢拜右驍衛將軍，乃令史官編次其事。

translations.literal: When Xuanzong took the throne, recalling Jinzang's loyal integrity, he issued an edict praising him, promoted and appointed him Right Valiant Cavalry General, and ordered the historians to compile and arrange the account of this matter.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanzong came to the throne, he remembered Jinzang's loyalty, issued an edict of praise, promoted him to general of the Right Valiant Cavalry Guard, and ordered the historians to record his story.

sentences.zh: ，又特封代國公，仍於東嶽等諸碑鐫勒其名。

translations.literal: , again was specially enfeoffed as Duke of Dai, and still at Mount Tai and other steles his name was carved and inscribed.
translations.idiomatic: He was also specially made Duke of Dai, and his name was carved on steles at Mount Tai and elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 竟以壽終，贈兵部尚書。

translations.literal: In the end he ended by longevity; posthumously granted Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: He lived out his full span of years and died a natural death, and was posthumously made Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 李憕李憕，太原文水人。

translations.literal: Li Qi—Li Qi was a man of Wenshui in Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qi was a native of Wenshui in Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 父希倩，中宗神龍初，右臺監察御史。

translations.literal: His father Xiqian, at the beginning of Shenlong under Zhongzong, was a Right Platform supervising censor.
translations.idiomatic: His father Li Xiqian served as a censor of the Right Censorate in the early Shenlong reign of Emperor Zhongzong.

sentences.zh: 憕早聰敏，以明經舉，開元初為咸陽尉。

translations.literal: Qi was early bright and keen; through the Classicist examination he was recommended; at the beginning of Kaiyuan he served as magistrate of Xianyang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qi was precociously brilliant. He passed the Classicist examination and, at the start of the Kaiyuan era, became magistrate of Xianyang.

sentences.zh: 時張說自紫微令、燕國公出為相州刺史、河北按察使，有洺州劉行善相人，說問：「寮采後誰貴達？」

translations.literal: At the time Zhang Shuo, departing from Director of the Purple Pavilion and Duke of Yan, went out as prefect of Xiangzhou and Hebei investigation commissioner; there was Liu Xingshan of Mingzhou, a physiognomist; Shuo asked: "Among the staff and assistants, afterward who will be honored and reach eminence?"
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Shuo left his post as chief minister and Duke of Yan to become prefect of Xiangzhou and commissioner for Hebei, he consulted Liu Xingshan, a physiognomist from Mingzhou: "Which of my staff will rise to greatness?"

sentences.zh: 行乃稱憕及臨河尉鄭巖。

translations.literal: Xingshan then named Qi and Zheng Yan, magistrate of Linhe.
translations.idiomatic: Xingshan named Li Qi and Zheng Yan, magistrate of Linhe.

sentences.zh: 說乃以女妻巖，妹婿陰行真女妻於憕。

translations.literal: Shuo then gave his daughter as wife to Yan; his sister's son-in-law Yin Xingzhen's daughter he gave in marriage to Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shuo married his daughter to Zheng Yan and gave Yin Xingzhen's daughter to Li Qi.

sentences.zh: 及說為并州長史、天兵軍大使，引憕常在幕下。

translations.literal: When Shuo became governor-general of Bingzhou and grand ambassador of the Heavenly Army, he brought Qi and kept him constantly in his staff.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Shuo became military governor of Bingzhou and commander of the Heavenly Army, he kept Li Qi on his personal staff.

sentences.zh: 九年，入為相，憕又為長安尉。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, he entered to serve as chancellor; Qi again became magistrate of Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year Zhang Shuo returned to the capital as chancellor, and Li Qi was appointed magistrate of Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 屬宇文融為御史，括田戶，奏知名之士崔希逸、咸廙業、宇文順、於孺卿、李宙及悽為判官，攝監察御史，分路檢察，以課並遷監察御史。

translations.literal: When Yuwen Rong served as censor, registering field households, he memorialized recommending noted scholars Cui Xiyi, Xian Yiye, Yuwen Shun, Yu Ruqing, Li Zhou, and Qi as case officers, acting as supervising censors, inspecting by separate routes; through their evaluations all were transferred to supervising censors.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuwen Rong was made censor and ordered to register landholdings, he appointed distinguished officials including Cui Xiyi, Xian Yiye, Yuwen Shun, Yu Ruqing, Li Zhou, and Li Qi as case officers with acting status as supervising censors. They inspected the work in separate districts and, on the strength of their performance, all were promoted to full censor.

sentences.zh: 憕驟歷兵、吏部郎中，給事中。

translations.literal: Qi rapidly passed through Bureau of Military Affairs and Bureau of Personnel directors, and palace advisor.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qi rose quickly through posts as director in the Ministries of War and Personnel and finally as palace advisor.

sentences.zh: 憕有吏幹，明於幾案，甚有當官之稱。

translations.literal: Qi possessed administrative competence, clear in desk and case matters, greatly having a reputation for proper official conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qi was an able administrator with a sharp eye for paperwork and a reputation for integrity in office.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，為河南少尹。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year, he served as Vice Governor of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year of Kaiyuan he became vice governor of Henan.

sentences.zh: 時蕭炅為尹，依倚權貴，蒞事多不法。

translations.literal: At the time Xiao Jiong served as governor; relying on powerful and noble persons, in handling affairs there were many unlawful acts.
translations.idiomatic: The governor was Xiao Jiong, who relied on powerful patrons and ran his office with little regard for the law.

sentences.zh: 憕以公直正之，人用繫賴。

translations.literal: Qi with public uprightness corrected him; people thereby relied on and trusted.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qi corrected him with impartial firmness, and the people came to depend on him.

sentences.zh: 又道士孫甑生以左道求進，托以修功德，往來嵩山，求請無度，憕必挫之。

translations.literal: Again the Daoist Sun Zhensheng, seeking advancement through heterodox ways, entrusting himself to repairing meritorious works, coming and going to Mount Song, asking and requesting without limit—Qi always thwarted him.
translations.idiomatic: A Daoist named Sun Zhensheng sought influence through sorcery, using charitable projects as a pretext for endless requests at Mount Song. Li Qi blocked him at every turn.

sentences.zh: 炅及甑生患之，而構於朝廷。

translations.literal: Jiong and Zhensheng resented this, and framed accusations at court.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Jiong and Sun Zhensheng bore him a grudge and slandered him at court.

sentences.zh: 天寶初，出為清河太守。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao, he was sent out as prefect of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Tianbao era he was transferred out to serve as prefect of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 十一載，累轉河東太守、本道采訪。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, he was repeatedly transferred to prefect of Hedong and circuit investigating commissioner of his circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was promoted to prefect of Hedong and investigating commissioner for the circuit.

sentences.zh: 謁於行在所，改尚書右丞、京兆尹。

translations.literal: He had an audience at the traveling palace; changed to Right Vice Minister of the Secretariat and Governor of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: When he reported to the emperor at the traveling palace, he was made vice minister of the Secretariat and governor of the capital district.

sentences.zh: 十四載，轉光祿卿、東京留守，判尚書省事。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, transferred to Chamberlain for Attendants, Eastern Capital garrison commander, handling Secretariat matters.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he became chamberlain for attendants, commissioner for the Eastern Capital, and acting head of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 其載十一月，安祿山反於范陽，人心震懼。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of that year, An Lushan rebelled at Fanyang; people's hearts were shaken and fearful.
translations.idiomatic: That November An Lushan rose in rebellion at Fanyang, and panic swept the realm.

sentences.zh: 玄宗遣安西節度封常清兼御史大夫為將，召募於東京以禦之。

translations.literal: Xuanzong dispatched Anxi Military Commissioner Feng Changqing, concurrently Censor-in-Chief, as general, recruiting at the Eastern Capital to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong sent Feng Changqing, military governor of Anxi and concurrently censor-in-chief, to raise troops in Luoyang to meet the rebel advance.

sentences.zh: 憕與留臺御史中丞盧奕、河南尹達奚珣，綏輯將士，完繕城郭，遏其侵逼。

translations.literal: Qi together with Acting Censorate Vice Censor Lu Yi and Henan Governor Daxi Xun pacified and gathered soldiers and officers, completed and repaired city walls and defenses, and checked their invasion and pressure.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qi, together with the acting censor Lu Yi and Henan governor Daxi Xun, rallied the troops, repaired the fortifications, and held back the enemy's advance.

sentences.zh: 遷憕禮部尚書，依前留守。

translations.literal: Qi was transferred to Minister of Rites, continuing as before as garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qi was promoted to Minister of Rites while remaining commissioner of the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 自逆徒發范陽，至渡河，令嚴，覘候計絕。

translations.literal: From when the rebel band departed Fanyang until crossing the river, orders were strict and scouting plans were cut off.
translations.idiomatic: From the rebel departure at Fanyang until they crossed the Yellow River, their discipline was iron tight and intelligence reports dried up.

sentences.zh: 及渡河，陷陳留、滎陽二郡，殺張介然、崔無诐，數日間已至都城下。

translations.literal: When they crossed the river, they captured Chenliu and Xingyang two commanderies, killed Zhang Jieran and Cui Wubi, and within several days had already reached beneath the capital walls.
translations.idiomatic: Once across the river they seized Chenliu and Xingyang, killed the defenders Zhang Jieran and Cui Wubi, and within days were at the gates of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 祿山所統，皆蕃漢精兵，訓練已久；

translations.literal: Those under Lushan's command were all barbarian and Han elite troops, long trained;
translations.idiomatic: Lushan's army was made up of seasoned barbarian and Han veterans;

sentences.zh: 常清之眾，多市井之人，初不知戰。

translations.literal: Feng Changqing's multitude were mostly market-and-street people, at first not knowing battle.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Changqing's recruits were mostly townspeople who had never seen combat.

sentences.zh: 及兵交之後，被鐵騎唐突，飛矢如雨，皆魂懾色沮，望賊奔散。

translations.literal: When armies joined in battle afterward, struck by iron cavalry charging and breaking through, flying arrows like rain—all souls were fearful and faces downcast, seeing the bandits they fled and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: When battle was joined, armored cavalry bore down on them and arrows fell like rain. Terror drained the color from their faces and they fled at the sight of the enemy.

sentences.zh: 憕謂奕曰：「吾曹荷國重寄，誓無避死，雖力不敵，其若官守何！」

translations.literal: Qi said to Yi: "We bear the state's heavy trust; we swear not to avoid death; though strength does not match, what of our official charge!"
translations.idiomatic: Li Qi said to Lu Yi: "The state has entrusted us with grave responsibility. We have sworn not to flee from death. Even if we cannot prevail, how can we abandon our posts?"

sentences.zh: 奕亦便許願守本司。

translations.literal: Yi also promptly promised to wish to guard his own bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yi immediately vowed to hold his office to the end.

sentences.zh: 於是憕居留守宅，奕獨居臺中。

translations.literal: Thereupon Qi dwelt in the garrison commander's residence; Yi alone dwelt within the censorate.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qi stayed at the commissioner's residence while Lu Yi remained alone in the censorate headquarters.

sentences.zh: 及常清西奔，祿山領其眾，椎鼓大呼，以入都城，殺掠數千人，箭及宮闕。

translations.literal: When Feng Changqing fled west, Lushan led his multitude, beating drums and shouting loudly, to enter the capital; they killed and plundered several thousand people, arrows reaching the palace gates.
translations.idiomatic: When Feng Changqing fled westward, Lushan marched his army into the city with drums beating and battle cries. They slaughtered and plundered thousands, and arrows flew as far as the palace gates.

sentences.zh: 然後住居於閑廄中，令擒悽及奕、判官蔣清等三人，害之，以威於眾。

translations.literal: Then he halted and dwelt in the idle stables, ordering the capture of Qi, Yi, and case officer Jiang Qing—the three of them—harmed to awe the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: He established his headquarters in the abandoned stables and ordered Li Qi, Lu Yi, and the case officer Jiang Qing seized and executed as a warning to the populace.

sentences.zh: 祿山傳悽、奕、清三人之首，以徇河北。

translations.literal: Lushan sent the three men's heads—Qi, Yi, and Qing—to parade through Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan sent the heads of Li Qi, Lu Yi, and Jiang Qing through Hebei as a grim display.

sentences.zh: 信宿，至平原，太守顏真卿斬其使，浴其首，殮以木函，祭而瘞之，以聞。

translations.literal: After a night's lodging, arriving at Pingyuan, Prefect Yan Zhenqing beheaded their envoy, washed their heads, encoffined them in a wooden box, sacrificed and buried them, and reported upward.
translations.idiomatic: Two days later the procession reached Pingyuan, where Governor Yan Zhenqing executed the bearer, washed the heads, placed them in a wooden coffin, buried them with proper rites, and reported to the throne.

sentences.zh: 玄宗贈悽司徒，仍與一子五品官。

translations.literal: Xuanzong posthumously granted Qi Minister over the Masses, still bestowing a fifth-rank office on one son.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong posthumously made Li Qi Minister over the Masses and granted a fifth-rank office to one of his sons.

sentences.zh: 奕武部尚書，崔無诐工部尚書，各與一子官。

translations.literal: Yi Minister of War, Cui Wubi Minister of Works; each granted an office to one son.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yi was posthumously made Minister of War and Cui Wubi Minister of Works; each man's son was also granted an office.

sentences.zh: 蔣清文部郎中。

translations.literal: Jiang Qing Director of the Bureau of Documents.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Qing was posthumously made director in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 憕豐於產業，伊川膏腴，水陸上田，修竹茂樹，自城及闕口，別業相望，與吏部侍郎李彭年皆有地癖。

translations.literal: Qi was abundant in estates; in Yichuan fertile land, upland fields by water and land, cultivated bamboo and luxuriant trees—from the city to Que Pass, separate estates faced one another; together with Vice Minister of Personnel Li Pengnian both had a passion for land.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qi was enormously wealthy. His estates in Yichuan stretched along the Yi River—irrigated fields, bamboo groves, and thick woodland from the city to Que Pass, one villa facing another. He and Vice Minister Li Pengnian shared an obsession with land.

sentences.zh: 鄭巖，天寶中仕至絳郡太守，入為少府監，田產亞於憕。

translations.literal: Zheng Yan, during Tianbao served up to prefect of Jiang Commandery, entered as Court of Palace Supplies supervisor; field estates were second to Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yan rose during Tianbao to prefect of Jiang Commandery and later became director of the Palace Supplies Office; his holdings ranked second only to Li Qi's.

sentences.zh: 憕有子十餘人，二子為僧，與憕同遇害；

translations.literal: Qi had more than ten sons; two sons became monks, sharing with Qi the same encounter with harm;
translations.idiomatic: Li Qi had more than a dozen sons; two who had become monks died with him;

sentences.zh: 二子彭、源，存焉。

translations.literal: Two sons Peng and Yuan survived.
translations.idiomatic: two others, Peng and Yuan, survived.

sentences.zh: 子 源源，時年八歲，為賊所俘，轉徙流離，凡七八年。

translations.literal: Son: Yuan. Yuan, then eight years old, was captured by bandits, transferred and displaced in wandering exile, altogether seven or eight years.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuan was eight years old when the rebels captured him. He was passed from hand to hand in exile for seven or eight years.

sentences.zh: 及史朝義走河北，洛陽故吏有義源者，贖之於民家。

translations.literal: When Shi Chaoyi fled to Hebei, a former Luoyang official named Yiyuan ransomed him from a civilian household.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Chaoyi fled north to Hebei, a former Luoyang official named Yiyuan bought him back from the family that held him.

sentences.zh: 代宗聞之，授河南府參軍，轉司農寺主簿。

translations.literal: When Daizong heard of it, he appointed him Henan Prefecture adjutant, transferred to chief clerk of the Court of the National Granaries.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Daizong learned of this, he appointed Yuan adjutant of Henan prefecture and later chief clerk of the Court of the National Granaries.

sentences.zh: 以父死禍難，無心祿仕，誓不婚妻，不食酒肉。

translations.literal: Because his father died in calamity and disaster, he had no heart for salary and office; he vowed not to marry a wife, not to eat wine and meat.
translations.idiomatic: After his father's death in the rebellion he renounced official life, swore never to marry, and abstained from wine and meat.

sentences.zh: 洛陽之北惠林寺，憕之舊堅墅也，源乃依寺僧，寓居一室，依僧齋戒，人未嘗見其所習。

translations.literal: Huilin Temple north of Luoyang was Qi's old estate villa; Yuan then relied on the temple monks, lodged in one room, following monastic abstinence and precepts; people never saw what he practiced.
translations.idiomatic: North of Luoyang lay Huilin Temple, once site of Li Qi's country villa. Yuan took up residence with the monks in a single cell, living by their vegetarian rules. No one ever saw him pursue an ordinary livelihood.

sentences.zh: 先穴地為墓，預為終制，時時偃仰於穴中。

translations.literal: First he dug earth to make a tomb, preparing in advance his final arrangements; from time to time he reclined and arose within the tomb pit.
translations.idiomatic: He dug his own grave in advance and would lie down in it from time to time, as if rehearsing his death.

sentences.zh: ，御史中丞李德裕表薦之曰：「處士李源，即故禮部尚書、東都留守、贈司徒、忠烈公李憕之少子。

translations.literal: , Censorate Vice Censor Li Deyu memorialized recommending him, saying: "Recluse Li Yuan is the younger son of the late Minister of Rites, Eastern Capital garrison commander, posthumously granted Minister over the Masses, Loyal and Stern Duke Li Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Later, Vice Censor Li Deyu memorialized the throne in his favor: "The recluse Li Yuan is the youngest son of the late Li Qi, Minister of Rites and commissioner of the Eastern Capital, posthumously honored as Minister over the Masses and Loyal and Stern Duke.

sentences.zh: 天與忠孝，嗣茲貞烈。

translations.literal: Heaven granted loyalty and filial piety; he inherits this steadfast integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven endowed him with loyalty and filial devotion, and he inherits his father's steadfast virtue.

sentences.zh: 以父死國難，哀纏終身，自司農寺主簿，絕心祿仕，垂五十年。

translations.literal: Because his father died in national difficulty, grief wound through his whole life; from chief clerk of the Court of the National Granaries, he cut off his heart from salary and office, extending nearly fifty years.
translations.idiomatic: Since his father perished in the nation's crisis, grief has wrapped his life. He resigned his post as chief clerk of the Court of the National Granaries and has refused office for nearly fifty years.

sentences.zh: 暨於衰暮，多依惠林佛寺，本憕之墅也。

translations.literal: Reaching decrepit old age, he mostly relied on Huilin Buddhist temple—it was originally Qi's villa.
translations.idiomatic: In his old age he has lived chiefly at Huilin Temple, on what was once his father's estate.

sentences.zh: 寺之正殿，即悽之寢室，源過殿必趨，未嘗登踐。

translations.literal: The temple's main hall was precisely Qi's sleeping chamber; Yuan passing the hall always hastened, never once mounting and treading upon it.
translations.idiomatic: The temple's main hall was his father's former bedchamber. Yuan always hurried past it and never set foot inside.

sentences.zh: 隨僧一食，已五十年。

translations.literal: Following the monks in one meal, already fifty years.
translations.idiomatic: He has eaten one simple meal a day with the monks for fifty years.

sentences.zh: 其端心執孝，無有不至。

translations.literal: His upright heart holding filial piety—there was nothing to which he did not attain.
translations.idiomatic: His filial devotion has been absolute in every respect.

sentences.zh: 抱此貞節，棄於清朝，臣竊為陛下惜之。」

translations.literal: Embracing this steadfast integrity, abandoned in the clear court—I your subject privately grieve for Your Majesty over this."
translations.idiomatic: A man of such integrity languishes forgotten in Your Majesty's reign, and I grieve that the court should waste him."

sentences.zh: 詔曰：

translations.literal: An edict said:
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied:

sentences.zh: 《禮》著死綏，《傳》稱握節，捐生守位，取重人倫。

translations.literal: The "Rites" records dying while holding the reins; the "Traditions" praises grasping the tally; sacrificing life to guard one's post—this gives weight to human relations.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Rites commends dying at one's post; the Commentary praises holding fast to one's token of office. To give one's life guarding one's charge is the highest standard of human duty.

sentences.zh: 為義甚明，其風或替，言念於此，慨然興懷。

translations.literal: Acting for righteousness is very clear; that spirit at times has declined—speaking and reflecting on this, I am moved to heartfelt emotion.
translations.idiomatic: Righteous conduct once stood plainly before us, yet that spirit has faded; as I dwell on this, sorrow and resolve rise together within me.

sentences.zh: 而朝之公卿，有上言者，云天寶之季，盜起幽陵，振蕩生靈，噬吞河洛。

translations.literal: Yet among the court's dukes and ministers, some who submitted memorials said that at the end of the Tianbao era, bandits rose in Youling, shaking and agitating the living masses, devouring and swallowing the He and Luo regions.
translations.idiomatic: Court ministers have memorialized that in the closing years of Tianbao, rebellion erupted from the northeast, convulsing the realm and swallowing the heartland along the Yellow and Luo rivers.

sentences.zh: 贈司徒、忠烈公憕，處難居首，正色受屠，兩河聞風，再固危壁，首立殊節，到今稱之。

translations.literal: The posthumously appointed Situ, Duke of Loyalty and Martyrdom Ping—placed at the fore in facing hardship, with stern countenance accepting slaughter; the Two Rivers heard his example and twice strengthened perilous ramparts; he first established extraordinary integrity, and to this day he is praised.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumous Minister of Works Yan Ping, the Loyal and Martyr Duke, stood foremost in the crisis and met death with unflinching dignity; his example rallied the north, twice stiffened defenses on the brink of collapse, and won honor that endures to this day.

sentences.zh: 其子源，有曾、閔之行，可貫於神明；

translations.literal: His son Yuan had the conduct of Zeng and Min—it could pierce through to the spirits and gods.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuan displayed filial devotion worthy of Zengzi and Min Ziqian, devotion so pure it would move heaven itself.

sentences.zh: 有巢、由之風，可希於太古。

translations.literal: He had the air of Nest-dweller and Xu You—it could be hoped for in utmost antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: He carried the same withdrawn simplicity as the sage-recluses of primordial age, a way of life scarcely seen since the dawn of history.

sentences.zh: 山林以寄其跡，爵祿不入於心，泊然無營，五十餘載。

translations.literal: In mountains and forests he entrusted his footsteps; rank and stipend did not enter his heart—placid and without striving, for more than fifty years.
translations.idiomatic: He hid himself in the hills, untouched by titles or salary, living in quiet detachment for over fifty years.

sentences.zh: 夫褒忠可以勸臣節，旌孝可以激人倫，尚義可以警澆浮，敬老可以厚風俗。

translations.literal: Now, honoring loyalty can encourage ministers' integrity; commending filial piety can stir human relations; upholding righteousness can warn against shallow dissipation; respecting the aged can thicken customs.
translations.idiomatic: To reward loyalty steels officials in duty; to honor filial piety upholds the bonds of family; to exalt righteousness curbs frivolity; to respect the elderly deepens the character of society.

sentences.zh: 舉茲四者，大儆於時。

translations.literal: Raising up these four matters—a great admonition for the age.
translations.idiomatic: By advancing these four virtues, We set a commanding standard for Our times.

sentences.zh: 是用擢自衡門，立於文陛，處以諫職，冀聞讜言，仍加印紱，式示光寵。

translations.literal: Therefore We raise him from the humble gate, establish him on the patterned steps, place him in remonstrance office, hoping to hear straight counsel; We furthermore add seal and sash cord, thereby displaying bright favor.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore We summon him from obscurity to stand before the imperial throne, assign him a remonstrance post in hope of frank counsel, and grant him rank and insignia as visible token of Our grace.

sentences.zh: 可守左諫議大夫，賜緋魚袋。

translations.literal: He may serve as Left Remonstrance Censor Doctor, and be granted a scarlet fish pouch.
translations.idiomatic: Let him serve as Left Remonstrance Censor and be presented with the scarlet official pouch.

sentences.zh: 仍敕河南尹差官就所居敦諭遣發。

translations.literal: We furthermore command the Henan Intendant to dispatch officials to his dwelling to earnestly instruct and send him forth.
translations.idiomatic: The Henan governor is further ordered to send officials to his residence with urgent summons to take up his post.

sentences.zh: 穆宗尋令中使賫手詔、緋袍、牙笏、絹二百匹，往洛陽惠林寺宣賜。

translations.literal: Muzong soon ordered a palace envoy to carry the imperial handwritten edict, scarlet robe, ivory tablet, and two hundred bolts of silk, proceeding to Huilin Temple in Luoyang to proclaim and bestow them.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Muzong soon dispatched a palace messenger bearing an autograph decree, a scarlet robe, an ivory court tablet, and two hundred bolts of silk to Huilin Temple in Luoyang to invest him formally.

sentences.zh: 源受詔，對中使苦陳疾甚年高，不能趨拜，附表謝恩，其官告服色絹，皆辭不受。

translations.literal: Yuan received the edict and, facing the palace envoy, painfully declared that his illness was severe and his years advanced—he could not hasten to bow; he appended a memorial thanking the grace; the commission, robes, insignia, and silk—all he declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan received the decree but pleaded before the messenger that age and illness left him unable to perform court obeisance; in a written reply he thanked the emperor but refused the appointment, robes, insignia, and silk alike.

sentences.zh: 竟卒於寺。

translations.literal: In the end he died at the temple.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the temple shortly thereafter.

sentences.zh: 子 彭彭，以一子官累歷州縣令長。

translations.literal: His son Peng, by merit of one son's office, successively held posts as prefectural and county magistrate and chief.
translations.idiomatic: His son Peng rose through county and prefectural office by the privilege granted to the son of an honored man.

sentences.zh: 子宏，仕官愈卑。

translations.literal: His son Hong held office even lower.
translations.idiomatic: Another son, Hong, served in lesser posts still.

sentences.zh: 生三子：景讓、景莊、景溫，自元和後，相繼以進士登第。

translations.literal: He bore three sons: Jingrang, Jingzhuang, and Jingwen; from after the Yuanhe era they successively passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons—Jingrang, Jingzhuang, and Jingwen—each of whom earned the jinshi degree in succession after the Yuanhe reign.

sentences.zh: 彭孫 景讓景讓，太和中為尚書郎，出為商州刺史。

translations.literal: Peng's grandson Jingrang—Jingrang—in the Tahe era served as a Secretariat official; he went out as governor of Shangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Peng's grandson Jingrang served as a secretariat official in the Tahe era before being appointed governor of Shang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: ，入朝為中書舍人。

translations.literal: [He] entered court as Secretariat Drafting Official.
translations.idiomatic: He later returned to court as Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 二年十月，出為華州刺史、潼關防禦、鎮國軍使。

translations.literal: In the second year, tenth month, he went out as governor of Hua Prefecture, Defender of Tong Pass, and commissioner of Zhenguo Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the second year he was posted as governor of Huazhou, defender of Tong Pass, and commander of the Zhenguo army.

sentences.zh: 四年，入為禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he entered [court] as Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was recalled as Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 五年，選貢士李蔚，後至宰相；

translations.literal: In the fifth year he selected the presented scholar Li Wei, who later reached chancellor;
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he selected Li Wei in the examinations; Wei would later become chief minister.

sentences.zh: 楊知退為尚書。

translations.literal: Yang Zhituo became a Secretariat Director.
translations.idiomatic: He also selected Yang Zhituo, who rose to director of a ministry.

sentences.zh: 大中朝，為襄州刺史、山南道節度使，入為吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the Dazhong reign he served as governor of Xiang Prefecture and military commissioner of the Shannan Circuit; he entered court as Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: During the Dazhong era he served as governor of Xiangzhou and military commissioner of Shannan, then returned to court as Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 十一年，轉御史大夫。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was transferred to Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was promoted to Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 景讓有大志，事親以孝聞，正色立朝，言無避忌。

translations.literal: Jingrang had great aspiration; in serving parents he was known for filial piety; with stern countenance he stood at court, his words without avoidance or taboo.
translations.idiomatic: Jingrang was a man of high ambition, famed for filial devotion, who spoke at court with stern integrity and never flinched from the truth.

sentences.zh: 為大夫時，宣宗舅鄭光卒，詔贈司徒，罷朝三日。

translations.literal: When serving as Censor-in-Chief, the maternal uncle of Emperor Xuanzong, Zheng Guang, died; an edict posthumously granted him Situ rank and suspended court for three days.
translations.idiomatic: While censor-in-chief, he learned that the emperor's maternal uncle Zheng Guang had died and that the throne had ordered three days of court mourning and posthumous promotion to Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 景讓曰：「國舅雖親，朝典有素，無容過越。」

translations.literal: Jingrang said: "Though the imperial maternal uncle is kin, court statutes have long-standing rules—there is no allowance for exceeding them."
translations.idiomatic: Jingrang objected: "Kinship with the emperor's uncle does not justify bending established court precedent."

sentences.zh: 乃上言曰：

translations.literal: He then submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized the throne as follows:

sentences.zh: 鄭光是陛下親舅，外族之愛，誠軫聖心，況皇太后哀切之時，理合加等，而賜之粟帛，隆其第宅，自家刑國，允謂合宜。

translations.literal: Zheng Guang is Your Majesty's maternal uncle; love for maternal kin truly moves the sacred heart—moreover, at a time when the Empress Dowager's grief is acute, it is reasonable to add higher honors; granting grain and silks and elevating his residence—disciplining the family to teach the state—may truly be called fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Guang was indeed the emperor's uncle, and compassion for maternal kin naturally stirred Your Majesty's heart—especially amid the empress dowager's grief, enrichment with grain and silk and enlargement of his residence were appropriate expressions of family virtue taught to the realm.

sentences.zh: 今以輟朝之數，比於親王公主，則前例所無。

translations.literal: But now, comparing the number of days of suspended court to that for imperial princes and princesses—such precedent does not exist.
translations.idiomatic: Yet matching the court mourning period to that granted princes and princesses has no precedent.

sentences.zh: 縱有，亦不可施用。

translations.literal: Even if there were one, it still could not be applied.
translations.idiomatic: Even if one existed, it should not be invoked here.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why is this so?

sentences.zh: 先王制禮，所以防微。

translations.literal: The former kings instituted ritual in order to guard against the slight.
translations.idiomatic: The sages fashioned ritual precisely to check small excesses before they grow.

sentences.zh: 大凡人情，於外族則深，於宗屬則薄。

translations.literal: Generally speaking, in human feeling toward maternal kin one is deep, toward paternal clan one is thin.
translations.idiomatic: Human nature runs deep toward maternal kin and comparatively thin toward the paternal line.

sentences.zh: 所以先王制禮，割愛厚親，士庶猶然，況當萬乘！

translations.literal: Therefore the former kings instituted ritual—cutting love short to thicken closeness to paternal kin; commoners and officials are still thus—how much more when one holds the chariot of ten thousand!
translations.idiomatic: That is why ritual deliberately restrains affection for outsiders and strengthens bonds within the clan—a rule binding on commoners and nobles alike, and all the more on the sovereign.

sentences.zh: 親王公主，宗屬也；

translations.literal: Imperial princes and princesses are paternal clan members;
translations.idiomatic: Princes and princesses belong to the imperial clan—

sentences.zh: 舅氏，外族也。

translations.literal: Maternal uncles are maternal kin.
translations.idiomatic: a maternal uncle belongs to the outer kin.

sentences.zh: 今朝廷公卿以至庶人，據《開元禮》，外祖父母及親舅喪服，小功五月，若親伯叔親兄弟即服齊缞周年。

translations.literal: Now from court dukes and ministers down to commoners, according to the Kaiyuan Rites, mourning garb for maternal grandparents and maternal uncle is xiaogong for five months; for paternal uncles and full brothers one wears qicui for a full year.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Kaiyuan Rites, officials and subjects alike wear five months' mourning for maternal grandparents and uncles, but a full year for paternal uncles and brothers—

sentences.zh: 所以疏其外而密於內也。

translations.literal: Thereby making the outer sparse and the inner dense.
translations.idiomatic: ritual thus keeps distant kin at a remove and holds close those within the clan.

sentences.zh: 有天下者，尤不可使外戚強盛。

translations.literal: One who possesses all under Heaven must especially not allow maternal kin to grow powerful.
translations.idiomatic: A ruler above all must never permit consort kin to grow strong.

sentences.zh: 故西漢有呂氏之侈，幾滅劉氏；

translations.literal: Therefore in the Western Han there was the extravagance of the Lü clan, nearly extinguishing the Liu house;
translations.idiomatic: The Western Han nearly fell when the Lü clan grew overmighty;

sentences.zh: 國朝有則天之篡，殆革唐命。

translations.literal: Our dynasty had Wu Zetian's usurpation, nearly altering Tang's mandate.
translations.idiomatic: Our own dynasty trembled when Wu Zetian seized the throne.

sentences.zh: 皆非一朝一夕，其所由來漸也。

translations.literal: None arose in a single morning or evening—their origins came by gradual steps.
translations.idiomatic: Neither calamity sprang up overnight; both crept forward step by step.

sentences.zh: 今鄭光輟朝日數，與親王公主同，設使陛下速改詔命，輟朝一日或兩日，示其升降有差，恩禮無僭，使四方見陛下欽明之德，青史傳陛下制度之文，垂之百王，播之芳烈。

translations.literal: Now Zheng Guang's days of suspended court equal those for imperial princes and princesses; if Your Majesty would quickly amend the edict—suspending court one or two days—showing that grades of elevation and descent differ, favor and ritual without overstepping, so the four quarters see Your Majesty's reverent brilliance, blue history transmits Your Majesty's institutional writings, handing them down to a hundred kings, spreading fragrant renown.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty would now reduce court mourning to one or two days—making clear the proper gradation of honors—the realm would witness imperial wisdom, historians would record a model for ages to come, and Your Majesty's restraint would echo among the sage-kings.

sentences.zh: 臣愚不肖，謬竊恩私，實願陛下處於堯、舜之上，羲、軒之列，所以甘心鼎鑊，伏進危言！

translations.literal: Your subject is foolish and without talent, wrongly possessing private favor—truly wishing Your Majesty to stand above Yao and Shun, in the ranks of Xi and Xuan; therefore willingly accepting the cauldron and boiling oil, I bow and advance stern words!
translations.idiomatic: Your humble servant, undeserving of Your grace, dares urge that Your Majesty rank with Yao, Shun, and the sage-emperors of old—even at the risk of death for speaking so bluntly.

sentences.zh: 優詔報之，乃罷兩日。

translations.literal: A gracious edict replied to him; [court mourning] was then reduced to two days.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor answered with a gentle decree and reduced mourning to two days.

sentences.zh: 景讓復為吏部尚書，卒，謚曰孝。

translations.literal: Jingrang again became Minister of Personnel; he died, posthumous title "Filial."
translations.idiomatic: Jingrang later served again as Minister of Personnel until his death; he was posthumously titled "Filial."

sentences.zh: 景溫，登第後踐歷臺閣。

translations.literal: Jingwen, after passing the examination, tread through terrace and pavilion offices.
translations.idiomatic: Jingwen, after earning his degree, served through central government posts.

sentences.zh: 咸通中，自工部侍郎出為華州刺史、潼關防禦、鎮國軍使。

translations.literal: In the Xiantong era, from Vice Minister of Works he went out as governor of Hua Prefecture, Defender of Tong Pass, and commissioner of Zhenguo Army.
translations.idiomatic: During Xiantong he left his post as Vice Minister of Works to become governor of Huazhou, defender of Tong Pass, and commander of the Zhenguo army.

sentences.zh: 景莊，亦至達官。

translations.literal: Jingzhuang also reached eminent official rank.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhuang likewise rose to high office.

sentences.zh: 張介然張介然者，蒲州猗氏人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Jieran. Zhang Jieran was a native of Yishi in Pu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jieran was a native of Yishi County in Pu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 本名六朗。

translations.literal: His original name was Liulang.
translations.idiomatic: He had originally been named Liulang.

sentences.zh: 謹慎善籌算，為郡守在河、隴。

translations.literal: Careful and cautious, skilled at calculation; he served as prefectural administrator in the He and Long regions.
translations.idiomatic: Careful and adept at accounts, he served as a prefectural official in the He-Long frontier region.

sentences.zh: 及天寶中，王忠嗣、皇甫惟明、哥舒翰相次為節將，並委以營田支度等使。

translations.literal: When in the Tianbao era Wang Zhongsi, Huangfu Weiming, and Geshu Han succeeded one another as military commissioners, all entrusted him as Commissioner of Farm Colonies and Logistics, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianbao, as Wang Zhongsi, Huangfu Weiming, and Geshu Han served in succession as frontier commanders, each appointed him commissioner of military farms and supplies.

sentences.zh: 進位衛尉卿，仍兼行軍司馬，使如故。

translations.literal: He advanced to Inspector of the Court of Imperial Guards, still concurrently serving as army march chief of staff; his commissioner posts remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Inspector of the Guard and continued as army chief of staff while retaining his supply duties.

sentences.zh: 及加銀青光祿大夫，帶上柱國，因入奏稱旨，特加賜賫。

translations.literal: When he was additionally made Silver-Green Glory Grand Master and Bearer of Upper Pillar State, because on entering court to report he pleased the emperor, special additional gifts were granted.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Silver-Green Glory Grand Master with the rank of Upper Pillar State, he so pleased the emperor in audience that special rewards were added.

sentences.zh: 介然乘間奏曰：「臣今三品，合列棨戟。

translations.literal: Jieran seized an interval to memorialize: "Your subject is now third rank and should have halberds displayed.
translations.idiomatic: Jieran took the occasion to say, "As a third-rank official I am entitled to halberds at my gate.

sentences.zh: 若列於帝城，鄉里不知臣貴。

translations.literal: If they are displayed in the imperial capital, my hometown will not know of my eminence.
translations.idiomatic: If they stand in the capital, my home village will never see that I have risen.

sentences.zh: 臣，河東人也，請列戟於故鄉。」

translations.literal: Your subject is a man of Hedong; I request halberds displayed in my old hometown."
translations.idiomatic: I am a son of Hedong—let the halberds be posted in my native place."

sentences.zh: 玄宗曰：「所給可列故鄉，京城佇當別賜。」

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong said: "What is granted may be displayed in your hometown; for the capital, wait—we shall grant separately."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, "Place them in your hometown; a separate set will be provided for the capital.

sentences.zh: 介然拜謝而出，仍賜絹五百匹，令宴集閭里，以寵異之。

translations.literal: Jieran bowed in thanks and withdrew; he was still granted five hundred bolts of silk and ordered to hold a feast gathering in the hamlet, thereby showing special favor.
translations.idiomatic: Jieran thanked him and withdrew, receiving five hundred bolts of silk and orders to feast his neighbors—a mark of extraordinary honor.

sentences.zh: 本鄉列戟，自介然始也。

translations.literal: Displayed halberds in one's hometown began with Jieran.
translations.idiomatic: The custom of displaying honor halberds in one's native village began with Jieran.

sentences.zh: 哥舒翰追在西京，薦為少府監。

translations.literal: Geshu Han, pursuing [the rebels] in the Western Capital, recommended him as Director of the Palace Buildings Office.
translations.idiomatic: When Geshu Han fell back to Chang'an, he recommended Jieran for director of palace works.

sentences.zh: 安祿山將犯河洛，以介然為河南防禦使，令守陳留。

translations.literal: When An Lushan was about to invade the He and Luo regions, [the court] made Jieran Henan Defense Commissioner and ordered him to hold Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: As An Lushan moved against the Yellow and Luo heartland, Jieran was made Henan defense commissioner and charged with holding Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 陳留水陸所湊，邑居萬家，而素不習戰。

translations.literal: Chenliu was where waterways and roads converged; the settlement held ten thousand households, yet was never accustomed to warfare.
translations.idiomatic: Chenliu stood at a hub of land and river traffic with ten thousand households, but its people were unused to war.

sentences.zh: 介然至任數日，賊已渡河。

translations.literal: Within days of Jieran's arrival, the rebels had already crossed the river.
translations.idiomatic: Jieran had barely taken office when the rebels crossed the river.

sentences.zh: 雖率兵登城，兼守要害，虜騎十萬，所過殺戮，煙塵亙天，彌漫數十里。

translations.literal: Though he led troops up the walls and also guarded strategic points, the barbarian cavalry numbered one hundred thousand; wherever they passed slaughter followed; smoke and dust filled the sky, spreading for several tens of li.
translations.idiomatic: He rallied the garrison and held the key positions, but a hundred thousand rebel horsemen swept past in a tide of slaughter, dust blotting the sky for miles on end.

sentences.zh: 介然之眾，聞吹角鼓噪之聲，授甲不得，氣已奪矣，故至覆敗。

translations.literal: Jieran's forces, hearing the sound of horns blowing and drums roaring, could not even don armor before their spirit was already seized—thus they met total defeat.
translations.idiomatic: His men never even finished arming themselves before the rebel horns and drums broke their nerve, and the defense collapsed.

sentences.zh: 初，玄宗以祿山起逆，於河南要路懸榜以購其首，又諭已殺其子慶宗等。

translations.literal: Initially, because Lushan had risen in rebellion, Xuanzong posted placards on key roads in Henan offering a reward for his head, and also announced that his son Qingzong and others had already been executed.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the rebellion the emperor had posted rewards for An Lushan's head along the Henan roadways and proclaimed the execution of his son Qingzong and others.

sentences.zh: 祿山入陳留北郭，安慶緒見榜，白於祿山。

translations.literal: Lushan entered the north suburb of Chenliu; An Qingxu saw the placard and reported it to Lushan.
translations.idiomatic: When Lushan entered the northern outskirts of Chenliu, his son Qingxu saw the reward proclamation and told him.

sentences.zh: 祿山於輿中兩手撫胸，大哭數聲，曰：「我有何罪，已殺我兒？」

translations.literal: Lushan, from within his carriage, placed both hands on his chest and wailed several times, saying: "What crime have I committed, that they have already killed my son?"
translations.idiomatic: Lushan clutched his chest in his carriage and wailed, "What have I done that they should kill my son?"

sentences.zh: 便縱兇毒。

translations.literal: He then unleashed savage poison.
translations.idiomatic: Then he gave free rein to his cruelty.

sentences.zh: 前有陳留兵將降者向萬人，行列於路，祿山命其牙將殺戮皆盡，流血如川。

translations.literal: Ahead were nearly ten thousand Chenliu soldiers and officers who had surrendered, arrayed in ranks along the road; Lushan ordered his bodyguard generals to slaughter them all—blood flowed like a river.
translations.idiomatic: Some ten thousand Chenliu troops who had surrendered stood lined along the road; Lushan ordered his officers to cut them down until blood ran like a stream.

sentences.zh: 乃斬介然於軍門，祿山氣乃稍解。

translations.literal: He then beheaded Jieran at the army gate; Lushan's rage only then slightly eased.
translations.idiomatic: He then executed Jieran before the army gate, and only then did his fury subside a little.

sentences.zh: 頓軍於陳留郭下，以其將李庭望為節度鎮之。

translations.literal: He encamped the army below the walls of Chenliu and appointed his general Li Tingwang as military commissioner to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: He halted his army outside Chenliu and left the general Li Tingwang to hold the city.

sentences.zh: 十五載，玄宗贈介然工部尚書，與一子五品官。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Tianbao, Xuanzong posthumously granted Jieran Vice Minister of Works and a fifth-rank office to one son.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao fifteen Xuanzong posthumously made him Vice Minister of Works and granted a fifth-rank post to one of his sons.

sentences.zh: 崔無詖崔無詖者，京兆長安人也。

translations.literal: Cui Wubi. Cui Wubi was a native of Chang'an in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Wubi was a native of Chang'an in the capital district.

sentences.zh: 本博陵舊族。

translations.literal: Originally of the old Boling clan.
translations.idiomatic: He came from the ancient Boling Cui lineage.

sentences.zh: 父從禮，中宗韋庶人之舅，景龍中衛尉卿。

translations.literal: His father Congli was maternal uncle to Empress Wei the commoner of Emperor Zhongzong; in the Jinglong era he was Inspector of the Court of Imperial Guards.
translations.idiomatic: His father Congli, maternal uncle to Empress Wei during Zhongzong's reign, had served as Inspector of the Guard in the Jinglong era.

sentences.zh: 時中書令、酂國公蕭至忠才位素高，甚承恩顧，敕亡先女冥婚韋庶人亡弟。

translations.literal: At the time Chief Minister and Duke of Zan of Xiao Zhizhong's talent and rank had long been high, and he received much imperial favor; an edict ordered the posthumous marriage of Zhizhong's deceased daughter to the deceased younger brother of Empress Wei the commoner.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Xiao Zhizhong then enjoyed great favor at court, and the emperor ordered a posthumous marriage between Zhizhong's deceased daughter and Empress Wei's deceased brother.

sentences.zh: 無詖婚至忠女，後為女家，中宗為兒家，供擬甚厚，時人為之語曰：「皇后嫁女，天子娶婦。」

translations.literal: Wubi married Zhizhong's daughter; afterward serving as the bride's family, Zhongzong serving as the groom's family—the provisions were very lavish; people of the time made a saying: "The empress marries off her daughter; the Son of Heaven takes a bride."
translations.idiomatic: Wubi married Zhizhong's daughter in a spectacle so lavish—the bride's side funded by Zhizhong, the groom's side by the emperor—that people jested, "The empress gives away a daughter while the Son of Heaven takes a bride."

sentences.zh: 及韋庶人敗，至忠女亦死，無詖坐累久貶在外。

translations.literal: When Empress Wei the commoner fell, Zhizhong's daughter also died; Wubi, implicated by association, was long demoted and sent away.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wei fell, Zhizhong's daughter died as well, and Wubi, caught in the disgrace, spent years in exile.

sentences.zh: 開元中，為益州司馬。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan era he served as Vice Administrator of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: During Kaiyuan he served as vice administrator of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 會楊國忠為新都尉，與之歡甚，國忠因事引用之，累轉陜郡太守、少府監、滎陽郡太守。

translations.literal: It happened that Yang Guozhong was magistrate of Xindu and became very friendly with him; Guozhong, seizing an opportunity, recommended him; he successively transferred to governor of Shaan Commandery, Director of the Palace Buildings Office, and governor of Xingyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: There he befriended Yang Guozhong, then magistrate of Xindu, who later advanced him through posts as governor of Shaan, director of palace works, and governor of Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 安祿山率眾南向，無詖召募拒之。

translations.literal: When An Lushan led his armies southward, Wubi recruited troops to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan marched south, Wubi raised troops to resist.

sentences.zh: 及賊陷陳留郡後，兇威轉盛，戈矛鼓角，驚駭城邑，兩宿及滎陽。

translations.literal: After the rebels captured Chenliu Commandery, their savage power turned stronger; spears and halberds, drums and horns alarmed and terrified the walled cities—they reached Xingyang in two nights.
translations.idiomatic: After Chenliu fell the rebels grew bolder still; spears, drums, and war horns terrified every town they passed, and within two nights they stood before Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 乘城自墜如雨，故無詖及官吏，盡為賊所虜。

translations.literal: Those ascending the walls fell of themselves like rain; therefore Wubi and the officials were all taken captive by the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Defenders fell from the walls in droves, and Wubi with his officials were all captured.

sentences.zh: 賊以其將武令珣鎮之。

translations.literal: The rebels appointed their general Wu Lingxun to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels left the general Wu Lingxun to hold the city.

sentences.zh: 盧奕盧奕，黃門監懷慎之少子也。

translations.literal: Lu Yi. Lu Yi was the youngest son of Yellow Gate Supervisor Huaishen.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yi was the youngest son of Vice Director Lu Huaishen.

sentences.zh: 與其兄奐齊名。

translations.literal: With his elder brother Huan he shared equal fame.
translations.idiomatic: He was as renowned as his elder brother Huan.

sentences.zh: 大腹豐下，眉目疏朗。

translations.literal: Great belly, full lower body; eyebrows and eyes sparse and clear.
translations.idiomatic: He was broad of belly and handsome of feature, with open, composed countenance.

sentences.zh: 謹願寡欲，不尚輿馬，克己自勵。

translations.literal: Careful and sincere, few desires; he did not esteem carriages and horses; restraining himself he self-exhorted.
translations.idiomatic: Restrained and frugal, he scorned fine carriages and disciplined himself rigorously.

sentences.zh: 開元中，任京兆司錄參軍。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan era he served as Recorder of the Jingzhao metropolitan administration.
translations.idiomatic: During Kaiyuan he served as recorder in the capital administration.

sentences.zh: 天寶初，為鄠縣令、兵部郎中。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao he served as magistrate of Hu County and director in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the opening years of Tianbao he held the magistracy of Hu County and a directorship in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 所歷有聲，皆如奐之所治也。

translations.literal: Every post he held gained renown—all like what Huan had governed.
translations.idiomatic: Every post he held won praise equal to his brother's record.

sentences.zh: ，轉給事中。

translations.literal: [He] was transferred to Supervising Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 十一載，為御史中丞。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he became Assistant Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he became vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 始懷慎及奐並為中丞，父子三繼，清節不易，時人美之。

translations.literal: From the beginning Huaishen and Huan both served as censor-in-chief; father and sons three in succession—integrity unchanged; people of the time praised this.
translations.idiomatic: Since his father Huaishen and brother Huan had both held the censorate, three generations in succession upheld the same spotless integrity—a virtue widely admired.

sentences.zh: 奕留臺東都，又分知東都武部選事。

translations.literal: Yi remained at the eastern capital office; he additionally shared in managing eastern-capital personnel selection in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: Yi remained at the eastern capital and also shared responsibility for military appointments at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 十四載，安祿山犯東都，人吏奔散；

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, An Lushan attacked the eastern capital; officials and commoners fled and scattered;
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of the reign, An Lushan struck the eastern capital and officials and people scattered in flight;

sentences.zh: 奕在臺獨居，為賊所執，與李憕同見害。

translations.literal: Yi alone remained at the office; he was seized by bandits and met harm together with Li Ming.
translations.idiomatic: Yi alone stayed at his post; the rebels seized him, and he was killed along with Li Ming.

sentences.zh: 玄宗聞而湣之，贈兵部尚書。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong heard and pitied him, posthumously awarding him Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanzong heard, he mourned him and posthumously appointed him Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 太常議謚，博士獨孤及議曰：

translations.literal: The Directorate of Ceremonials deliberated on posthumous titles; Erudite Du Guji proposed, saying:
translations.idiomatic: When the Directorate of Ceremonials debated his posthumous name, Erudite Du Guji argued as follows:

sentences.zh: 盧奕剛毅樸忠，直方而清，勵精吏事，所居可紀。

translations.literal: Lu Yi was resolute and plain in loyalty, upright and square yet pure, exerting spirit in clerical affairs; what he held in office is worth recording.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yi was stern and steadfast, plainspoken and loyal, upright and incorruptible; he threw himself into his duties, and his tenure in office deserves to be remembered.

sentences.zh: ，洛陽陷沒。

translations.literal: , Luoyang fell and was lost.
translations.idiomatic: When Luoyang fell to the rebels,

sentences.zh: 於時東京人士，狼狽鹿駭，猛虎磨牙而爭其肉，居位者皆欲保命而全妻子。

translations.literal: At that time the people of the eastern capital were in wolfish disorder and deerlike fright; tigers bared fangs disputing their flesh—all in office wished to preserve life and save wives and children.
translations.idiomatic: The people of the eastern capital were thrown into panic; like tigers snarling over prey, everyone in authority sought only to save his own skin and protect his family.

sentences.zh: 或先策高足，爭脫羿彀；

translations.literal: Some first mounted high feet, struggling to escape Yi's bowstring;
translations.idiomatic: Some fled on swift horses, desperate to escape the bow;

sentences.zh: 或不恥茍活，甘飲盜泉。

translations.literal: Some were not ashamed of base survival, willingly drinking robber's spring.
translations.idiomatic: Others, unashamed to cling to life at any price, were ready to drink from a thief's well.

sentences.zh: 奕獨正身守位義不去，以死全節誓不辱。

translations.literal: Yi alone upright body guarded position, righteousness would not leave; by death to complete integrity he vowed not to be shamed.
translations.idiomatic: Only Yi held his post with unbending dignity, refusing to flee; he chose death to preserve his honor and swore never to suffer disgrace.

sentences.zh: 勢窘力屈，以朝服就執，猶慷慨感憤，數賊梟獍之罪。

translations.literal: Situation trapped strength exhausted, in court robes he submitted to seizure; still expansive and stirred with indignation, he enumerated the bandits' owl-beast crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Though cornered and helpless, he went to his capture still in full court dress; undaunted, he denounced the rebels' monstrous crimes with passionate fury.

sentences.zh: 觀者股栗，奕不變其色，而北面辭君，然後受害。

translations.literal: Watchers' thighs trembled; Yi did not change his countenance, yet turned north to take leave of the ruler, and only then met harm.
translations.idiomatic: Those who looked on trembled in terror, but Yi's face never changed; he bowed toward the north in farewell to his sovereign and only then suffered death.

sentences.zh: 雖古烈士，方之者鮮矣！

translations.literal: Even ancient martyrs—for comparison there are few!
translations.idiomatic: Even among heroes of antiquity, few can stand comparison with him!

sentences.zh: 或曰：「洛陽之存亡，操兵者實任其咎，非執法吏所能抗。

translations.literal: Some said: "The survival or fall of Luoyang—those wielding arms truly bear the blame; it is not what law-enforcing clerks can resist.
translations.idiomatic: Some argued: "Whether Luoyang stood or fell rested on the soldiers; a civil official could hardly have made a difference.

sentences.zh: 師敗將奔，去之可也。

translations.literal: Army defeated generals flee—leaving is acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: When the army is beaten and the generals run, it is only natural to flee.

sentences.zh: 委身寇仇，以死誰懟？」

translations.literal: Surrendering the body to bandit foes—by death who is confronted?"
translations.idiomatic: To throw yourself into the enemy's hands—what good does dying serve?

sentences.zh: 及以為不然。

translations.literal: Du Guji considered this not so.
translations.idiomatic: Du Guji rejected this view.

sentences.zh: 勇者禦而忠者守，必社稷是衛，則死生以之。

translations.literal: The brave resist and the loyal guard; they must shield the altars of state—then life and death follow accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: The courageous fight; the loyal hold their ground; when the realm itself is at stake, they accept whatever death or life may bring.

sentences.zh: 危而去之，是智免也，於忠何有？

translations.literal: In peril yet leaving—it is wisdom's escape; where is loyalty in it?
translations.idiomatic: To flee at the first sign of danger is merely clever self-preservation—what has that to do with loyalty?

sentences.zh: 昔荀息殺身於晉，不食其言也；

translations.literal: Formerly Xun Xi killed himself at Jin, not eating his word;
translations.idiomatic: Long ago Xun Xi gave his life at Jin rather than break his pledge;

sentences.zh: 仲由結纓於衛，食焉不避其難也；

translations.literal: Zhong You tied his cap-cord at Wei, having eaten there not avoiding its hardship;
translations.idiomatic: Zhong You bound his cap-strings at Wei, refusing to abandon the lord who had fed him even in peril;

sentences.zh: 玄冥勤其官而水死，守位而忘軀也；

translations.literal: Xuan Ming diligently held his office and died in water, guarding post and forgetting his body;
translations.idiomatic: Xuan Ming died in floodwaters while dutifully performing his office, holding his station and giving no thought to himself;

sentences.zh: 伯姬待保姆而火死，先禮而後身也。

translations.literal: Bo Ji waited for the nurse and died in fire, putting ritual first and body after.
translations.idiomatic: Bo Ji perished in the flames because she would not leave before her nurse—a woman who put duty before her own life.

sentences.zh: 彼四人者，死之日，皆於事無補，夫豈愛死而賈禍也！

translations.literal: Those four men—on the day of their death all added nothing to the affairs; how could they have loved death and courted disaster!
translations.idiomatic: None of those four, on the day they died, changed the outcome of events—yet who would say they courted death for its own sake!

sentences.zh: 以為死輕於義，故蹈義而捐生。

translations.literal: They considered death lighter than righteousness, therefore treading righteousness and abandoning life.
translations.idiomatic: They held their lives cheap beside righteousness, and so walked the path of duty even unto death.

sentences.zh: 古史書之，使事君者勸。

translations.literal: Ancient histories recorded them, to encourage those who serve rulers.
translations.idiomatic: The historians of old recorded their deeds to inspire loyalty in those who serve their sovereign.

sentences.zh: 然則祿山之亂，大於裏克、孔悝；

translations.literal: Thus then An Lushan's rebellion was greater than Li Ke and Kong Kui;
translations.idiomatic: An Lushan's rebellion was a crisis far beyond those faced by Li Ke or Kong Kui;

sentences.zh: 奕廉察之任，切於玄冥之官。

translations.literal: Yi's duty of integrity and investigation was urgent compared to Xuan Ming's office.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yi's charge as censor bore directly on the realm's welfare—no less pressing than Xuan Ming's post.

sentences.zh: 分命所繫，不啻於保姆；

translations.literal: The charge entrusted to him was not less than a nurse;
translations.idiomatic: The trust placed in him was every bit as solemn as the charge of a royal attendant;

sentences.zh: 逆黨兵威，甚於水火。

translations.literal: The rebel faction's military might exceeded water and fire.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels' army was a devastation worse than flood or flame.

sentences.zh: 於斯時也，能與執干戈者同其戮力，挽之不來，推之不去，豈不以師可虧，免不可茍，身可殺，節不可奪。

translations.literal: In such a time, able to with those bearing spears and halberds share their strength; pulled yet not coming, pushed yet not leaving—is it not because the army may be diminished, escape cannot be base, the body may be killed, integrity cannot be seized?
translations.idiomatic: At such a moment he strove alongside those who bore arms—could not be pulled away or driven off—for he held that armies may fail but honor cannot be surrendered, life may be taken but integrity cannot be stolen.

sentences.zh: 故全其特操於白刃之下，孰與夫懷安偷生者同其風哉！

translations.literal: Therefore completing his singular integrity beneath white blades—who shares the same air as those cherishing comfort and stealing life!
translations.idiomatic: To preserve one's character unsullied under the naked sword—how could such a man breathe the same air as those who clung to comfort and chose a coward's survival!

sentences.zh: 謹按謚法，圖國忘身曰「貞」，秉德遵業曰「烈」。

translations.literal: Respectfully examining posthumous-title regulations: plotting for the state and forgetting the body is called "Upright"; holding virtue and following the enterprise is called "Ardent."
translations.idiomatic: According to the rules for posthumous names, one who devotes himself to the state at the cost of his life receives "Zhen" (Upright); one who upholds virtue and honors his forebears receives "Lie" (Ardent).

sentences.zh: 奕執憲戎馬之間，志籓王室，可謂圖國；

translations.literal: Yi executed law amid war-horses, his will to shield the royal house—this may be called plotting for the state;
translations.idiomatic: Yi upheld the law even in the thick of battle, his heart set on protecting the throne—surely this is devotion to the realm;

sentences.zh: 國危不能拯，而繼之以死，可謂忘身；

translations.literal: The state in peril he could not rescue, yet following with death—this may be called forgetting the body;
translations.idiomatic: He could not save the realm in its hour of peril but followed with his life—this is selflessness unto death;

sentences.zh: 歷官一十任，言必正，事必果，而清節不撓，去之若始至，可謂秉德；

translations.literal: Through ten appointments in office, speech always upright, affairs always decisive, pure integrity unbent, leaving as if just arrived—this may be called holding virtue;
translations.idiomatic: Over ten official postings his word was always honest, his actions resolute, his integrity unbroken from first day to last—this is steadfast virtue;

sentences.zh: 先黃門以直道佐時，奕嗣之以忠純，可謂遵業。

translations.literal: Formerly the Yellow Gate with upright path assisted the age; Yi succeeded with loyal purity—this may be called following the enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: His father served at court with uncompromising integrity; Yi inherited that legacy in loyal purity—this is honoring one's ancestral charge.

sentences.zh: 請謚曰「貞烈」。

translations.literal: I request the posthumous title "Upright-Ardent."
translations.idiomatic: I therefore propose the posthumous name Zhenlie ("Steadfast and Ardent").

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: They followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was accepted.

sentences.zh: 蔣清蔣清者，故吏部侍郎欽緒之子。

translations.literal: Jiang Qing—Jiang Qing was the son of the former Vice Minister of Personnel Qinxu.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Qing was the son of the former Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, Jiang Qinxu.

sentences.zh: 舉明經，調補太子校書郎、鞏縣丞，盧奕留之憲府。

translations.literal: He passed the Mingjing examination; was assigned as Palace Proofreader and Gong county assistant—Lu Yi retained him at the censorate.
translations.idiomatic: Having passed the Mingjing examination, he was appointed Palace Proofreader and assistant magistrate of Gong County; Lu Yi kept him on at the censorate.

sentences.zh: 清與諸兄溢、演、沇，知名於時。

translations.literal: Qing together with his elder brothers Yi, Yan, and Yuan were renowned in the age.
translations.idiomatic: Qing and his elder brothers Yi, Yan, and Yuan were all celebrated men of their day.

sentences.zh: 奕之被害，清亦死焉。

translations.literal: When Yi met harm, Qing also died there.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Yi was killed, Qing died with him.

sentences.zh: 顏杲卿顏杲卿，瑯邪臨沂人。

translations.literal: Yan Gaoqing—Yan Gaoqing was a man of Langye Linyi.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Gaoqing, a native of Linyi in Langye commandery.

sentences.zh: 世仕江左。

translations.literal: His family for generations served the lands south of the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: His clan had served for generations in the south.

sentences.zh: 五代祖之推，北齊黃門侍郎、修文館學士。

translations.literal: His fifth-generation ancestor Zhitui was Northern Qi Vice Censor-in-Chief and Academician of the Hall of Cultivated Letters.
translations.idiomatic: His fifth-generation ancestor Yan Zhitui had been Vice Censor-in-Chief under Northern Qi and a scholar of the Hall of Cultivated Letters.

sentences.zh: 齊亡入周，始家關內，遂為長安人焉。

translations.literal: When Qi perished they entered Zhou; first established household within the Passes, thus became people of Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: When Northern Qi fell they entered Zhou territory, settled within the Passes, and became residents of Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 曾伯祖師古，貞觀中秘書監，自有傳。

translations.literal: His great-great-uncle Shigu in the Zhenguan era was Director of the Secretariat; he has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His great-great-uncle Yan Shigu served as Director of the Secretariat under Emperor Taizong and has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 曾祖勤禮，崇文館學士。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Qinli was a Chongwen Hall academician.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Yan Qinli was an academician of the Hall of Splendid Culture.

sentences.zh: 祖甫，曹王侍讀。

translations.literal: His grandfather Fu was tutor to the Prince of Cao.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yan Fu served as tutor to the Prince of Cao.

sentences.zh: 父元孫，垂拱初登進士第，考功員外郎劉奇榜其詞策，文瑰俊拔，多士聳觀。

translations.literal: His father Yuansun in the early Chuigong era passed the jinshi examination; Examination Section Vice Director Liu Qi placed his literary policy at the head; the writing was rare and outstanding, many scholars raised eyes to view.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yan Yuansun passed the jinshi examination in the early Chuigong period; Liu Qi of the Examination Section ranked his policy essay first—a work of such brilliance that the entire cohort looked on in awe.

sentences.zh: 歷官長安尉、太子舍人、亳州刺史卒。

translations.literal: He passed through offices as Chang'an magistrate, Palace Attendant, and died as prefect of Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served as magistrate of Chang'an and Palace Attendant, and died while prefect of Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 杲卿以廕受官，性剛直，有吏幹。

translations.literal: Gaoqing received office through yin privilege; his nature was rigid and straight, with administrative competence.
translations.idiomatic: Gaoqing entered office through hereditary privilege; stern and upright by nature, he possessed genuine talent for administration.

sentences.zh: 開元中，為魏州錄事參軍，振舉綱目，政稱第一。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan era he was Wei prefecture administrative assistant; he raised and established statutes and measures, governance ranked first.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaiyuan reign he served as administrative assistant of Wei Prefecture; he strengthened every line of governance until his district ranked first in the realm.

sentences.zh: ，攝常山太守。

translations.literal: , acting Changshan prefect.
translations.idiomatic: and was appointed acting governor of Changshan.

sentences.zh: 時安祿山為河北、河東采訪使，常山在其部內。

translations.literal: At the time An Lushan was commissioner of Hebei and Hedong; Changshan lay within his jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: An Lushan was then regional commissioner of Hebei and Hedong, and Changshan fell within his territory.

sentences.zh: 其年十一月，祿山舉范陽之兵詣闕。

translations.literal: That year in the eleventh month, Lushan raised the armies of Fanyang toward the capital.
translations.idiomatic: That November Lushan marched the armies of Fanyang against the capital.

sentences.zh: 十二月十二日，陷東都。

translations.literal: On the twelfth day of the twelfth month, the eastern capital fell.
translations.idiomatic: On the twelfth of the twelfth month the eastern capital fell.

sentences.zh: 杲卿忠誠感發，懼賊遂寇潼關，即危宗社。

translations.literal: Gaoqing loyal and sincere stirred forth, fearing the bandits would then invade Tong Pass and immediately endanger the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: Stirred by loyalty, Gaoqing feared the rebels would press on to Tong Pass and threaten the dynasty itself.

sentences.zh: 時從弟真卿為平原太守，初聞祿山逆謀，陰養死士，招懷豪右，為拒賊之計。

translations.literal: At the time his younger cousin Zhenqing was Pingyuan prefect; on first hearing Lushan's treasonous plot, he secretly nurtured men willing to die, summoned and embraced magnates and power-holders, making plans to resist bandits.
translations.idiomatic: His cousin Yan Zhenqing was governor of Pingyuan; as soon as he learned of Lushan's conspiracy he secretly trained die-hard fighters, rallied local leaders, and laid plans for resistance.

sentences.zh: 至是遣使告杲卿，相與起義兵，掎角斷賊歸路，以紓西寇之勢。

translations.literal: Now he sent envoys to inform Gaoqing; together they would raise righteous armies, pincer-like cut the bandits' return road, to loosen the western invaders' momentum.
translations.idiomatic: He now sent word to Gaoqing, and together they raised loyalist troops to strike from two sides, cut off the rebels' retreat, and ease the pressure on the western front.

sentences.zh: 杲卿乃與長史袁履謙、前真定令賈深、前內丘丞張通幽等，謀開土門以背之。

translations.literal: Gaoqing then with Chief Administrator Yuan Lüqian, former Zhending magistrate Jia Shen, former Neiqiu assistant Zhang Tongyou and others plotted to open Tumen Pass and turn against them.
translations.idiomatic: Gaoqing joined Chief Administrator Yuan Lüqian, the former magistrate of Zhending Jia Shen, the former assistant magistrate of Neiqiu Zhang Tongyou, and others in a plan to seize Tumen Pass and attack from the rear.

sentences.zh: 時祿山遣蔣欽湊、高邈率眾五千守土門。

translations.literal: At the time Lushan dispatched Jiang Qincou and Gao Miao leading five thousand troops to guard Tumen.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan had sent Jiang Qincou and Gao Miao with five thousand men to hold Tumen Pass.

sentences.zh: 杲卿欲誅欽湊，開土門之路。

translations.literal: Gaoqing wished to execute Qincou and open the road through Tumen.
translations.idiomatic: Gaoqing intended to kill Qincou and open the pass.

sentences.zh: 時欽湊軍隸常山郡，屬欽湊遣高邈往幽州未還，杲卿遣吏召欽湊至郡計事。

translations.literal: At the time Qincou's army was subordinate to Changshan commandery; just as Qincou had sent Gao Miao to Youzhou and he had not returned, Gaoqing sent clerks to summon Qincou to the commandery to plan affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Qincou's troops reported to Changshan commandery; with Gao Miao away on a mission to Youzhou, Gaoqing summoned Qincou to the prefectural seat on pretext of consultation.

sentences.zh: 是月二十二日夜，欽湊至，舍之於傳舍。

translations.literal: That month on the twenty-second night, Qincou arrived; they lodged him at the post station.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of the twenty-second he arrived and was put up at the official guesthouse.

sentences.zh: 會飲既醉，令袁履謙與參軍馮虔、縣尉李棲默、手力翟萬德等殺欽湊。

translations.literal: When the drinking meeting was finished and he was drunk, he ordered Yuan Lüqian together with staff officer Feng Qian, county captain Li Qimo, personal guard Zhai Wande and others to kill Qincou.
translations.idiomatic: Once Qincou was drunk at the banquet, Gaoqing had Yuan Lüqian, the military adjutant Feng Qian, the county captain Li Qimo, and the guard Zhai Wande kill him.

sentences.zh: 中夜，履謙以欽湊首見杲卿，相與垂泣，喜事交濟也。
