translations.literal: In the middle of the night Lüqian with Qincou's head came before Gaoqing; together they wept, glad affairs intersecting in support.
translations.idiomatic: At midnight Yuan Lüqian brought Qincou's head to Gaoqing; the two men wept together, rejoicing that fortune had smiled on their cause.

sentences.zh: 是夜，稾城尉崔安石報高邈還至蒲城，即令馮虔、翟萬德與安石往圖之。

translations.literal: That same night Gaocheng captain Cui Anshi reported Gao Miao returning to Pucheng; immediately he ordered Feng Qian, Zhai Wande and Anshi to go and scheme against him.
translations.idiomatic: That same night the Gaocheng captain Cui Anshi reported that Gao Miao was returning through Pucheng; Gaoqing at once sent Feng Qian, Zhai Wande, and Anshi to ambush him.

sentences.zh: 詰朝，高邈之騎從數人至稾城驛，安石皆殺之。

translations.literal: At dawn the next morning, a few of Gao Miao's mounted followers arrived at Gaocheng station; Anshi killed them all.
translations.idiomatic: At daybreak several of Gao Miao's mounted escort reached the Gaocheng post station; Anshi killed every one of them.

sentences.zh: 俄而邈至，安石紿之曰：「太守備酒樂於傳舍。」

translations.literal: Shortly afterward Miao arrived; Anshi deceived him saying: "The prefect has prepared wine and music at the post station."
translations.idiomatic: When Miao himself appeared moments later, Anshi tricked him: "The governor has wine and entertainment waiting at the guesthouse.

sentences.zh: 邈方據廳下馬，馮虔等擒而縶之。

translations.literal: Miao had just dismounted in the hall when Feng Qian and others seized and bound him.
translations.idiomatic: As Miao dismounted in the courtyard, Feng Qian and the others seized and bound him.

sentences.zh: 是日，賊將何千年自東都來趙郡，馮虔、萬德伏兵於醴泉驛，千年至，又擒之。

translations.literal: That day, rebel general He Qiannian from the eastern capital came toward Zhao commandery; Feng Qian and Wande hid troops at Liquan station; when Qiannian arrived, they seized him again.
translations.idiomatic: That same day the rebel general He Qiannian was traveling from the eastern capital toward Zhao; Feng Qian and Wande lay in wait at the Liquan post station and captured him too.

sentences.zh: 即日縛二賊將還郡。

translations.literal: That same day they bound the two rebel generals and returned to the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: That day they brought the two captive rebel generals back to the prefectural seat.

sentences.zh: 杲卿遣子安平尉泉明及賈深、張通幽、翟萬德，函欽湊之首，械二賊，送於京師。

translations.literal: Gaoqing dispatched his son Anping captain Quan Ming together with Jia Shen, Zhang Tongyou, Zhai Wande—boxed Qincou's head, fettered the two bandits, sent to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Gaoqing sent his son Quan Ming, the captain of Anping, together with Jia Shen, Zhang Tongyou, and Zhai Wande to carry Qincou's head in a box and the two prisoners in chains to the capital.

sentences.zh: 至太原，節度使王承業留泉明、賈深等，寢杲卿之表。

translations.literal: Reaching Taiyuan, Military Commissioner Wang Chengye detained Quan Ming, Jia Shen and others, and suppressed Gaoqing's memorial.
translations.idiomatic: At Taiyuan the military commissioner Wang Chengye detained Quan Ming and Jia Shen and suppressed Gaoqing's report.

sentences.zh: 承業自上表獻之，以為己功。

translations.literal: Chengye himself submitted a memorial presenting them, taking it as his own merit.
translations.idiomatic: Chengye then submitted his own memorial claiming the prisoners as his own achievement.

sentences.zh: 玄宗不之知，擢拜承業大將軍，牙官獲賞者百數。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong did not know this; he promoted Chengye to Grand General; yamen officers receiving rewards numbered in the hundreds.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong, unaware of the truth, promoted Chengye to Grand General and rewarded a hundred of his staff.

sentences.zh: 玄宗尋知杲卿之功，乃加衛尉卿、兼御史大夫，以袁履謙為常山太守，賈深為司馬。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong soon learned of Gaoqing's merit; then he added Guardian of the Palace of Grand Brightness, concurrently Censor-in-Chief; he made Yuan Lüqian Changshan prefect and Jia Shen Chief Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor finally learned of Gaoqing's deeds he appointed him Minister of the Court of Imperial Regalia and concurrent Censor-in-Chief, made Yuan Lüqian governor of Changshan, and Jia Shen his chief administrator.

sentences.zh: 杲卿既斬賊將，收兵練卒，乃檄告河北郡縣，言朝廷以榮王為河北兵馬大元帥，哥舒翰為副，統眾三十萬，即出土門。

translations.literal: Gaoqing having already beheaded the bandit generals, gathered troops and trained soldiers, then issued proclamations notifying Hebei commanderies and counties, saying the court had made Prince Rong Hebei Grand Marshal of armies and cavalry, with Geshu Han as deputy, commanding three hundred thousand men, about to exit Tumen Pass.
translations.idiomatic: After executing the rebel generals and drilling his troops, Gaoqing sent proclamations throughout Hebei announcing that Prince Rong commanded three hundred thousand imperial troops as Grand Marshal, with Geshu Han as his deputy, and would soon march out through Tumen Pass.

sentences.zh: 郡縣聞之，皆殺賊守將，遠近響應，時十五郡皆為國家所守。

translations.literal: Commanderies and counties hearing this all killed bandit garrison generals; near and far responded; at the time fifteen commanderies were all held for the state.
translations.idiomatic: Where the proclamation reached, local officials killed their rebel garrisons and rose in support; within weeks fifteen commanderies were back under imperial control.

sentences.zh: 時安祿山遣使傳李憕、盧奕之首徇河北。

translations.literal: At the time An Lushan sent envoys to display the heads of Li Ming and Lu Yi throughout Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: An Lushan sent agents through Hebei parading the severed heads of Li Ming and Lu Yi.

sentences.zh: 至平原，真卿殺賊使，收藏憕等首。

translations.literal: Reaching Pingyuan, Zhenqing killed the bandit envoys and preserved the heads of Ming and the others.
translations.idiomatic: At Pingyuan, Zhenqing executed the rebel messengers and honorably buried the heads of Li Ming and the others.

sentences.zh: 清池尉賈載亦斬偽署景城守劉玄道，傳首於平原。

translations.literal: Qingchi captain Jia Zai also beheaded the falsely appointed Jingcheng garrison commander Liu Xuandao and transmitted the head to Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: The Qingchi captain Jia Zai also killed the rebel-appointed garrison commander of Jingcheng, Liu Xuandao, and sent his head to Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 饒陽郡守盧全誠亦據郡舉兵，會於真卿。

translations.literal: Raoyang commandery prefect Lu Quancheng also held the commandery and raised troops, joining with Zhenqing.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Quancheng, governor of Raoyang, also seized his district and raised troops, then joined forces with Zhenqing.

sentences.zh: 時常山、平原二郡兵威大振。

translations.literal: At the time Changshan and Pingyuan two commanderies' military prestige greatly flourished.
translations.idiomatic: The loyalist armies of Changshan and Pingyuan now commanded the field.

sentences.zh: 祿山方自率眾而西，已至陜，聞河北有變而還，乃命史思明、蔡希德率眾渡河。

translations.literal: Lushan was just personally leading troops westward, already reaching Shaan; hearing Hebei had change he returned, then ordered Shi Siming and Cai Xide to lead troops crossing the river.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan had been marching west in person and had reached Shaan when news of the uprising reached him; he turned back and ordered Shi Siming and Cai Xide to cross the Yellow River with their armies.

sentences.zh: 十五年正月，思明攻常山郡。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year first month, Siming attacked Changshan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fifteenth year Shi Siming besieged Changshan.

sentences.zh: 城中兵少，眾寡不敵，禦備皆竭。

translations.literal: Within the city troops were few; multitude and few could not match; all defenses were exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: The city held too few defenders to match the enemy; every resource for defense was spent.

sentences.zh: 其月八日，城陷，杲卿、履謙為賊所執，送於東都。

translations.literal: That month on the eighth day the city fell; Gaoqing and Lüqian were seized by bandits and sent to the eastern capital.
translations.idiomatic: On the eighth of that month the city fell; Gaoqing and Yuan Lüqian were captured and sent to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 思明既陷常山，遂攻諸郡，鄴、廣平、鉅鹿、趙郡、上谷、博陵、文安、魏郡、信都，復為賊守。

translations.literal: Siming having already fallen Changshan, then attacked the commanderies: Ye, Guangping, Julu, Zhao, Shanggu, Boling, Wen'an, Wei, Xindu—all again became bandit-held.
translations.idiomatic: After taking Changshan, Siming swept through the region; Ye, Guangping, Julu, Zhao, Shanggu, Boling, Wen'an, Wei, and Xindu all fell back under rebel control.

sentences.zh: 祿山見杲卿，面責之曰：「汝昨自范陽戶曹，我奏為判官，遂得光祿、太常二丞，便用汝攝常山太守，負汝何事而背我耶？」

translations.literal: Lushan saw Gaoqing and face-to-face reproached him saying: "You yesterday came from Fanyang household registrar; I memorialized making you judge; thus you obtained two ranks of Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Grand Master of Imperial Harmony, then immediately used you as acting Changshan prefect—what did I fail you in that you betray me?"
translations.idiomatic: When Lushan confronted Gaoqing he raged: "You were nothing but a clerk in Fanyang until I made you my aide and raised you to high office, even appointing you governor of Changshan—what wrong did I do you that you turned against me?

sentences.zh: 杲卿瞋目而報曰：「我世為唐臣，常守忠義，縱受汝奏署，復合從汝反乎！

translations.literal: Gaoqing glaring eyes replied saying: "My family for generations has been Tang subjects, always keeping loyalty and righteousness; even if accepting your memorial appointment, how should I follow you in rebellion!
translations.idiomatic: Gaoqing glared back: "My family has served the Tang for generations in loyalty and faith; even if you appointed me, should I therefore join your rebellion?

sentences.zh: 且汝本營州一牧羊羯奴耳，叨竊恩寵，致身及此，天子負汝何事而汝反耶？」

translations.literal: Moreover you originally were a Camp Prefecture sheep-herding Jie slave; presumptuously stealing favor, reaching this body—what did the Son of Heaven fail you in that you rebel!"
translations.idiomatic: And you—what were you but a sheepherding slave of Jie stock from Camp Prefecture, who clawed his way to power on imperial favor? What wrong did the Son of Heaven ever do you that you would rebel?"

sentences.zh: 祿山怒甚，令縛於中橋南頭從西第二柱，節解之，比至氣絕，大罵不息。

translations.literal: Lushan rage extreme, ordered binding at Central Bridge south head from west second pillar, dismembering limb by limb; by the time breath ceased, great cursing did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan was furious; he had Gaoqing bound to the second pillar from the west at the south end of Central Bridge and dismembered limb by limb. He cursed without pause until his last breath was gone.

sentences.zh: 是日杲卿幼子誕、侄詡及袁履謙，皆被先截手足，何千年弟在傍，含血噴其面，因加割臠，路人見之流涕。

translations.literal: That day Gaoqing's young son Dan, nephew Xu and Yuan Lüqian—all first had hands and feet cut off; He Qiannian's younger brother was at the side, holding blood spitting on his face, then added cutting flesh; passersby seeing wept.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Gaoqing's young son Dan, his nephew Xu, and Yuan Lüqian all had their limbs severed first; He Qiannian's brother stood by, spat blood in their faces, then carved them to pieces before the watching crowd, which wept at the sight.

sentences.zh: 其年二月，李光弼、郭子儀之師自土門東下，復收常山郡。

translations.literal: That year second month, Li Guangbi and Guo Ziyi's armies from Tumen eastward descended, again recovered Changshan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of that year the armies of Li Guangbi and Guo Ziyi marched east through Tumen Pass and recaptured Changshan.

sentences.zh: 杲卿、履謙等妻女數百人，繫之獄中，光弼破械出之，令行喪服，給遣周厚。

translations.literal: Gaoqing, Lüqian and others' wives and daughters numbering several hundred were imprisoned; Guangbi broke fetters and released them, ordered mourning garments worn, provisions and dispatch generous and thick.
translations.idiomatic: Several hundred wives and daughters of Gaoqing, Yuan Lüqian, and the others had been thrown into prison; Guangbi freed them, had them put on mourning dress, and saw to their generous support and safe passage.

sentences.zh: 冬，廣平王收復兩京，史思明以河朔歸國。

translations.literal: Winter, Prince of Guangping recovered both capitals; Shi Siming with Hebei and Shu returned to the state.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Prince of Guangping recaptured both capitals; Shi Siming and the armies of the north submitted to the throne.

sentences.zh: 時真卿為蒲州刺史，乃令泉明於河北求訪血屬。

translations.literal: At the time Zhenqing was Puzhou prefect; then he ordered Quan Ming in Hebei to seek and visit blood relations.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zhenqing was then governor of Pu Prefecture; he sent Quan Ming through Hebei to search for surviving kin.

sentences.zh: 杲卿妹先適故榆次令張景儋，妹女流落賊中，泉明一女亦落賊中，俱索購錢三萬。

translations.literal: Gaoqing's younger sister had earlier been married to the former magistrate of Yuci, Zhang Jingdan; her daughter was lost wandering among the rebels, and one of Quan Ming's daughters was also lost among the rebels—both demanded ransom money of thirty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Gaoqing's sister had married the former magistrate of Yuci, Zhang Jingdan. Her daughter and one of Quan Ming's daughters were both captured by the rebels, each held for a ransom of thirty thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 泉明悉索所費，購姑女而還，比復納購，己女遂失。

translations.literal: Quan Ming exhausted all he could gather in expenses, purchased his aunt's daughter and returned; by the time he paid ransom again, his own daughter was already lost.
translations.idiomatic: Quan Ming spent everything he had to ransom his cousin and bring her back; when he tried to pay again for his own daughter, she was already gone.

sentences.zh: 而袁履謙已下，父之將吏妻子奴隸三百餘人，轉徙賊中，窮窘無告。

translations.literal: Moreover, from Yuan Lüqian downward, his father's generals, officials, wives, children, and slaves numbering over three hundred drifted among the rebels, destitute with none to appeal to.
translations.idiomatic: More than three hundred people—Yuan Lüqian and the other officers, officials, wives, children, and servants who had served under Gaoqing—were scattered among the rebels, destitute and with nowhere to turn.

sentences.zh: 泉明悉以歸蒲州，真卿贍給久之，隨其所詣而資送之。

translations.literal: Quan Ming brought them all back to Puzhou; Zhenqing supported and provisioned them for a long time, according to wherever each wished to go providing funds and escort.
translations.idiomatic: Quan Ming brought them all to Pu Prefecture, where Zhenqing supported them for a long time and gave each person funds and safe passage wherever they wished to go.

sentences.zh: 泉明求其父屍於東都，得其行刑者，言杲卿被害時，先斷一足，與履謙同坎瘞之。

translations.literal: Quan Ming sought his father's corpse in the Eastern Capital; he found his executioner, who said when Gaoqing was killed, first one foot was severed, and he was buried in the same pit with Lüqian.
translations.idiomatic: In the Eastern Capital Quan Ming tracked down the man who had executed his father, who said that when Gaoqing was killed one of his feet was cut off first and he was buried in the same grave as Yuan Lüqian.

sentences.zh: 及發瘞得屍，果無一足，即日與履謙之屍，各為一柩，扶護還長安。

translations.literal: When they opened the burial and obtained the corpse, indeed there was no one foot; that same day with Lüqian's corpse, each was made a separate coffin, escorted and returned to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: When they exhumed the body they found, as reported, that one foot was missing. That same day they placed Gaoqing and Yuan Lüqian each in his own coffin and escorted them back to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 初，履謙妻疑夫柩殮衣儉薄，發棺視之，一與杲卿等，履謙妻號踴感嘆，待之如父。

translations.literal: Initially, Lüqian's wife suspected her husband's coffin shroud clothes were meager and thin; opening the coffin to view them, they were exactly the same as Gaoqing's and the others'; Lüqian's wife wailed and lamented, treating him as a father.
translations.idiomatic: At first Lüqian's wife feared her husband had been buried in mean grave clothes; when she opened the coffin she saw he had been laid out exactly like Gaoqing. She wept in grief and from then on treated Quan Ming as she would a father.

sentences.zh: 泉明之志行仁義如此。

translations.literal: Quan Ming's will and conduct in benevolence and righteousness were such as this.
translations.idiomatic: Such was Quan Ming's character—a life lived in benevolence and righteousness.

sentences.zh: 五月，詔曰：「故衛尉卿、兼御史中丞、恆州刺史顏杲卿，任彼專城，志梟狂虜，艱難之際，忠義在心。

translations.literal: Fifth month, an edict said: "The late Chamberlain for the Palace Garrison, concurrently Censor-in-Chief, Hengzhou prefect Yan Gaoqing—entrusted there with sole charge of a walled city, his will to decapitate the mad invader; in times of hardship, loyalty and righteousness in his heart.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month an edict proclaimed: "The late Yan Gaoqing, Chamberlain for the Palace Garrison, Censor-in-Chief, and governor of Heng Prefecture—charged with defending a city on his own, resolved to destroy the rebel horde—never lost his loyalty even in the darkest hour.

sentences.zh: 憤群兇而慷慨，臨大節而奮發，遂擒元惡，成此茂勛。

translations.literal: Angry at the multitude of villains and impassioned, facing great integrity and stirred to action, then captured the chief villain, accomplished this abundant merit.
translations.idiomatic: Roused by righteous wrath against the rebels, he seized the moment when honor demanded action, captured the ringleader, and won splendid distinction.

sentences.zh: 屬胡虜憑陵，流毒方熾，孤城力屈，見陷寇仇，身歿名存，實彰忠烈。

translations.literal: When barbarian invaders relied on aggression, flowing poison just blazing fiercely, the lone city strength exhausted, fell into enemy hands, body perished yet name survives—truly manifest loyalty and heroism.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels swept over the land and his isolated city could hold no longer, he fell into enemy hands; though he died, his name endures—a true exemplar of loyalty and courage.

sentences.zh: 夫仁者有勇，驗之於臨難；

translations.literal: Now the benevolent have courage—tested in facing difficulty;
translations.idiomatic: The truly virtuous prove their courage when hardship comes;

sentences.zh: 臣之報國，義存於捐軀。

translations.literal: a minister's repayment of the state—the righteousness exists in surrendering the body.
translations.idiomatic: a loyal subject repays his sovereign by giving his life.

sentences.zh: 嘉其死節之誠，未備飾終之禮，可贈太子太保。」

translations.literal: Commend his death in integrity's sincerity; final honors not yet complete—may posthumously grant Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent."
translations.idiomatic: We honor his faithful death; full funeral rites were never given. Let him be posthumously appointed Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent."

sentences.zh: 薛願薛願，河東汾陰人。

translations.literal: Xue Yuan—Xue Yuan was a man of Hedong Fenyin.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Yuan was a native of Fenyin in Hedong.

sentences.zh: 父縚，禮部郎中。

translations.literal: His father Tao was a Langbu Langzhong.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xue Tao was a director in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 兄崇一，尚惠宣太子女宜君縣主。

translations.literal: His elder brother Chongyi married Princess Huixuan's daughter, the Lady of Yijun County.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Chongyi had married the Lady of Yijun County, daughter of Princess Huixuan.

sentences.zh: 女弟為廢太子瑛妃。

translations.literal: A younger sister was consort to the deposed Crown Prince Ying.
translations.idiomatic: A younger sister had been a consort to the deposed Crown Prince Li Ying.

sentences.zh: 願坐宮廢貶官。

translations.literal: Yuan because of palace deposal was demoted in office.
translations.idiomatic: Because of the palace intrigue that brought down the crown prince, Yuan was demoted.

sentences.zh: 祿山之亂，南陽節度使魯炅奏用願為潁川太守、本郡防禦使。

translations.literal: In the An Lushan rebellion, Nanyang military governor Lu Kui memorialized to employ Yuan as Yingchuan prefect and defense commissioner of that commandery.
translations.idiomatic: During the An Lushan rebellion, Lu Kui, military governor of Nanyang, recommended Yuan as prefect of Yingchuan and commissioner for the commandery's defense.

sentences.zh: 時賊已陷陳留、滎陽、汝南等郡，方圍南陽。

translations.literal: At the time the rebels had already taken Chenliu, Xingyang, Runan and other commanderies, and were just then besieging Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels had already captured Chenliu, Xingyang, Runan, and other commanderies and were now laying siege to Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 潁川當其來往之路，願與防禦副使龐堅同力固守，城中儲蓄無素，兵卒單寡。

translations.literal: Yingchuan lay on their coming-and-going route; Yuan with defense vice-commissioner Pang Jian together exerted strength to hold fast—the city had no prior stores, soldiers few and sparse.
translations.idiomatic: Yingchuan stood on the rebels' main line of march. Yuan and his deputy Pang Jian resolved to hold the city together, but supplies were scant and their force was small.

sentences.zh: 自正月至十一月，賊晝夜攻之不息，距城百里，廬舍墳墓林樹開發斬徹殆盡，而外救無至。

translations.literal: From the first month to the eleventh month, the rebels day and night attacked without cease; within a hundred li of the city, dwellings, tombs, groves and trees were stripped and cut down nearly to exhaustion, yet outside relief did not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: From the first month through the eleventh the rebels attacked without pause, day and night. Within a hundred li of the city they stripped the land bare—houses, graves, woods, and orchards all cut down—and no relief force ever came.

sentences.zh: 賊將阿史那承慶悉以銳卒並攻，為木驢木鵝，雲梯沖棚，四面雲合，鼓噪如雷，矢石如雨，力攻十餘日，城中守備皆竭，賊夜半乘梯而入。

translations.literal: The rebel general Ashina Chengqing with all elite troops jointly attacked, making wooden donkeys and wooden geese, cloud ladders and battering sheds; on four sides clouds converged, drums and shouts like thunder, arrows and stones like rain; forcefully attacked over ten days—the city's defenses all exhausted; at midnight the rebels mounted ladders and entered.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel general Ashina Chengqing threw his best troops into the assault, deploying siege towers, battering rams, and covered approaches. The attackers closed in from every side amid thunderous war cries and a storm of arrows and stones. After more than ten days of fierce fighting the defenders were spent, and at midnight the rebels scaled the walls.

sentences.zh: 願、堅俱被執，送於東都，將支解之。

translations.literal: Yuan and Jian were both seized, sent to the Eastern Capital, about to be dismembered.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan and Pang Jian were both captured and sent to the Eastern Capital, where they were about to be torn limb from limb.

sentences.zh: 或說祿山曰：「薛願、龐堅，義士也。

translations.literal: Someone said to Lushan: "Xue Yuan and Pang Jian are righteous men.
translations.idiomatic: Someone urged An Lushan: "Xue Yuan and Pang Jian are men of honor.

sentences.zh: 人各為其主，屠之不祥。」

translations.literal: Each man serves his own lord; to slaughter them is inauspicious."
translations.idiomatic: Each was only doing his duty to his master. To butcher them would bring ill fortune."

sentences.zh: 乃繫於洛水之濱，屬苦寒，一夕凍死。

translations.literal: Then they were bound on the banks of the Luo River; it happened to be bitter cold, and in one night they froze to death.
translations.idiomatic: So the two men were bound on the banks of the Luo River. The weather turned bitterly cold, and they froze to death in a single night.

sentences.zh: 附 龐堅堅，武德功臣玉之玄孫。

translations.literal: Appendix: Pang Jian—Jian was the great-great-grandson of the Wude-era meritorious subject Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Appendix: Pang Jian was the great-great-grandson of Pang Yu, a founding hero of the Tang.

sentences.zh: 初娶邠王守禮女建寧縣主。

translations.literal: Initially he married Prince Bin Shouli's daughter, the Lady of Jianning County.
translations.idiomatic: He had first married the Lady of Jianning County, daughter of Prince Bin Shouli.

sentences.zh: 魯炅奏為潁川郡長史，兼防禦副使。

translations.literal: Lu Kui memorialized appointing him Yingchuan commandery chief secretary, concurrently defense vice-commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Kui had him appointed chief secretary of Yingchuan commandery and deputy defense commissioner.

sentences.zh: 張巡張巡，蒲州河東人。

translations.literal: Zhang Xun—Zhang Xun was a man of Hedong in Puzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xun was a native of Hedong in Pu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 兄曉，開元中監察御史。

translations.literal: His elder brother Xiao in the Kaiyuan era was a supervising censor.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Zhang Xiao had served as a supervising censor under Emperor Xuanzong.

sentences.zh: 兄弟皆以文行知名。

translations.literal: The brothers were both known for literary conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Both brothers were known for learning and upright character.

sentences.zh: 巡聰悟有才幹，舉進士，三以書判拔萃入等。

translations.literal: Xun was perceptive and talented, passed the jinshi examination, three times by document judgment distinguished and entered the grade.
translations.idiomatic: Xun was quick-witted and capable. He passed the jinshi examination and three times earned top marks in the document-judgment portion of the civil service exam.

sentences.zh: 天寶中，調授清河令。

translations.literal: In the Tianbao era, through transfer was appointed magistrate of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianbao reign he was posted as magistrate of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 有能名，重義尚氣節，人以危窘告者，必傾財以恤之。

translations.literal: He had a reputation for ability, valued righteousness and honored integrity; when people reported distress and hardship to him, he always poured out wealth to relieve them.
translations.idiomatic: He earned a reputation for competence and prized loyalty above all. Whenever anyone came to him in distress he would give freely of his own money to help.

sentences.zh: 祿山之亂，巡為真源令。

translations.literal: In the An Lushan rebellion, Xun was magistrate of Zhenyuan.
translations.idiomatic: When the An Lushan rebellion broke out, Xun was serving as magistrate of Zhenyuan.

sentences.zh: 說譙郡太守，令完城，募市人，為拒賊之勢。

translations.literal: He persuaded the Qiao commandery prefect, ordering completion of the walls, recruiting townspeople, to form a posture of resisting the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: He persuaded the prefect of Qiao commandery to repair the city walls, recruit townspeople, and prepare to resist the rebels.

sentences.zh: 時吳王祗為靈昌太守，奉詔糾率河南諸郡，練兵以拒逆黨，濟南太守李隨副之。

translations.literal: At the time Prince of Wu Zhi was Lingchang prefect, received the edict to muster and lead the Henan commanderies, drill troops to resist the rebel faction; Jinan prefect Li Sui assisted him.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Wu Li Zhi was then governor of Lingchang. By imperial order he was rallying the commanderies of Henan, training troops to resist the rebels, with Li Sui, governor of Jinan, as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 巡與單父尉賈賁各召募豪傑，同為義舉。

translations.literal: Xun with Shanfu assistant magistrate Jia Ben each recruited bold heroes, together making a righteous rising.
translations.idiomatic: Xun and Jia Ben, assistant magistrate of Shanfu, each raised bands of local leaders and joined in a loyalist uprising.

sentences.zh: 時雍丘令令狐潮欲以其城降賊，民吏百餘人不從命，潮皆反接，仆之於地，將斬之。

translations.literal: At the time Yongqiu magistrate Linghu Chao wished to surrender his city to the rebels; over a hundred commoners and officials did not obey the order—Chao all had their arms bound behind them, thrown to the ground, about to be beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: The magistrate of Yongqiu, Linghu Chao, wanted to surrender the city to the rebels. More than a hundred officials and townspeople refused. Chao had them bound, thrown to the ground, and was about to execute them.

sentences.zh: 會賊來攻城，潮遽出鬥，而反接者自解其縛，閉城門拒潮召賁。

translations.literal: Just then rebels came to attack the city; Chao hastily went out to fight, while those bound behind freed their own bonds, closed the city gates to reject Chao and summoned Ben.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels then attacked the city. Chao rushed out to fight them, but the bound men freed themselves, shut the gates against him, and sent for Jia Ben.

sentences.zh: 賁與巡引眾入雍丘，殺潮妻子，嬰城守備。

translations.literal: Ben with Xun led the multitude into Yongqiu, killed Chao's wife and children, encircled the city and prepared defenses.
translations.idiomatic: Ben and Xun marched into Yongqiu with their men, killed Chao's wife and children, and sealed the city to prepare its defense.

sentences.zh: 吳王祗承制授賁監察御史。

translations.literal: Prince of Wu Zhi by provisional order appointed Ben supervising censor.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Wu Li Zhi provisionally appointed Ben supervising censor.

sentences.zh: 數日，賊來攻城，賁出鬥而死，巡乃合賁之眾城守。

translations.literal: Several days later, rebels came to attack the city; Ben went out to fight and died; Xun then combined Ben's troops to defend the city.
translations.idiomatic: A few days later the rebels attacked again. Ben sallied forth and was killed in battle. Xun then took command of Ben's men and continued the defense.

sentences.zh: 令狐潮引賊將李廷望攻圍累月，賊傷夷大半。

translations.literal: Linghu Chao led the rebel general Li Tingwang to attack and besiege for accumulated months; the rebels' casualties and wounds were over half.
translations.idiomatic: Linghu Chao brought the rebel general Li Tingwang to besiege the city for months on end, and the attackers lost more than half their force.

sentences.zh: 祿山乃於雍丘北置杞州，築城壘以絕餉路，自是內外隔絕。

translations.literal: Lushan then north of Yongqiu established Qi prefecture, building walled camps to cut off supply routes—from then on inside and outside were cut off.
translations.idiomatic: An Lushan then established Qi Prefecture north of Yongqiu and built fortified camps to sever the supply lines, isolating the city completely.

sentences.zh: 又相持累月，賊鋒轉熾，城中益困。

translations.literal: Again they faced off for accumulated months; the rebels' edge turned ever fiercer, the city grew ever more distressed.
translations.idiomatic: The stalemate dragged on for months. The rebel assaults grew fiercer and conditions inside the city grew ever more desperate.

sentences.zh: 時許遠為睢陽守，與城父令姚同守睢陽城，賊攻之不下。

translations.literal: At the time Xu Yuan was Suiyang defender, with Chengfu magistrate Yao jointly defending Suiyang city—the rebels attacked but could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yuan was then defending Suiyang, together with Yao Gun, magistrate of Chengfu. The rebels besieged the city but could not capture it.

sentences.zh: 初祿山陷河洛，許叔冀守靈昌，薛願守潁川，許遠守睢陽，皆城孤無援。

translations.literal: Initially when Lushan took He and Luo, Xu Shuji defended Lingchang, Xue Yuan defended Yingchuan, Xu Yuan defended Suiyang—all cities isolated without relief.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan first overran the Yellow River basin and the two capitals, Xu Shuji held Lingchang, Xue Yuan held Yingchuan, and Xu Yuan held Suiyang—each city alone and without aid.

sentences.zh: 願守一年而城陷，督冀一年而自拔，獨睢陽堅守。

translations.literal: Yuan defended one year then the city fell; Shuji defended one year then broke out on his own—only Suiyang held fast.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan's city fell after a year of defense; Shuji broke out after a year under siege. Only Suiyang continued to hold.

sentences.zh: 賊將尹子奇攻圍經年。

translations.literal: The rebel general Yin Ziqi attacked and besieged for a full year.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel general Yin Ziqi laid siege to the city for an entire year.

sentences.zh: 巡以雍丘小邑，儲備不足，大寇臨之，必難保守，乃列卒結陣詐降，正月也。

translations.literal: Xun because Yongqiu was a small town, stores insufficient, with great invaders approaching it would surely be hard to preserve—then lined troops and formed ranks feigning surrender; it was the first month.
translations.idiomatic: Xun judged that Yongqiu, a small town with meager stores, could not long withstand a major enemy force. In the first month he marched his men out in battle order under the pretense of surrender.

sentences.zh: 玄宗聞而壯之，授巡主客郎中、兼御史中丞。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong heard and admired it, appointing Xun Director of the Bureau of Receptions, concurrently Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanzong heard of this he was greatly impressed and appointed Xun Director of the Bureau of Receptions and Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 尹子奇攻圍既久，城中糧盡，易子而食，析骸而爨，人心危恐，慮將有變。

translations.literal: Yin Ziqi's attack and siege had already been long; in the city grain was exhausted—exchanging children to eat, splitting bones to cook; people's hearts were fearful and alarmed, fearing there would be a change.
translations.idiomatic: After a long siege by Yin Ziqi the city ran out of food. People traded their children to eat and broke open bones for fuel. Morale collapsed and mutiny seemed imminent.

sentences.zh: 巡乃出其妾，對三軍殺之，以饗軍士。

translations.literal: Xun then brought out his concubine, before the three armies killed her, to feast the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Xun then brought out his concubine, slaughtered her before the entire army, and had her flesh served to the troops.

sentences.zh: 曰：「諸公為國家戮力守城，一心無二，經年乏食，忠義不衰。

translations.literal: He said: "You gentlemen for the state exert strength to hold the city, one heart without duality; for a year lacking food, loyalty and righteousness undiminished.
translations.idiomatic: He said: "You have all fought as one to defend this city for the realm. For a year you have gone without food, yet your loyalty has never wavered.

sentences.zh: 巡不能自割肌膚，以啖將士，豈可惜此婦，坐視危迫。」

translations.literal: Xun cannot himself cut his flesh to feed officers and soldiers—how can he cherish this woman and sit watching peril and urgency?"
translations.idiomatic: I cannot cut my own flesh to feed you—how then could I spare this woman and stand by while you starve?"

sentences.zh: 將士皆泣下，不忍食，巡強令食之。

translations.literal: The officers and soldiers all wept tears, unwilling to eat; Xun forcibly ordered them to eat.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers wept and refused to eat, but Xun forced them to do so.

sentences.zh: 乃括城中婦人；

translations.literal: Then he gathered the women in the city;
translations.idiomatic: He then rounded up the women still in the city;

sentences.zh: 既盡，以男夫老小繼之，所食人口二三萬，人心終不離變。

translations.literal: When they were exhausted, with adult men, old and young succeeding them, those eaten numbered twenty or thirty thousand; people's hearts to the end did not depart in mutiny.
translations.idiomatic: When they were gone, the men, the old, and the children followed. Some twenty or thirty thousand people were consumed, yet the garrison never broke.

sentences.zh: 時賀蘭進明以重兵守臨淮，巡遣帳下之士南霽雲夜縋出城，求援於進明。

translations.literal: At the time Helan Jinming with heavy troops guarded Linhuai; Xun sent a man under his command, Nan Jiyun, who at night was lowered by rope out of the city, to seek relief from Jinming.
translations.idiomatic: Helan Jinming was then encamped at Linhuai with a large force. Xun sent his officer Nan Jiyun, who was lowered over the wall by rope at night to beg Jinming for relief.

sentences.zh: 進明日與諸將張樂高會，無出師意。

translations.literal: Jinming daily with the generals spread music in high feasting, with no intention of marching out.
translations.idiomatic: Jinming spent his days feasting with his generals and showed no sign of marching to their aid.

sentences.zh: 霽雲泣告之曰：「本州強寇淩逼，重圍半年，食盡兵窮，計無從出。

translations.literal: Jiyun weeping told him: "This prefecture—strong invaders press and threaten; heavy siege half a year, food exhausted troops at end, no plan from which to escape.
translations.idiomatic: Jiyun wept as he pleaded: "Our city has been crushed under siege for half a year. Food is gone and our men are spent. We see no way out.

sentences.zh: 初圍城之日，城中數萬口，今婦人老幼，相食殆盡，張中丞殺愛妾以啖軍人，今見存之數，不過數千，城中之人，分當餌賊。

translations.literal: On the first day of the siege, within the city were tens of thousands; now women, old and young, eating one another nearly to exhaustion—Assistant Censor Zhang killed his beloved concubine to feed the soldiers; now those surviving number no more than several thousand; the people in the city by rights ought to become bait for the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: When the siege began there were tens of thousands in the city. Now the women, the old, and the children have nearly all been eaten. Assistant Censor Zhang slaughtered his own concubine to feed the troops. Fewer than a few thousand remain, and they are ready to die fighting.

sentences.zh: 但睢陽既拔，即及臨淮，皮毛相依，理須援助。

translations.literal: But if Suiyang is already taken, then it reaches Linhuai—fur and skin depend on each other; by reason relief must be sent.
translations.idiomatic: But if Suiyang falls, Linhuai will be next. Our fates are bound together—you must send help.

sentences.zh: 霽雲所以冒賊鋒刃，匍匐乞師，謂大夫深念危亡，言發響應，何得宴安自處，殊無救恤之心？

translations.literal: The reason Jiyun braved the rebels' blades, crawling to beg for troops, was thinking the Grandee deeply considered peril and extinction, words spoken would ring in response—how can he feast in ease and dwell at ease, utterly without a heart to save and relieve?
translations.idiomatic: I crossed enemy lines on my knees to beg for troops because I believed you understood how close we are to ruin and would answer at once. How can you feast in comfort while showing no will to save us?

sentences.zh: 夫忠臣義士之所為，豈宜如此！

translations.literal: What loyal ministers and righteous men do—how should it be thus!
translations.idiomatic: Is this how a loyal officer behaves?

sentences.zh: 霽雲既不能達主將之意，請嚙一指，留於大夫，示之以信，歸報本州。」

translations.literal: Jiyun since he could not convey the commander-in-chief's intent, requested to bite off one finger, leave it with the Grandee to show as proof of faith, and return to report to his prefecture."
translations.idiomatic: Since I cannot win your assent, I ask leave to bite off a finger and leave it with you as proof that I came—and then return to report to my commanders."

sentences.zh: 霽雲自臨淮還睢陽，繩城而入。

translations.literal: Jiyun from Linhuai returned to Suiyang, by rope entered the city.
translations.idiomatic: Jiyun returned from Linhuai to Suiyang and was hauled back over the wall by rope.

sentences.zh: 城中將吏知救不至，慟哭累日。

translations.literal: The officers and officials in the city knowing relief would not arrive, wailed in grief for accumulated days.
translations.idiomatic: When the garrison learned that no relief was coming, they wept for days.

sentences.zh: 十月，城陷。

translations.literal: Tenth month, the city fell.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the city fell.

sentences.zh: 巡與姚、南霽雲、許遠，皆為賊所執。

translations.literal: Xun with Yao, Nan Jiyun, and Xu Yuan were all seized by the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Xun, Yao, Nan Jiyun, and Xu Yuan were all captured by the rebels.

sentences.zh: 巡神氣慷慨，每與賊戰，大呼誓師，眥裂血流，齒牙皆碎。

translations.literal: Xun's spirit was impassioned and bold; each time he fought the rebels he shouted loudly to rally the troops—eye corners split and blood flowed, teeth and gums all shattered.
translations.idiomatic: Xun's bearing was fierce and defiant. In every battle he roared his battle cry until the corners of his eyes split and bled and his teeth were ground to splinters.

sentences.zh: 城將陷，西向再拜，曰：「臣智勇俱竭，不能式遏強寇，保守孤城。

translations.literal: As the city was about to fall, he bowed twice facing west and said: "Your servant's wisdom and courage are both exhausted, unable to check the strong invaders and preserve this lone city.
translations.idiomatic: As the city was about to fall he bowed twice toward the west and said: "I have spent my wit and my strength. I could not hold back the enemy or save this isolated city.

sentences.zh: 臣雖為鬼，誓與賊為厲，以答明恩。」

translations.literal: Though your servant becomes a ghost, he vows to be a baleful spirit against the rebels, to repay bright grace."
translations.idiomatic: Even as a ghost I swear to harry these rebels and repay your grace."

sentences.zh: 及城陷，尹子奇謂巡曰：「聞君每戰眥裂，嚼齒皆碎，何至此耶？」

translations.literal: When the city fell, Yin Ziqi said to Xun: "I hear that each battle your eye corners split and you chew until teeth all shatter—how did it come to this?"
translations.idiomatic: After the city fell Yin Ziqi said to Xun: "They say that in every battle your eyes split open and you grind your teeth to pieces. How did you come to that?"

sentences.zh: 巡曰：「吾欲氣吞逆賊，但力不遂耳！」

translations.literal: Xun said: "I wished with my breath to swallow the rebel invaders—only my strength did not succeed!"
translations.idiomatic: Xun replied: "I meant to devour you rebels whole—I simply lacked the strength!"

sentences.zh: 子奇以大刀剔巡口，視其齒，存者不過三數。

translations.literal: Ziqi with a great knife pried open Xun's mouth, viewed his teeth—those remaining were no more than three or four.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Ziqi forced Xun's mouth open with a blade and looked inside. Only three or four teeth were left.

sentences.zh: 巡大罵曰：「我為君父義死。

translations.literal: Xun greatly reviled him, saying: "I die in righteousness for lord and father.
translations.idiomatic: Xun cursed him loudly: "I die in loyalty to my sovereign and my father.

sentences.zh: 爾附逆賊，犬彘也，安能久哉！」

translations.literal: You attach yourself to rebel invaders—you are dogs and pigs; how can you long endure!"
translations.idiomatic: You serve the rebels—you are less than beasts, and you will not last long!"

sentences.zh: 子奇義其言，將禮之，左右曰：「此人守義，必不為我用。

translations.literal: Ziqi admired his words, about to treat him with ceremony; those at his side said: "This man keeps to righteousness—he surely will not serve our use.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Ziqi was moved by his words and meant to treat him with honor, but his attendants said: "This man is too loyal ever to serve us.

sentences.zh: 素得士心，不可久留。」

translations.literal: He has long won soldiers' hearts—he cannot be long kept."
translations.idiomatic: The troops already revere him. He must not be kept alive."

sentences.zh: 是日，與姚、霽雲同被害，唯許遠執送洛陽。

translations.literal: That day, with Yao and Jiyun he was together killed; only Xu Yuan was seized and sent to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Yao and Nan Jiyun were executed with him. Only Xu Yuan was taken alive to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 附 姚誾姚誾者，浹州平陸人，故相梁國公崇之侄孫。

translations.literal: Appendix: Yao Yin—Yao Yin was a man of Pinglu in Jia Prefecture, the grand-nephew of the former chancellor Duke of Liang, Chong.
translations.idiomatic: Appendix: Yao Gun was a native of Pinglu in Jia Prefecture and a grand-nephew of the former chancellor Yao Chong, Duke of Liang.

sentences.zh: 父弇，開元初歷處州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Yan in early Kaiyuan successively served as Chuzhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yao Yan had served as governor of Chu Prefecture in the early Kaiyuan reign.

sentences.zh: 誾性豪蕩，好飲謔，善絲竹。

translations.literal: Yin's nature was bold and unrestrained; he loved drinking and jesting, skilled in string and bamboo music.
translations.idiomatic: Gun was bold and free-spirited, fond of wine and banter, and skilled at music.

sentences.zh: 歷壽安尉、城父令，與張巡素相親善。

translations.literal: He successively served as Shou'an assistant magistrate and Chengfu magistrate; with Zhang Xun from of old he was mutually close and friendly.
translations.idiomatic: He served as assistant magistrate of Shou'an and then magistrate of Chengfu, and had long been close to Zhang Xun.

sentences.zh: 以守睢陽之功，春，加檢校尚書侍郎。

translations.literal: For the merit of defending Suiyang, in spring he was additionally appointed Acting Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: For his defense of Suiyang he was promoted in the spring to Acting Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 賈賁者，故閬州刺史璿之子也。

translations.literal: Jia Ben was the son of the former Langzhou prefect Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Ben was the son of the former governor of Lang Prefecture, Jia Xuan.

sentences.zh: 許遠許遠者，杭州鹽官人也。

translations.literal: Xu Yuan—Xu Yuan was a man of Yanguan in Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yuan was a native of Yanguan in Hang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 世仕江右。

translations.literal: His family for generations served in the lands west of the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: His clan had served for generations in the south.

sentences.zh: 曾祖高陽公敬宗，龍朔中宰相，自有傳。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Duke of Gaoyang Jingzong in the Longshuo era was chancellor; he has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Xu Jingzong, Duke of Gaoyang, had served as chancellor under Emperor Gaozong and has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 遠清幹，初從軍河西，為磧西支度判官。

translations.literal: Yuan was clear and capable; initially he followed the army in Hexi, serving as Qixi supply commissioner judge.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan was capable and upright. He first saw military service in Hexi as supply commissioner for the Western Deserts command.

sentences.zh: 章仇兼瓊鎮劍南，又辟為從事。

translations.literal: Zhangqiu Jianqiong governed Jiannan, again recruiting him as staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhangqiu Jianqiong was military governor of Jiannan he recruited Yuan as a staff officer.

sentences.zh: 慕其門，欲以子妻之。

translations.literal: He admired his house, wished to give his son in marriage to him.
translations.idiomatic: Impressed by the Xu family's standing, he wanted his son to marry Yuan's daughter.

sentences.zh: 遠辭，兼瓊怒，積他事中傷，貶為高要尉。

translations.literal: Yuan declined; Jianqiong was angry, accumulated other matters to slander him, and demoted him to Gaoyao assistant magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan refused. Jianqiong took offense, found pretexts to attack him, and had him demoted to assistant magistrate of Gaoyao.

sentences.zh: 後遇赦得還。

translations.literal: Later he encountered an amnesty and was able to return.
translations.idiomatic: He was later restored by an amnesty.

sentences.zh: 祿山之亂，不次拔將帥，或薦遠素練戎事。

translations.literal: In the An Lushan rebellion, out of turn generals and commanders were promoted; someone recommended that Yuan from of old was practiced in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: During the An Lushan rebellion commanders were promoted outside the usual order, and someone recommended Yuan as a man long versed in military affairs.

sentences.zh: 玄宗召見，拜睢陽太守，累加侍御史、本州防禦使。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong summoned him for an audience and appointed him Prefect of Suiyang; he was repeatedly promoted to Attendant Censor and Defender-in-Chief of his own prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor summoned him to court and named him prefect of Suiyang; he was then promoted step by step to attendant censor and defensive commissioner of the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 及賊將尹子奇攻圍，遠與張巡、姚摐嬰城拒守經年，外救不至，兵糧俱盡而城陷。

translations.literal: When the rebel general Yin Ziqi attacked and besieged the city, Yuan together with Zhang Xun and Yao Zhen tied themselves to the city and resisted for a year; outside relief did not arrive, troops and grain were both exhausted, and the city fell.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebel commander Yin Ziqi laid siege, Yuan joined Zhang Xun and Yao Zhen in holding the city for a full year. No relief came from outside; when arms and provisions were gone, the city fell.

sentences.zh: 尹子奇執送洛陽，與哥舒翰、程千里，俱囚之客省。

translations.literal: Yin Ziqi seized him and sent him to Luoyang; together with Geshu Han and Cheng Qianli, all were imprisoned in the Guest Reception Office.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Ziqi had him taken to Luoyang, where he and Geshu Han and Cheng Qianli were all held prisoner in the Guest Reception Office.

sentences.zh: 及安慶緒敗，渡河北走，使嚴莊皆害之。

translations.literal: When An Qingxu was defeated, crossing the river he fled north and ordered Yan Zhuang to kill them all.
translations.idiomatic: When An Qingxu was defeated and fled north across the Yellow River, he had Yan Zhuang put them all to death.

sentences.zh: 初，賀蘭進明與房琯素不相葉。

translations.literal: Initially, Helan Jinming and Fang Guan from of old did not harmonize with each other.
translations.idiomatic: From the first, Helan Jinming and Fang Guan had never been on good terms.

sentences.zh: 及琯為宰相，進明時為御史大夫。

translations.literal: When Guan became chief minister, Jinming was then Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: When Fang Guan became chief minister, Helan Jinming was serving as censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 琯奏用進明為彭城太守、河南節度使、兼御史大夫，代嗣虢王巨；

translations.literal: Guan memorialized to appoint Jinming as Prefect of Pengcheng, Military Governor of Henan, and concurrent Censor-in-Chief, replacing the heir Prince of Guo, Wang Ju;
translations.idiomatic: Fang Guan recommended appointing Jinming prefect of Pengcheng, military governor of Henan, and concurrent censor-in-chief, to replace the heir Prince of Guo, Wang Ju;

sentences.zh: 復用靈昌太守許叔冀為進明都知兵馬、兼御史大夫，重其官以挫進明。

translations.literal: Again he employed Lingchang Prefect Xu Shuji as Jinming's deputy in overall command of troops, concurrent Censor-in-Chief, elevating his office to check Jinming.
translations.idiomatic: He also appointed Xu Shuji, prefect of Lingchang, as Jinming's deputy commander of all forces with the concurrent title of censor-in-chief—raising Xu's rank deliberately to check Jinming's power.

sentences.zh: 虢王巨受代之時，盡將部曲而行，所留者揀退羸兵數千人、劣馬數百匹，不堪扞賊。

translations.literal: When Prince of Guo Ju accepted replacement, he took all his personal troops and departed; what he left behind were several thousand picked-out weak soldiers and several hundred inferior horses, unfit to resist rebels.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Ju was relieved of command he marched away with his entire personal force, leaving behind only a few thousand weeded-out weak troops and a few hundred poor horses—useless against the rebels.

sentences.zh: 叔冀恃部下精銳，又名位等於進明，自謂匹敵，不受進明節制。

translations.literal: Shuji relied on his subordinates' elite sharpness, and his name and rank were equal to Jinming's; he considered himself a match and did not accept Jinming's control.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Shuji counted on his own crack troops, and his rank matched Jinming's; he considered himself an equal and refused to submit to Jinming's authority.

sentences.zh: 故南霽雲之乞師，進明不敢分兵，懼叔冀見襲。

translations.literal: Therefore when Nan Jiyun begged for troops, Jinming did not dare divide his forces, fearing Shuji would be attacked.
translations.idiomatic: That is why when Nan Jiyun came to plead for reinforcements, Jinming would not detach troops—he feared Xu Shuji might strike him if he did.

sentences.zh: 兩相觀望，坐視危亡，致河南郡邑為墟，由執政之乖經制也。

translations.literal: The two watched each other and sat viewing peril and death, causing Henan prefectures and districts to become ruins—this was because those in power violated standard regulations.
translations.idiomatic: The two commanders stood idle, watching disaster unfold, until the prefectures and towns of Henan lay in ruins—a consequence of the court's mismanagement of military command.

sentences.zh: 程千里程千里，京兆人。

translations.literal: Cheng Qianli—Cheng Qianli, a man of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Qianli was a native of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 身長七尺，骨相魁岸，有勇力。

translations.literal: His body was seven chi in height, his bone structure towering, and he had courage and strength.
translations.idiomatic: He stood seven feet tall, with an imposing build and great strength.

sentences.zh: 本磧西募人，累以戎勛，官至安西副都護。

translations.literal: Originally a conscript from the Western Regions, through repeated military merit he reached the office of Vice Protector-General of Anxi.
translations.idiomatic: Originally a frontier recruit from beyond the desert passes, he rose through repeated battlefield service to become vice protector-general of Anxi.

sentences.zh: ，授御史中丞。

translations.literal: [He] was appointed Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 十二載，兼北庭都護，充安西北庭節度使。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, he additionally held the post of Protector of Beiting, serving as Military Governor of Anxi and Beiting.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Tianbao he was also made protector of Beiting and military governor of Anxi and Beiting.

sentences.zh: 突厥首領阿布思先率眾內附，隸朔方軍，玄宗賜姓名曰李獻忠。

translations.literal: The Türk chieftain Abusi first led his masses to submit inward, was placed under the Shuofang Army, and Emperor Xuanzong bestowed the surname and personal name Li Xianzhong.
translations.idiomatic: The Türk chieftain Abusi had earlier led his people to submit and was assigned to the Shuofang Army; Emperor Xuanzong granted him the surname Li and the name Xianzhong.

sentences.zh: 李林甫遙領朔方節度，用獻忠為副將。

translations.literal: Li Linfu remotely held the Shuofang military governorship and used Xianzhong as deputy general.
translations.idiomatic: Li Linfu held the Shuofang command in absentia and made Xianzhong his deputy.

sentences.zh: 後有詔移獻忠部落隸幽州，獻忠素與祿山有隙，懼不奉詔，乃叛歸磧北，數為邊患。

translations.literal: Later there was an edict moving Xianzhong's tribal group to be subordinate to Youzhou; Xianzhong from of old had rifts with Lushan, feared not obeying the edict, then rebelled and returned north of the desert, repeatedly becoming a border trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Later an edict ordered Xianzhong's tribe transferred to Youzhou. He had long been at odds with An Lushan and, fearing the consequences of obeying, fled back beyond the desert and repeatedly raided the frontier.

sentences.zh: 玄宗憤之，命千里將兵討之。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong was angry at this and ordered Qianli to lead troops to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong, enraged, ordered Cheng Qianli to take troops against him.

sentences.zh: 十二載十一月，千里兵至磧西，以書喻葛祿，令其相應。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the twelfth year, Qianli's troops reached the Western Regions; by letter he instructed the Karluk, ordering them to respond in concert.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the twelfth year Qianli's army reached the Western Regions and sent word to the Karluk, asking them to join the campaign.

sentences.zh: 獻忠勢窮，歸葛祿部。

translations.literal: Xianzhong's power was exhausted; he returned to the Karluk tribe.
translations.idiomatic: With his forces spent, Xianzhong took refuge with the Karluk.

sentences.zh: 葛祿縛獻忠並其妻子及帳下數千人，送之千里，飛表獻捷，天子壯之。

translations.literal: The Karluk bound Xianzhong together with his wife and children and several thousand men under his tent, sent them to Qianli, and flew a memorial presenting victory; the Son of Heaven admired this.
translations.idiomatic: The Karluk seized Xianzhong along with his wife, children, and several thousand followers and delivered them to Cheng Qianli; they sent a rapid dispatch announcing victory, and the Emperor was much pleased.

sentences.zh: 十三載三月，千里獻俘於勤政樓，斬之於硃雀街，以功授右金吾衛大將軍同正，仍留佐羽林軍。

translations.literal: In the third month of the thirteenth year, Qianli presented captives at Qinzheng Tower; he was beheaded at Vermilion Bird Street, and for merit was appointed Grand General of the Right Gold Crow Guard as Regular, still remaining to assist the Feathered Forest Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the thirteenth year Cheng Qianli presented the prisoners at Qinzheng Tower; Xianzhong was beheaded in Vermilion Bird Street. For this service Qianli was made grand general of the Right Gold Crow Guard and retained to assist the Imperial Guard.

sentences.zh: 祿山之亂，詔千里於河東召募，充河東節度副使、雲中太守。

translations.literal: In the An Lushan rebellion, an edict ordered Qianli to recruit at Hedong, serving as Deputy Military Governor of Hedong and Prefect of Yunzhong.
translations.idiomatic: When the An Lushan rebellion broke out, Qianli was ordered to raise troops in Hedong and was appointed deputy military governor of Hedong and prefect of Yunzhong.

sentences.zh: 十五載正月，遷上黨郡長史、特進，攝御史中丞，以兵守上黨。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifteenth year, he was transferred to Senior Administrator of Shangdang Commandery and Special Advancement, acting Vice Censor-in-Chief, holding troops to defend Shangdang.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fifteenth year he was made senior administrator of Shangdang commandery with the rank of special advancement, acting as vice censor-in-chief, and took troops to hold Shangdang.

sentences.zh: 賊來攻城，屢為千里所敗，以功累加開府儀同三司、禮部尚書、兼御史大夫。

translations.literal: When rebels came to attack the city, they were repeatedly defeated by Qianli; for merit he was repeatedly promoted to Generalissimo with the Same Privileges as the Three Excellencies, Minister of Rites, and concurrent Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Each time rebels attacked the city Cheng Qianli drove them back; for these services he was promoted step by step to generalissimo with ceremonial privileges of the Three Excellencies, minister of rites, and concurrent censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 九月，賊將蔡希德圍城，數以輕騎挑戰。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, the rebel general Cai Xide besieged the city, repeatedly challenging with light cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the rebel commander Cai Xide laid siege and sent light cavalry to provoke battle again and again.

sentences.zh: 千里恃其驍果，開懸門，率百騎，欲生擒希德。

translations.literal: Qianli relied on his fierce valor, opened the suspension gate, led a hundred horsemen, and wished to capture Xide alive.
translations.idiomatic: Trusting his own fierce riders, Cheng Qianli opened the drawbridge and led a hundred horsemen out, hoping to take Cai Xide alive.

sentences.zh: 勁騎搏之，垂將擒而希德救兵至，千里斂騎而退，橋壞墜坑，反為希德所執。

translations.literal: Strong horsemen grappled with him; just about to capture him when Xide's rescue troops arrived; Qianli gathered his horses and withdrew; the bridge broke and he fell into a pit, and was instead seized by Xide.
translations.idiomatic: His best riders closed in and nearly had Cai Xide when reinforcements arrived; Cheng Qianli wheeled his men to retreat, but the bridge gave way and he fell into a ditch—and was captured by Xide instead.

sentences.zh: 仰首告諸騎曰：「非吾戰之過，此天也！

translations.literal: Raising his head he told the horsemen: "It is not my fault in battle—this is Heaven!
translations.idiomatic: He looked up and called to his riders: "This was no failure of mine in battle—it was Heaven's will!

sentences.zh: 為我報諸將士，乍可失帥，不可失城。」

translations.literal: For me report to all officers and soldiers: better lose the commander for a moment than lose the city.
translations.idiomatic: Tell the officers and men for me: you may lose your general, but you must not lose the city.

sentences.zh: 軍人聞之泣下，晝夜嚴兵城守，賊竟不能拔。

translations.literal: The soldiers hearing this wept; day and night they strictly manned the city defense, and the rebels ultimately could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison wept at his words; day and night they kept strict guard, and in the end the rebels could not take the city.

sentences.zh: 千里至東都，安慶緒舍之，偽署特進，囚之客省。

translations.literal: Qianli arrived at the Eastern Capital; An Qingxu pardoned him, falsely appointed him Special Advancement, and imprisoned him in the Guest Reception Office.
translations.idiomatic: When Cheng Qianli reached the eastern capital, An Qingxu spared his life, gave him the hollow title of special advancement, and kept him prisoner in the Guest Reception Office.

sentences.zh: 及慶緒敗走，為嚴莊所害。

translations.literal: When Qingxu was defeated and fled, he was killed by Yan Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: When An Qingxu was defeated and fled, Yan Zhuang put him to death.

sentences.zh: 其年十二月，上御丹鳳樓大赦，節文曰：「忠臣事君，有死無貳；

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of that year, the Emperor ascended Danfeng Tower for a general amnesty; the text of the proclamation said: "Loyal ministers serve their ruler—there is death but no second allegiance;
translations.idiomatic: That December the Emperor went to Danfeng Tower and proclaimed a general amnesty whose text read: "A loyal minister serves his sovereign unto death and never wavers in allegiance;

sentences.zh: 烈士徇義，雖歿如存。

translations.literal: Heroic gentlemen follow righteousness; though dead they are as if alive.
translations.idiomatic: A man of principle dies for what is right; though gone, he lives on as if still among us.

sentences.zh: 其李憕、盧奕、袁履謙、張巡、許遠、張介然、蔣清、龐堅等，即與追贈，訪其子孫，厚其官爵，家口深加優恤。」

translations.literal: As for Li Cheng, Lu Yi, Yuan Lüqian, Zhang Xun, Xu Yuan, Zhang Jieran, Jiang Qing, Pang Jian, and others—instantly grant posthumous honors, seek out their descendants, enrich their offices and ranks, and deeply add generous relief for their households.
translations.idiomatic: Li Cheng, Lu Yi, Yuan Lüqian, Zhang Xun, Xu Yuan, Zhang Jieran, Jiang Qing, Pang Jian, and the like shall at once receive posthumous honors; their descendants shall be sought out and granted generous offices and ranks, and their families shall receive deep relief.

sentences.zh: 自是赦恩，無不該於節義，而程千里終以生執賊庭，不霑褒贈。

translations.literal: From this time general amnesty favors invariably covered those of integrity and righteousness, yet Cheng Qianli in the end because he was captured alive in the rebel court did not receive laudatory posthumous gifts.
translations.idiomatic: From then on every act of clemency honored those who had upheld duty and honor—yet Cheng Qianli, because he had been taken alive in the rebel capital, never received posthumous honors.

sentences.zh: 袁光庭袁光庭者，河西戍將，天寶末為伊州刺史。

translations.literal: Yuan Guangting—Yuan Guangting was a garrison general of Hexi; at the end of Tianbao he was Prefect of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Guangting was a frontier commander of Hexi who, near the end of the Tianbao era, served as prefect of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 祿山之亂，西北邊戎兵入赴難，河、隴郡邑，皆為吐蕃所拔。

translations.literal: In the An Lushan rebellion, northwestern frontier soldiers entered to rush to the emergency; the commanderies and districts of He and Long were all seized by Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: When the An Lushan rebellion broke out, frontier troops marched east to answer the throne's call—but the prefectures and districts of He and Long were all overrun by Tibet.

sentences.zh: 唯光庭守伊州累年，外救不至。

translations.literal: Only Guangting held Yizhou for many years; outside relief did not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Only Yuan Guangting held Yizhou for years while no relief came from outside.

sentences.zh: 虜百端誘說，終不之屈，部下如一。

translations.literal: The barbarians by every means enticed and persuaded; in the end he did not submit, and his subordinates were as one.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy tried every persuasion, but he never yielded—and his men stood with him to a man.

sentences.zh: 及矢石既盡，糧儲並竭，城將陷沒，光庭手殺其妻子，自焚而死。

translations.literal: When arrows and stones were already exhausted and grain stores were both depleted, the city was about to fall; Guangting with his own hand killed his wife and children and burned himself to death.
translations.idiomatic: When ammunition and provisions were gone and the city was about to fall, Yuan Guangting killed his wife and children with his own hand and burned himself alive.

sentences.zh: 朝廷聞之，贈工部尚書。

translations.literal: The court hearing of this, posthumously granted Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: When the court learned of this it posthumously made him minister of works.

sentences.zh: 邵真邵真者，恆州節度使李寶臣之判官也。

translations.literal: Shao Zhen—Shao Zhen was the aide to Hengzhou Military Governor Li Baochen.
translations.idiomatic: Shao Zhen served as aide to Li Baochen, military governor of Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 累加檢校司封郎中、兼御史中丞，專掌文翰，寶臣深所信任。

translations.literal: Repeatedly promoted to Acting Director of the Department of Enfeoffment and concurrent Vice Censor-in-Chief, he exclusively managed documents; Baochen deeply trusted him.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to acting director of the Department of Enfeoffment and concurrent vice censor-in-chief, handled all correspondence, and Baochen placed deep trust in him.

sentences.zh: 寶臣死，其子惟嶽擅領父眾。

translations.literal: When Baochen died, his son Weiyue on his own authority took over his father's forces.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Baochen's death his son Weiyue seized command of his father's army on his own authority.

sentences.zh: 李正己、田悅遣人說惟嶽同叛，真泣諫曰：「先公位兼將相，受國厚恩，大夫缞绖之中，遽欲違命，同鄰道之惡，違先公之志，必不可也！

translations.literal: Li Zhengyi and Tian Yue sent men to persuade Weiyue to rebel together; Zhen wept and remonstrated, saying: "Your late father held positions combining general and minister, receiving the state's thick grace; the great officer, in the midst of hempen mourning garb, hastening wishes to disobey orders, together with the evil of neighboring circuits, violating your late father's will—it absolutely cannot be done!
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhengyi and Tian Yue sent envoys urging Weiyue to join them in rebellion. Shao Zhen wept as he remonstrated: "Your father held both military and civil rank and received the deepest favors from the throne. You are still in mourning—how can you think of defying the court, joining the wicked neighbors, and betraying your father's wishes? You must not do this!

sentences.zh: 田悅與我密邇，絕之又恐速禍；

translations.literal: Tian Yue is close to us in secret proximity; cutting him off again fears hastening disaster;
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yue's territory borders ours—if we break with him outright we may bring disaster on ourselves too quickly;

sentences.zh: 正己稍遠，絕之易耳。

translations.literal: Zhengyi is somewhat distant; cutting him off is easy.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhengyi is farther away; breaking with him would be the easier choice.

sentences.zh: 但令悅使還報，請徐思其宜；

translations.literal: Only order Yue's envoy to return reporting, asking to slowly consider what is fitting;
translations.idiomatic: Simply have Tian Yue's envoy go back and report that we need time to weigh the matter;

sentences.zh: 執正己使送京師，因請致討，朝廷必嘉大夫之忠，而旌節可得。」

translations.literal: Detain Zhengyi's envoy and send him to the capital, and thereby request dispatching a punitive campaign—the court will surely praise the great officer's loyalty, and the command baton can be obtained."
translations.idiomatic: hold Li Zhengyi's envoy and send him to the capital, then ask the court to march against him. The throne is sure to reward your loyalty, and you may win official confirmation of your command."

sentences.zh: 惟嶽然之，令真草奏。

translations.literal: Weiyue agreed and ordered Zhen to draft the memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Weiyue accepted this and told Shao Zhen to draft the memorial.

sentences.zh: 將發，孔目吏胡震謂惟嶽曰：「此事非細，請與將吏會議。」

translations.literal: About to send it off, the chief clerk Hu Zhen said to Weiyue: "This matter is no small thing; please meet with the generals and officials to discuss it."
translations.idiomatic: Before the dispatch could go out, the chief clerk Hu Zhen told Weiyue: "This is no small matter—consult the officers first."

sentences.zh: 長史畢華曰：「先公與二道親好，二十餘年，一朝背之，伏恐生事。

translations.literal: Chief Administrator Bi Hua said: "Your late father had close friendship with the two circuits for more than twenty years; in one morning turning against them—I submit fearing trouble will arise.
translations.idiomatic: Chief administrator Bi Hua said: "Your father maintained close ties with both circuits for more than twenty years. To turn on them overnight may well provoke trouble.

sentences.zh: 今執其來使，送於京師，大善。

translations.literal: Now detaining their arriving envoy and sending him to the capital—very good.
translations.idiomatic: Detaining the envoy from Li Zhengyi and sending him to the capital—that would be excellent.

sentences.zh: 脫未為朝廷所信，正己兵強，忽來襲城，孤軍無援，何以敵之？

translations.literal: If not yet trusted by the court, and Zhengyi's troops are strong, suddenly coming to attack the city—a lone army without relief—how can one oppose them?
translations.idiomatic: But if the court does not yet trust you, and Li Zhengyi's armies are strong enough to strike without warning, how could an isolated garrison hold out?

sentences.zh: 不若仍舊勿絕，徐觀其變。」

translations.literal: Better still maintain the old connections without breaking off, slowly observing their changes."
translations.idiomatic: Better to keep the old ties for now and watch how things develop."

sentences.zh: 惟嶽又從之。

translations.literal: Weiyue again followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Weiyue again went along with this.

sentences.zh: 真又勸惟嶽遣其弟惟簡入朝，仍遣軍吏薛廣嗣詣河東節度馬燧軍求保薦。

translations.literal: Zhen again urged Weiyue to send his younger brother Weijian to court, and still send military officer Xue Guangsi to Hedong Military Governor Ma Sui's army seeking protection and recommendation.
translations.idiomatic: Shao Zhen again urged Weiyue to send his younger brother Weijian to court and dispatch the staff officer Xue Guangsi to Ma Sui's army in Hedong to seek protection and a court recommendation.

sentences.zh: 田悅屯兵束鹿，聞其謀，遣人謂惟嶽曰：「邵真惑亂軍政，必速殺之。

translations.literal: Tian Yue stationed troops at Shulu, heard of this plan, sent a man to tell Weiyue: "Shao Zhen is confusing and disordering military governance—you must quickly kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yue, encamped at Shulu, learned of the scheme and sent word to Weiyue: "Shao Zhen is sowing discord in your command—kill him at once.

sentences.zh: 不然，吾且討其罪矣。」

translations.literal: If not, I will soon punish his crime."
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise I shall move against you for his offense."

sentences.zh: 惟嶽懼，遂殺真。

translations.literal: Weiyue feared and then killed Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Weiyue had Shao Zhen put to death.

sentences.zh: 朝廷聞而嘉之，贈戶部尚書。

translations.literal: The court hearing of this praised him and posthumously granted Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: When the court learned what had happened it honored Shao Zhen's loyalty and posthumously made him minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 符璘符璘者，田悅之將。

translations.literal: Fu Lin—Fu Lin was Tian Yue's general.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Lin was one of Tian Yue's generals.

sentences.zh: 初，馬燧、李抱真、李芃等破田悅於洹水，燧等進屯魏州。

translations.literal: Initially, Ma Sui, Li Baozhen, Li Kang, and others defeated Tian Yue at Huan River; Sui and the others advanced and encamped at Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Ma Sui, Li Baozhen, and Li Kang had defeated Tian Yue at Huan River; Ma Sui and his allies then pushed forward and encamped at Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 時悅與李納會於濮陽，因請助兵，納分麾下數千人隨之。

translations.literal: At that time Yue met with Li Na at Puyang, and therefore requested auxiliary troops; Na divided several thousand men under his command to follow him.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yue was then meeting Li Na at Puyang and asked for reinforcements; Li Na detached several thousand men to accompany him.

sentences.zh: 至是納為河南諸軍所逼，自濮陽奔歸濮州，征兵於悅，悅遣璘將三百騎護送之。

translations.literal: At this time Na was pressed by the various armies of Henan, from Puyang fled and returned to Puzhou, requisitioned troops from Yue, and Yue sent Lin leading three hundred horsemen to escort them.
translations.idiomatic: By then Li Na was hard pressed by the Henan armies, fled from Puyang back to Puzhou, and called on Tian Yue for troops; Yue sent Fu Lin with three hundred horsemen to escort them.

sentences.zh: 納兵既歸，遂悉其眾降於燧。

translations.literal: When Na's troops had already returned, then he turned over all his masses in surrender to Sui.
translations.idiomatic: After escorting Li Na's men safely back, Fu Lin surrendered his entire command to Ma Sui.

sentences.zh: 遷璘試太子詹事、兼御史中丞，封義陽郡王，實封一百戶。

translations.literal: Lin was transferred to Acting Household Companion of the Heir Apparent and concurrent Vice Censor-in-Chief, enfeoffed as Prince of Yiyang Commandery, with a fief of one hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Lin was appointed acting household companion of the heir apparent and concurrent vice censor-in-chief, and enfeoffed as prince of Yiyang commandery with a fief of one hundred households.

sentences.zh: 璘父令奇，初為悅部將，至是因璘之出，遂令三子同降於燧。

translations.literal: Lin's father Lingqi, initially was Yue's departmental general; reaching this time because of Lin's departure, then ordered his three sons together to surrender to Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Lin's father Lingqi had been one of Tian Yue's officers; when his son defected he sent his three remaining sons to surrender to Ma Sui as well.

sentences.zh: 悅怒，執令奇，令奇大呼慢罵之，悅族其家。

translations.literal: Yue was angry, seized Lingqi; Lingqi shouted loudly and reviled him; Yue executed his entire family.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yue, enraged, seized Lingqi, who loudly cursed him; Yue had his whole family put to death.

sentences.zh: 贈令奇戶部尚書。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Lingqi Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: The court posthumously made Lingqi minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 趙曄趙曄，字雲卿，鄧州穰人，其先自天水徙焉。

translations.literal: Zhao Ye—Zhao Ye, courtesy name Yunqing, a man of Rang in Dengzhou; his forebears had moved there from Tianshui.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Ye, courtesy name Yunqing, was a native of Rang in Deng prefecture; his family had moved there from Tianshui.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，主客員外郎德言曾孫也。

translations.literal: In the Zhenguan era, he was the great-grandson of Master of Guests Vice Director Deyan.
translations.idiomatic: He was the great-grandson of Deyan, who had served as vice director in the Ministry of Rites during the Zhenguan era.

sentences.zh: 父敬先，殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: Father Jingxian, Palace Attendant Censor.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jingxian had been a palace attendant censor.

sentences.zh: 曄志學，善屬文。

translations.literal: Ye aspirated to learning and was skilled at composing literature.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Ye devoted himself to scholarship and wrote well.

sentences.zh: 開元中，舉進士，連擢科第，補太子正字，累授大理評事，貶北陽尉，移雷澤、河東二丞。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan era, he passed the jinshi examination, continuously advanced in examinations, was appointed Collator of the Heir Apparent, repeatedly received Senior Reviser of the Court of Judicial Review, was demoted to Beiyang Magistrate, and transferred to magistrate of Leize and Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: During Kaiyuan he earned his jinshi degree, rose through successive postings, became collator to the heir apparent, served repeatedly as senior reviser in the Court of Judicial Review, was demoted to magistrate of Beiyang, and later served as magistrate of Leize and Hedong.

sentences.zh: 河東采訪使韋陟以曄履操清直，頗推敬之，表為賓僚。

translations.literal: Hedong Investigating Commissioner Wei Zhi because Ye's conduct and integrity were pure and straight greatly promoted and respected him, memorializing him as a guest aide.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhi, investigating commissioner of Hedong, greatly respected Zhao Ye for his upright character and recommended him as a staff aide.

sentences.zh: 陟罷，陳留采訪使郭納復奏曄為支使。

translations.literal: When Zhi was dismissed, Chenliu Investigating Commissioner Guo Na again memorialized Ye as branch secretary.
translations.idiomatic: After Wei Zhi left office, Guo Na, investigating commissioner of Chenliu, recommended Zhao Ye as branch secretary.

sentences.zh: 及安祿山陷陳留，因沒於賊。

translations.literal: When An Lushan took Chenliu, thereby he was captured by rebels.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan captured Chenliu, Zhao Ye fell into rebel hands.

sentences.zh: 時有京兆韋氏，夫任畿官，以不供賊軍遇害，韋被逆賊沒入為婢。

translations.literal: At that time there was a woman of the Wei clan of Jingzhao; her husband held a capital-district office, and because he did not supply the rebel army was killed; Wei was seized by the rebel bandits and made a maidservant.
translations.idiomatic: There was then a woman of the Wei clan of the capital region whose husband, a metropolitan official, had been killed for refusing to supply the rebels; she herself was seized and made a slave.

sentences.zh: 江西觀察使韋儇，族兄弟也。

translations.literal: Jiangxi Observation Commissioner Wei Tong, a clansman, was her clansman brother.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Tong, observation commissioner of Jiangxi, was her kinsman.

sentences.zh: 曄哀其冤抑，以錢贖之，俾其妻置之別院，厚供衣食，而曄竟不面其人。

translations.literal: Ye pitied her wrongful oppression, used money to redeem her, had his wife place her in a separate courtyard, generously supplied clothing and food, yet Ye ultimately did not face that person.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Ye, pitying her plight, paid to ransom her; his wife housed her in a separate courtyard and saw that she was well provided for—yet Zhao Ye himself never sought to meet her.

sentences.zh: 明年，收復東都，曄以家財資給，而訪其親屬歸之，識者咸重焉。

translations.literal: The next year, the Eastern Capital was recovered; Ye used family wealth to supply and on behalf of her sought her relatives and returned her to them; those who knew all respected this.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, after the eastern capital was recovered, Zhao Ye drew on his family's resources to help locate her kin and restore her to them—an act widely admired.

sentences.zh: 乾元初，三司議罪，貶晉江尉。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianyuan, the Three Departments deliberated on crimes and demoted him to magistrate of Jinjiang.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Qianyuan era the Three Departments reviewed his case and demoted him to magistrate of Jinjiang.

sentences.zh: 數年，改錄事參軍。

translations.literal: After several years, he was changed to recording secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later he became recording secretary.

sentences.zh: 征拜左補闕，未至。

translations.literal: Summoned and appointed Left Reminder; he did not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to serve as left reminder but never took up the post.

sentences.zh: 福建觀察使李承昭奏為判官，授試大理司直、兼監察御史。

translations.literal: Fujian Observation Commissioner Li Chengzhao memorialized him as aide, appointing Acting Senior Directing Secretary of the Court of Judicial Review and concurrent Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chengzhao, observation commissioner of Fujian, recommended him as aide, with the titles of acting senior directing secretary in the Court of Judicial Review and concurrent investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 試司議郎、兼殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: Acting Guiding Censor and concurrent Palace Attendant Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was also acting guiding censor and concurrent palace attendant censor.

sentences.zh: 入為膳部、比部二員外，膳部、倉部二郎中，秘書少監。

translations.literal: Entered office as two Vice Directors of the Board of Revisions and the Board of Justice; two Directors of the Board of Revisions and the Board of Granaries; and Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He then served in the capital as vice director of both the Board of Revisions and the Board of Justice, director of the Board of Revisions and the Board of Granaries, and vice director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 曄性孝悌，敦重交友，雖經艱危，不改其操。

translations.literal: Ye's nature was filial and fraternal, solid and heavy in befriending others; though passing through hardship and peril, he did not change his conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Ye was filial and devoted to his brothers, steadfast in friendship, and did not alter his principles even through years of hardship.

sentences.zh: 少時與殷寅、顏真卿、柳芳、陸據、蕭穎士、李華、邵軫、同志友善，故天寶中語曰：「殷、顏、柳、陸、蕭、李、邵、趙」，以其重行義，敦交道也。

translations.literal: In youth he was with Yin Yin, Yan Zhenqing, Liu Fang, Lu Ju, Xiao Yingshi, Li Hua, Shao Zuan, and others of one aspiration and friendly; therefore in the Tianbao era the saying went: "Yin, Yan, Liu, Lu, Xiao, Li, Shao, Zhao"—because they valued conduct and righteousness and were solid in social relations.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he was close to Yin Yin, Yan Zhenqing, Liu Fang, Lu Ju, Xiao Yingshi, Li Hua, Shao Zuan, and others who shared his ideals; hence the Tianbao saying "Yin, Yan, Liu, Lu, Xiao, Li, Shao, Zhao"—a roll call of men known for integrity and loyal friendship.

sentences.zh: 而曄早擅高名，在宦途五十年，累經貶謫，蹇躓備至。

translations.literal: Yet Ye early possessed high reputation; on the official path for fifty years, repeatedly passing demotion and exile, obstruction and stumbling reached completeness.
