translations.idiomatic: Yet Zhao Ye had won renown early; over fifty years in official life he was demoted again and again and met every kind of setback.

sentences.zh: 入仕三十年，方霑省官，身在郎署，子常徒步。

translations.literal: Entering office thirty years, only then touched provincial-level office; his person was in the secretariat bureau, his son often walked on foot.
translations.idiomatic: After thirty years of service he finally reached a provincial post; while he held a secretariat position, his son often went about on foot.

sentences.zh: 官既散曹，俸祿單寡，衣食不充，以至亡歿，服名檢者為之嘆息。

translations.literal: His office was a scattered department, stipend and salary single and meager, clothing and food not sufficient, reaching until death; those observing reputation all sighed for this.
translations.idiomatic: He held only minor posts with scant pay; he could not fully clothe and feed his household, and died in that condition—men who cared about integrity mourned him for it.

sentences.zh: 建中四年冬，涇原兵叛，曄竄於山谷。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jianzhong, winter, Jingyuan troops rebelled; Ye fled into mountain valleys.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the fourth year of Jianzhong, when the Jingyuan garrison mutinied, Zhao Ye took refuge in the mountains.

sentences.zh: 尋以疾終，追贈華州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon afterward because of illness he ended, posthumously granted Prefect of Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died of illness, and the court posthumously named him prefect of Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 子宗儒，別有傳。

translations.literal: His son Zongru has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zongru is treated in a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 石演芬石演芬，本西城胡人也。

translations.literal: Shi Yanfen—Shi Yanfen was originally a Hu man from the Western Regions.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Yanfen was a foreigner from the western borderlands.

sentences.zh: 以武勇為朔方邠寧節度兵馬使、兼御史大夫。

translations.literal: For military valor he served as Military Affairs Commissioner of the Shuofang-Binning Military Governor, concurrent Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: His martial prowess earned him appointment as troop commissioner under the Shuofang-Binning command, with the concurrent title of censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 李懷光養為子，累至右武鋒都將。

translations.literal: Li Huaiguang adopted him as a son; he rose to Right Martial Vanguard Commander.
translations.idiomatic: Li Huaiguang took him in as an adopted son, and he eventually became commander of the Right Martial Vanguard.

sentences.zh: 時懷光軍屯三橋，將與硃泚通謀。

translations.literal: At that time Huaiguang's army encamped at Sanqiao, about to conspire with Zhu Ci.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Huaiguang's forces were camped at Sanqiao and were on the verge of colluding with Zhu Ci.

sentences.zh: 演芬乃使門客郜成義密疏，具言懷光無狀，請罷其總統。

translations.literal: Yanfen then had his retainer Gao Chengyi submit a secret memorial, fully stating Huaiguang's impropriety and requesting removal of his supreme command.
translations.idiomatic: Yanfen dispatched his retainer Gao Chengyi with a secret memorial detailing Huaiguang's misconduct and urging that his overall command be revoked.

sentences.zh: 成義至奉天，乃反以其言告懷光子琟，琟密告其父。

translations.literal: Chengyi reached Fengtian, then instead turned and told Huaiguang's son Wei what had been said; Wei secretly informed his father.
translations.idiomatic: When Chengyi reached Fengtian he reversed himself, reporting Yanfen's words to Huaiguang's son Wei, who in turn secretly told his father.

sentences.zh: 懷光乃召演芬責之曰：「以爾為子，奈何欲破我家！

translations.literal: Huaiguang then summoned Yanfen and rebuked him, saying: "I took you as a son—how dare you seek to destroy my household!
translations.idiomatic: Huaiguang summoned Yanfen and rebuked him: "I raised you as my own son—how could you seek to ruin my house?

sentences.zh: 今死可乎？」

translations.literal: Now are you ready to die?"
translations.idiomatic: Are you ready to die now?

sentences.zh: 演芬對曰：「天子以公為腹心，公上負天子，安可責演芬！

translations.literal: Yanfen replied: "The Son of Heaven takes you as his trusted heart—you betrayed the Son of Heaven above; how can you blame Yanfen!
translations.idiomatic: Yanfen answered: "The Emperor trusted you as his own confidant, yet you betray him. How can you blame me for that!

sentences.zh: 且演芬胡人，不解異心，欲守事一人，幸免呼為賊。

translations.literal: Moreover Yanfen is a Hu man, not understanding divided loyalty; he wishes to serve only one person and merely escape being called a rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, I am a foreigner with no taste for treachery—I wanted to serve one master alone and avoid being called a traitor.

sentences.zh: 死，常分也！」

translations.literal: Death is one's allotted portion!"
translations.idiomatic: Death is only what every man must accept!

sentences.zh: 懷光使左右臠食之，皆曰：「此忠烈士也！

translations.literal: Huaiguang had his attendants cut him into pieces; all said: "This is a loyal martyr!
translations.idiomatic: Huaiguang ordered his men to hack him to pieces, but they all protested: "This man is a loyal martyr!

sentences.zh: 可令速死。」

translations.literal: Let him die quickly."
translations.idiomatic: At least let him die swiftly.

sentences.zh: 乃以刀斷其頸。

translations.literal: Then with a blade they cut through his neck.
translations.idiomatic: They then severed his neck with a blade.

sentences.zh: 德宗追思義烈，贈兵部尚書，仍賜錢三百千。

translations.literal: Emperor Dezong recalled his righteous valor, posthumously granted Minister of War, and still bestowed three hundred strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong, moved by his loyalty and courage, posthumously made him minister of war and granted three hundred strings of cash to his estate.

sentences.zh: 又捕得郜成義於朔方，戮之。

translations.literal: Again they captured Gao Chengyi in Shuofang and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Chengyi was later captured in Shuofang and put to death.

sentences.zh: 附 張名振先是，詔賜懷光鐵券。

translations.literal: Appendix: Zhang Mingzhen. First, an edict bestowed on Huaiguang an iron certificate.
translations.idiomatic: Appendix: Zhang Mingzhen. Earlier, an edict had granted Li Huaiguang an iron certificate of pardon.

sentences.zh: 懷光奉詔倨慢，左都將張名振大呼軍門曰：「太尉見賊不擊，天使到不迎，固將反耶！

translations.literal: Huaiguang received the edict with arrogance and disrespect; Left Vanguard Commander Zhang Mingzhen shouted at the army gate: "Grand Marshal, seeing rebels and not striking, when the imperial envoy arrives not receiving—surely you intend to rebel!
translations.idiomatic: Huaiguang received the edict with insolent disregard. Left vanguard commander Zhang Mingzhen shouted at the camp gate: "Grand Marshal, you refuse to fight the rebels and will not even receive the imperial envoy—do you mean to rebel after all?

sentences.zh: 且安史兩賊，僕固懷恩，今皆族滅，公欲何為？

translations.literal: Moreover the An and Shi two rebels, Pugu Huai'en—now all have had their clans extinguished; what do you intend?
translations.idiomatic: The rebel leaders An, Shi, and Pugu Huai'en have all been destroyed root and branch—what do you hope to accomplish?

sentences.zh: 是資忠義之士立功勛耳！」

translations.literal: This is simply providing loyal and righteous men the opportunity to establish merit!"
translations.idiomatic: You would only be giving loyal men their chance to win merit in battle!

sentences.zh: 懷光聞之，召謂曰：「我不反，為賊強盛，須蓄銳俟時耳。」

translations.literal: Huaiguang hearing this, summoned him and said: "I am not rebelling; because the rebels are strong and flourishing, I must store sharpness and wait for the time."
translations.idiomatic: Huaiguang heard this and summoned him, saying: "I am not rebelling—the rebels are too strong; I must keep my forces rested and bide my time.

sentences.zh: 無幾，懷光引軍入咸陽，名振曰：「公乃言不反，今此來何也？

translations.literal: Before long, Huaiguang led his army into Xianyang; Mingzhen said: "You just said you would not rebel—what is this march for?
translations.idiomatic: Before long Huaiguang marched into Xianyang. Mingzhen said: "You said you would not rebel—then why have you come here?

sentences.zh: 何不急攻硃泚，收復京城，以圖富貴？」

translations.literal: Why not urgently attack Zhu Ci, recover the capital, and seek wealth and rank?"
translations.idiomatic: Why not strike at Zhu Ci at once, retake the capital, and win wealth and honors?

sentences.zh: 懷光曰：「名振病狂。」

translations.literal: Huaiguang said: "Mingzhen is madly ill."
translations.idiomatic: Huaiguang said: "Mingzhen has gone mad.

sentences.zh: 使左右殺之。

translations.literal: He had his attendants kill him.
translations.idiomatic: He had his men put Mingzhen to death.

sentences.zh: 張伾張伾，建中初，以澤潞將鎮臨洺。

translations.literal: Zhang Pi—Zhang Pi, at the beginning of Jianzhong, as a Ze-Lu general garrisoned Linming.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Pi, at the start of the Jianzhong era, was a Ze-Lu commander holding Linming.

sentences.zh: 田悅攻之，伾度兵力不能出戰，嚴設守備，嬰城拒守，賊不能拔。

translations.literal: Tian Yue attacked him; Pi judged his military force could not go out to battle, strictly established defenses, tied himself to the city and resisted; the rebels could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yue attacked him. Judging his forces too weak to meet the enemy in the field, Zhang Pi tightened the defenses and held the city; the rebels could not breach it.

sentences.zh: 累月，攻之益急，士多死傷，糧儲漸乏，救兵未至。

translations.literal: Month after month, the attack grew more urgent; many soldiers died and were wounded, grain stores gradually ran short, and relief troops had not arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Month after month the siege intensified; casualties mounted, provisions dwindled, and no relief came.

sentences.zh: 伾知事不濟，無以激士心，乃悉召將卒於軍門，命其女出拜之，謂曰：「將士辛苦守戰，伾之家無尺寸物與公等，獨有此女，幸未嫁人，願出賣之，為將士一日之費。」

translations.literal: Pi knew affairs would not succeed and had no means to stir the soldiers' hearts; he then fully summoned generals and soldiers at the army gate, ordered his daughter to come out and bow to them, and said: "Officers and soldiers toil in bitter defense; Pi's household has not a foot's breadth of goods to share with you—all I have is this daughter, fortunately not yet married; I wish to sell her out to be one day's expense for the officers and soldiers."
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that all was lost and unable to rouse his men's morale by any other means, Zhang Pi assembled his officers and soldiers at the camp gate and had his daughter come forward to bow to them. He said: "You have fought hard to hold this city, and I have nothing in my house to give you but this unmarried daughter. I would sell her, if need be, to pay for one day's rations for the army.

sentences.zh: 眾皆大哭，曰：「誓為將軍死戰，幸無慮也！」

translations.literal: The crowd all wept greatly, saying: "We swear to fight to the death for the general—be assured, have no worries!"
translations.idiomatic: The men wept aloud and cried: "We swear to fight to the death for you, General—set your mind at ease!

sentences.zh: 會馬燧與太原之師至，與眾合擊悅於城下，大敗之。

translations.literal: It happened that Ma Sui and the troops from Taiyuan arrived; together with the crowd they jointly struck Yue below the city walls and greatly defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Ma Sui arrived with the Taiyuan army; joining with Zhang Pi's garrison they routed Tian Yue beneath the walls.

sentences.zh: 伾乘勢出戰，士卒無不一當百。

translations.literal: Pi riding the momentum went out to battle; among the officers and soldiers none was not one against a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Pi seized the moment and led a sortie; every man fought as if worth a hundred.

sentences.zh: 圍解，以功遷泗州刺史。

translations.literal: The siege was relieved; for merit he was transferred to Prefect of Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the siege was lifted he was promoted to prefect of Sizhou for his service.

sentences.zh: 在州十餘年，拜右金吾衛大將軍。

translations.literal: At the prefecture for more than ten years, he was appointed Grand General of the Right Gold Crow Guard.
translations.idiomatic: After more than ten years in office he was made grand general of the Right Gold Crow Guard.

sentences.zh: 詔未至，病卒。

translations.literal: The edict had not yet arrived when he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Before the appointment reached him he died of illness.

sentences.zh: ，贈尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: [He was] posthumously granted Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The court posthumously made him right vice director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 有子重政，軍吏欲立為郡將，重政母徐氏固拒不從。

translations.literal: He had a son Chongzheng; the military officers wished to install him as district commander, but Chongzheng's mother Lady Xu firmly refused and would not consent.
translations.idiomatic: He had a son, Chongzheng, whom the officers wished to install as military governor; his mother, Lady Xu, steadfastly refused.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「前昭義軍泗州行營衙前兵馬使、大中大夫、試太子賓客、兼監察御史張重政，門有勛力，惟推義勇。

translations.literal: The edict said: "Former Zhaoyi Army Sizhou Field Headquarters Yamen Vanguard Military Affairs Commissioner, Grand Master of Palace Attendance, Acting Guest of the Heir Apparent, concurrent Investigating Censor Zhang Chongzheng—his family has martial merit, he alone promotes righteous courage.
translations.idiomatic: An edict read: "Zhang Chongzheng, former vanguard military affairs commissioner of the Zhaoyi Army's Sizhou campaign headquarters, grand master of palace attendance, acting guest of the heir apparent, and concurrent investigating censor, comes from a family of military service and is known above all for righteous courage.

sentences.zh: 夙聞克家之美，常稱撫眾之才。

translations.literal: Long heard of the beauty of mastering the household, constantly praised for the talent of comforting the masses.
translations.idiomatic: He has long been known for upholding his family's honor and for his gift in winning the loyalty of troops.

sentences.zh: 近者其父初亡，群小扇惑，誘以奇計，俾執軍麾。

translations.literal: Recently his father had just died; petty men fanned and deluded, enticing with strange schemes, causing him to grasp the military banner.
translations.idiomatic: When his father had just died, lesser men tried to sway him with reckless schemes and urged him to seize military command.

sentences.zh: 而重政與其母兄，號泣固拒，遂全懇願，奔告元戎，不為利回，成其先志。

translations.literal: Yet Chongzheng together with his mother and elder brother, weeping and wailing firmly refused; then fully preserved earnest wish, ran to report to the supreme commander, was not turned by profit, and fulfilled his late father's will.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Chongzheng, weeping, refused together with his mother and elder brother, kept his father's loyal intent intact, reported to the commanding general, and would not be swayed by self-interest.

sentences.zh: 於家為孝子，在國為忠臣，軍政乂安，行義昭著。

translations.literal: In the household he was a filial son, in the state a loyal minister; military governance was well ordered and peaceful, conduct and righteousness clearly manifest.
translations.idiomatic: Filial at home and loyal to the throne, he kept the command stable and made his integrity plain for all to see.

sentences.zh: 念茲名節，感嘆良深，宜洽恩榮，俾弘激勸。

translations.literal: Reflecting on this reputation and integrity, sighing deeply, it is fitting to extend favor and glory, causing encouragement to be broadly stirred.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by such integrity, We should bestow honors upon him and hold him up as an example to others.

sentences.zh: 禮無避於金革，理當由於權奪，戎章憲府，式示兼崇。

translations.literal: In ritual there is no avoidance on account of arms and armor; principle ought to follow expedient suspension of mourning; military insignia and censorial office together display dual elevation.
translations.idiomatic: Custom does not excuse a man from service because he is in mourning; necessity may override filial observance, and both military rank and censorial office shall mark his dual distinction.

sentences.zh: 可起復雲麾將軍，守金吾衛大將軍、員外置同正員，檢校太子詹事、兼御史中丞，仍委淮南節度使與要職事任使。」

translations.literal: He may be recalled from mourning as Cloud Banner General, holding Grand General of the Gold Crow Guard as supernumerary appointee with full standing, Acting Household Companion of the Heir Apparent and concurrent Vice Censor-in-Chief, still entrusted to the Huainan Military Governor for important duties and assignment."
translations.idiomatic: He is hereby recalled from mourning as cloud-banner general, appointed grand general of the Gold Crow Guard with full standing, acting household companion of the heir apparent and concurrent vice censor-in-chief, and entrusted to the Huainan military governor for important assignments."

translations.literal: [The edict closes.]

sentences.zh: 又詔曰：「張重政母高平郡夫人徐氏，族茂姻閥，行表柔明，懷正家之美，有擇鄰之識。

translations.literal: Again the edict said: "Zhang Chongzheng's mother, Lady Xu of Gaoping Commandery, her clan flourishing in marriage alliances, conduct displaying gentleness and clarity, cherishing the beauty of rectifying the household, possessing the discernment of choosing neighbors.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict read: "Lady Xu of Gaoping commandery, mother of Zhang Chongzheng, comes from an eminent family, conducts herself with gentle wisdom, upholds the virtues of a well-ordered home, and shows the judgment of one who chooses her company with care.

sentences.zh: 頃當變故，曾不詭隨，保其門宗，訓成忠孝，雖圖史所載，何以加之！

translations.literal: Recently facing sudden change, never once deviating or following along, she preserved her clan and lineage, instructed and completed loyalty and filial piety—though histories and annals record such things, how could one add to this!
translations.idiomatic: When crisis came she never wavered, preserved her family line, and reared her son in loyalty and filial duty—deeds that histories praise, yet scarcely surpass what she has done!

sentences.zh: 念其令子，已申獎用，特彰母儀之德，俾崇封國之榮。

translations.literal: Reflecting on her worthy son, already declared for reward and employment, specially manifest the virtue of maternal example, causing elevation of enfeoffment and state glory.
translations.idiomatic: Her worthy son has already been honored; now let her maternal virtue be proclaimed and ennobled with a state rank.

sentences.zh: 可封魯國太夫人。」

translations.literal: She may be enfeoffed as Grand Lady of Lu State."
translations.idiomatic: She is hereby ennobled as grand lady of Lu.

sentences.zh: 甄濟甄濟，字孟成，中山無極人，家於衛州。

translations.literal: Zhen Ji—Zhen Ji, courtesy name Mengcheng, a man of Wuji in Zhongshan, his household in Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen Ji, courtesy name Mengcheng, was a native of Wuji in Zhongshan who made his home in Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 少孤，天寶中隱居衛州青巖山。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, in the Tianbao era he lived in seclusion on Qingyan Mountain in Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned in youth, he withdrew during the Tianbao era to Qingyan Mountain in Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 人伏其操行，約不畋漁。

translations.literal: People submitted to his conduct and integrity; he pledged not to hunt or fish.
translations.idiomatic: People respected his upright character, and he bound himself never to hunt or fish.

sentences.zh: 采訪使安祿山表薦之，授試大理評事，充范陽郡節度掌記。

translations.literal: Investigating Commissioner An Lushan memorialized recommending him; he was appointed Acting Senior Reviser of the Court of Judicial Review, serving as Fan Yang Commandery Military Governor's secretary.
translations.idiomatic: An Lushan, as investigating commissioner, recommended him; he was made acting senior reviser in the Court of Judicial Review and secretary to the Fan Yang military governor.

sentences.zh: 天寶末，安祿山有異志，謀以智免。

translations.literal: At the end of Tianbao, An Lushan had divergent intentions; Ji plotted to escape by wisdom.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Tianbao era, when An Lushan revealed rebellious ambitions, Zhen Ji sought a way to extricate himself by wit.

sentences.zh: 衛縣令齊玘誠信可託，乃求使至衛，具以誠告。

translations.literal: Weixian Magistrate Qi Chi's sincerity and trustworthiness could be entrusted; he then requested assignment to Wei and fully told him the truth.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate Qi Chi of Wei county was a man he could trust, so he asked to be sent there and confided the whole truth to him.

sentences.zh: 弟憕密求羊血以為備，至夜，偽嘔血疾不能支，遂舁歸。

translations.literal: Younger brother Cheng secretly sought sheep's blood as preparation; when night came, he feigned vomiting blood and illness unable to endure, and was then carried back.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Cheng secretly obtained sheep's blood as a precaution; that night Ji pretended to vomit blood and collapse, and was carried home.

sentences.zh: 及祿山反，使偽節度使蔡希德領行戮者李掞等二人，封刀來召，察濟詐不起，即就戮之。

translations.literal: When Lushan rebelled, he sent false Military Governor Cai Xide leading executioners Li Yan and two others, sealed blade coming to summon; observing Ji's deception he would not rise, and immediately proceeded to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: When Lushan rebelled he sent the puppet governor Cai Xide with the executioner Li Yan and two others, blades sealed in their summons. Seeing through Ji's ruse, they moved at once to kill him.

sentences.zh: 濟以左手書云：「去不得！」

translations.literal: Ji with his left hand wrote, saying: "Cannot go!"
translations.idiomatic: Ji wrote with his left hand: "I cannot go!

sentences.zh: 李掞持刀而前，濟引首以待，希德歔欷嗟嘆之，曰：「李掞退。」

translations.literal: Li Yan took the blade and advanced; Ji extended his neck to await it; Xide sighed and lamented, saying: "Li Yan, withdraw."
translations.idiomatic: Li Yan stepped forward with his blade drawn, and Ji bared his neck to receive it. Xide sighed in dismay and said: "Li Yan, stand back.

sentences.zh: 以實病報祿山。

translations.literal: He reported to Lushan that the illness was real.
translations.idiomatic: He reported to Lushan that Ji was genuinely ill.

sentences.zh: 後安慶緒亦使人至縣，強舁至東都安國觀。

translations.literal: Later An Qingxu also sent men to the county, forcibly carrying him to Anguo Abbey in the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Later An Qingxu also sent men to the county and had him forcibly taken to Anguo Abbey in the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 經月餘，代宗收東京。

translations.literal: After more than a month, Emperor Daizong recovered the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: More than a month later Emperor Daizong retook the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 濟起，詣軍門上謁，乃送上都。

translations.literal: Ji arose, went to the army gate to pay respects, and was then sent up to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen Ji got up, presented himself at the army gate, and was sent on to the capital.

sentences.zh: 肅宗館之於三司使，令受偽命官瞻望，以愧其心。

translations.literal: Emperor Suzong lodged him at the Three Departments office, ordering those who had received false appointments to look upon him, to shame their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Suzong housed him at the Three Departments office and had officials who had accepted appointments under the rebels come to see him, that they might feel shame.

sentences.zh: 授秘書郎，轉太子舍人。

translations.literal: He was appointed Secretariat Gentleman, transferred to Household Companion of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was made a secretariat gentleman and later household companion to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 寶應初，拜刑部員外郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Baoying, he was appointed Vice Director of the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Baoying era he was appointed vice director in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 魏少遊奏授著作郎、兼侍御史，終於襄州。

translations.literal: Wei Shaoyou memorialized appointing him Compilation Gentleman and concurrent Attendant Censor; he ended his life in Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shaoyou recommended him as compilation gentleman and concurrent attendant censor; he died in Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 元和中，襄州節度使袁滋奏其節行，詔曰：「符風樹節，謂之立名；

translations.literal: In the Yuanhe era, Xiangzhou Military Governor Yuan Zi memorialized his integrity and conduct; the edict said: "Upholding the wind and planting integrity—this is called establishing a name;
translations.idiomatic: During Yuanhe, Yuan Zi, military governor of Xiangzhou, memorialized Zhen Ji's integrity, and an edict read: "To uphold principle and establish one's character is to make a lasting name;

sentences.zh: 歿加褒贈，所以誘善。

translations.literal: After death adding laudatory posthumous gifts—this is how one leads toward goodness.
translations.idiomatic: to honor the dead with posthumous titles is to encourage the living toward virtue.

sentences.zh: 故朝散大夫、秘書省著作郎、兼侍御史甄濟，早以文雅，見稱於時。

translations.literal: The late Grand Master of Palace Attendance, Compilation Gentleman of the Secretariat and concurrent Attendant Censor Zhen Ji, early for literary elegance was praised in his time.
translations.idiomatic: The late Zhen Ji, former grand master of palace attendance, compilation gentleman in the Secretariat, and concurrent attendant censor, was early known for his literary refinement.

sentences.zh: 嘗因辟召，亦佐戎府。

translations.literal: Once because of recruitment summons, he also assisted a military headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He had once been summoned to serve and also worked on a military staff.

sentences.zh: 而能保堅貞之正性，不履危機；

translations.literal: Yet he was able to preserve a steadfast and upright nature, not treading perilous opportunity;
translations.idiomatic: yet he preserved an upright and steadfast nature and would not enter into treacherous paths;

sentences.zh: 睹逆亂之潛萌，不從脅汙。

translations.literal: Seeing rebellion and disorder secretly sprouting, he did not follow coercion and defilement.
translations.idiomatic: when he saw rebellion brewing he refused to be coerced or corrupted.

sentences.zh: 義聲可傳於竹帛，顯贈未賁於松楸。

translations.literal: Righteous fame may be transmitted on bamboo and silk, yet manifest posthumous gifts have not adorned his pine and oak.
translations.idiomatic: His righteous fame deserves to be recorded in history, yet no posthumous honors have graced his grave.

sentences.zh: 籓方所陳，允葉彜典，追加命秩，以獎忠魂。

translations.literal: What the frontier commander stated accords with constant canonical precedent; additional ranks are to be granted to reward the loyal spirit.
translations.idiomatic: The frontier commander's memorial conforms to precedent; additional ranks shall be granted to reward his loyal spirit.

sentences.zh: 可贈秘書少監。」

translations.literal: He may be posthumously granted Vice Director of the Secretariat."
translations.idiomatic: He is hereby posthumously made vice director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 劉敦儒劉敦儒，開元朝史官左散騎常侍子玄之孫。

translations.literal: Liu Dunru—Liu Dunru was the grandson of Zixuan, Left Regular Attendant and court historian of the Kaiyuan era.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Dunru was the grandson of Zixuan, who had served as left regular attendant and as a historian during the Kaiyuan reign.

sentences.zh: 敦儒母有心疾，非日鞭人不安，子弟僕使，不勝其苦，皆逃遁他處，唯敦儒侍養不息，體常流血。

translations.literal: Dunru's mother had a heart ailment; unless daily whipping someone she was not at ease; sons, younger brothers, and servants could not endure the suffering—all fled elsewhere; only Dunru attended and nourished her without ceasing, his body often bleeding.
translations.idiomatic: Dunru's mother suffered a mental illness that could be soothed only by daily beatings; sons, servants, and attendants could not bear it and fled, but Dunru alone nursed her without rest, his body often bloody from the lash.

sentences.zh: 及母亡，居喪毀瘠骨立，洛中謂之劉孝子。

translations.literal: When his mother died, in mourning he wasted away until only bones stood; Luoyang called him Liu the Filial Son.
translations.idiomatic: After her death he mourned until he was wasted to skin and bone, and Luoyang knew him as Liu the Filial Son.

sentences.zh: 元和中，東都留守權德輿具奏其至行，詔曰：「孝子劉敦儒，生於儒門，稟此至性。

translations.literal: In the Yuanhe era, Eastern Capital Garrison Commander Quan Deyu fully memorialized his utmost conduct; the edict said: "Filial son Liu Dunru, born in a Confucian household, endowed with this supreme nature.
translations.idiomatic: During Yuanhe, Quan Deyu, garrison commander of the eastern capital, memorialized his extraordinary filial conduct, and an edict read: "The filial son Liu Dunru, born into a scholar's family, is endowed with the deepest devotion.

sentences.zh: 王祥篤行，起孝敬而不移；

translations.literal: Wang Xiang with earnest conduct arose in filial respect and did not shift;
translations.idiomatic: Like Wang Xiang, whose steadfast conduct never wavered in filial duty;

sentences.zh: 曾參養志，積歲年而罔怠。

translations.literal: Zeng Shen nourished his father's will, accumulating years without slackening.
translations.idiomatic: like Zeng Shen, who for years on end never slackened in honoring his father's wishes.

sentences.zh: 用弘勸獎，而服官常，分曹洛師，俾遂私志。

translations.literal: Use this to broadly encourage and reward; yet he shall take up regular office, assigned a post in the Luoyang command, enabling fulfillment of private intent.
translations.idiomatic: Let this serve as encouragement to others: he shall take regular office, assigned to a post in Luoyang, that he may fulfill his private wish to remain near home.

sentences.zh: 可左龍武軍兵曹參軍，分司東都。」

translations.literal: He may be Left Dragon Martial Army Army Affairs Assistant, with detached service in the Eastern Capital."
translations.idiomatic: He is appointed army affairs assistant in the Left Dragon Martial Army, with detached service in the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 高沐高沐，渤海人。

translations.literal: Gao Mu—Gao Mu was a man of Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Mu was a native of Bohai.

sentences.zh: 父憑，從事於宣武軍，知曹州事。

translations.literal: Father Ping served on the staff of the Xuanwu Army and managed affairs of Caozhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ping served on the staff of the Xuanwu Army and administered Caozhou.

sentences.zh: 李靈曜作亂，憑密遣使奏賊中事狀，詔除曹州刺史。

translations.literal: When Li Lingyao raised rebellion, Ping secretly sent envoys memorializing conditions within the rebels; an edict appointed him Prefect of Caozhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Lingyao rebelled, Ping secretly sent reports on conditions in the rebel camp and was appointed prefect of Caozhou by imperial edict.

sentences.zh: 無何，李正己盜有曹、濮，憑遂陷於賊，數年卒。

translations.literal: Before long, Li Zhengyi seized Caozhou and Puzhou by force; Ping then fell into rebel hands and died after several years.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Li Zhengyi seized Caozhou and Puzhou by force; Ping fell into rebel hands and died there several years later.

sentences.zh: 沐，貞元中進士及第。

translations.literal: Mu, in the Zhenyuan era passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Mu earned his jinshi degree during the Zhenyuan era.

sentences.zh: 以家族在鄆，李師古置為判官。

translations.literal: Because his clan and family were in Yan, Li Shigu installed him as aide.
translations.idiomatic: Because his family lived in Yan, Li Shigu appointed him as his aide.

sentences.zh: 居數年，師道擅襲，每謀不順，沐與同列郭昈、李公度等，必廣引古今成敗諭之，前後說師道為善者凡千言。

translations.literal: After several years, Shidao on his own authority succeeded to command; whenever plotting disloyalty, Mu together with colleagues Guo Huang, Li Gongdu, and others invariably broadly cited ancient and modern success and failure to instruct him—in all, before and after, more than a thousand words urging Shidao toward goodness.
translations.idiomatic: After several years Li Shidao seized command on his own authority. Whenever he plotted rebellion, Gao Mu with colleagues Guo Huang, Li Gongdu, and others would cite examples from history to warn him—altogether more than a thousand words urging him toward loyalty.

sentences.zh: 其判官李文會、孔目官林英，皆為師道信用，乘間相與涕泣於師道前曰：「文會等血誠憂尚書家事，反為高沐輩所嫉。

translations.literal: His aides Li Wenhui and chief clerk Lin Ying were all trusted by Shidao; seizing an interval they together wept before Shidao, saying: "Wenhui and others in blood sincerity worry over the minister's household affairs, yet are instead envied by the likes of Gao Mu.
translations.idiomatic: His aides Li Wenhui and chief clerk Lin Ying, whom Shidao trusted, seized a moment to weep before him and say: "We are devoted to your house, yet men like Gao Mu resent us for it.

sentences.zh: 尚書奈何不惜十二州之城，成高沐等百代之名乎！」

translations.literal: Minister, how can you not cherish the twelve prefectures' cities, yet complete the hundred-generation fame of the likes of Gao Mu!"
translations.idiomatic: Will you throw away twelve prefectures just to let Gao Mu and his kind win eternal renown!

sentences.zh: 復日夜讒構，由是漸見疑忌，令沐知萊州事。

translations.literal: Again day and night they slandered and framed him; thereby he gradually came under suspicion and distrust, and Mu was ordered to manage affairs of Laizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Day and night they slandered him until Shidao grew suspicious and sent Gao Mu to administer Laizhou.

sentences.zh: 林英因奏事至京，逼邸吏密報師道云：「高沐潛有誠款至朝廷矣！」

translations.literal: Lin Ying because of memorializing affairs reached the capital, coerced the lodge clerk to secretly report to Shidao, saying: "Gao Mu secretly has sincere allegiance reaching the court!"
translations.idiomatic: When Lin Ying went to the capital on official business he forced the lodge clerk to send a secret report to Shidao: "Gao Mu has been secretly pledging loyalty to the court!

sentences.zh: 師道大怒，李文會從而構成之。

translations.literal: Shidao was greatly angered; Li Wenhui followed by framing the case against him.
translations.idiomatic: Shidao flew into a rage, and Li Wenhui helped fabricate the case against him.

sentences.zh: 沐遂遇害於遷所，而囚郭昈於萊州，其血屬皆徙遠地。

translations.literal: Mu then met calamity at his place of transfer; Guo Huang was imprisoned in Laizhou, and his blood relations were all relocated to distant lands.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Mu was killed at his new post; Guo Huang was imprisoned in Laizhou, and their kinsmen were all exiled to distant regions.

sentences.zh: 及淮西平，師道漸懼。

translations.literal: When Huai West was pacified, Shidao gradually grew fearful.
translations.idiomatic: When the Huai West rebellion was crushed, Li Shidao grew increasingly afraid.

sentences.zh: 李公度與其將李英曇乘其懼也，說師道獻三州及入質長子。

translations.literal: Li Gongdu together with his general Li Yingtan, riding upon his fear, persuaded Shidao to present three prefectures and send in his eldest son as hostage.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gongdu and his subordinate Li Yingtan seized on Shidao's terror to urge him to surrender three prefectures and send his eldest son to court as a hostage.

sentences.zh: 初，甚然之，中悔，將殺公度。

translations.literal: At the beginning, he greatly assented to it; midway he repented and was about to kill Gongdu.
translations.idiomatic: At first he strongly agreed, but then had second thoughts and was on the verge of executing Gongdu.

sentences.zh: 賈直言聞之，謂師道用事奴曰：「今大禍將至，豈非高沐冤氣所為！

translations.literal: Jia Zhiyan heard of it and said to Shidao's steward-in-power: "Now great calamity is about to arrive — can this not be the doing of Gao Mu's wrongful-victim qi!
translations.idiomatic: When Jia Zhiyan heard what was happening, he told Shidao's chief steward, "Disaster is coming — surely this is Gao Mu's restless ghost taking revenge!

sentences.zh: 又殺公度，是益其疾也！」

translations.literal: Again to kill Gongdu — this is to increase the malady!"
translations.idiomatic: Kill Gongdu too and you will only make it worse!"

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: — and so he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: With that, he relented.

sentences.zh: 逐英曇於萊州。

translations.literal: He banished Yingtan to Laizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Yingtan into exile at Laizhou.

sentences.zh: 未至，縊殺之。

translations.literal: Before arriving, they strangled and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Before Yingtan ever reached Laizhou, they had him strangled.

sentences.zh: 又有崔承寵、楊偕、陳佑、崔清，皆以仗順為賊所惡，李文會呼為高沐之黨。

translations.literal: Further there were Cui Chengc chong, Yang Xie, Chen You, and Cui Qing — all because upholding obedience were hated by the rebels; Li Wenhu called them Gao Mu's faction.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Chengc chong, Yang Xie, Chen You, and Cui Qing likewise earned the rebels' hatred because they stood with the court; Li Wenhu denounced them as Gao Mu's clique.

sentences.zh: 沐遇害，承寵等同被囚放。

translations.literal: When Mu met harm, Chengc chong and the others alike were imprisoned and released.
translations.idiomatic: After Gao Mu was killed, Chengc chong and his companions were thrown into prison and then set free.

sentences.zh: 郭昈名亞於沐，雖不死，備嘗困辱矣。

translations.literal: Guo Kuang's name ranked next below Mu's; though he did not die, he fully tasted hardship and humiliation.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Kuang's stature fell only a step below Gao Mu's; though he survived, he endured every manner of abuse and disgrace.

sentences.zh: 及劉悟平賊，遽召李公度，執手歔欷。

translations.literal: When Liu Wu pacified the rebels, he hastily summoned Li Gongdu, clasped his hand, and sighed and wept.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Wu crushed the rebellion, he immediately sent for Li Gongdu and, taking his hand, wept aloud.

sentences.zh: 既除滑州節度，首辟昈及公度為從事。

translations.literal: Once appointed military governor of Huazhou, he first recruited Kuang and Gongdu as staff members.
translations.idiomatic: Once installed as military governor of Huazhou, he made Kuang and Gongdu his first staff appointments.

sentences.zh: 四月，詔曰：

translations.literal: In the fourth month, an edict stated:
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month, the throne issued an edict:

sentences.zh: 圖難忘死，為臣之峻節；

translations.literal: To contemplate hardship and forget not death — this is the stern integrity of a minister;
translations.idiomatic: To face peril without flinching from death — this is the loftiest integrity a subject can show;

sentences.zh: 顯忠旌善，有國之令猷。

translations.literal: To display loyalty and commend virtue is a state's worthy policy.
translations.idiomatic: To honor loyalty and reward virtue is among a state's finest principles.

sentences.zh: 日者妖豎反覆，侮我朝章，而濮州刺史高沐，劫在兇威，潛輸忠款。

translations.literal: Recently the demonic rebel turned treacherous, insulting our court's law, while Puzhou Prefect Gao Mu, seized by brutal power, secretly conveyed loyal sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: Of late the wicked rebel has turned treacherous and defied our dynasty's laws, yet Gao Mu, prefect of Puzhou, though trapped under brutal coercion, secretly pledged his loyalty to the throne.

sentences.zh: 諷其不庭之咎，將冀革心；

translations.literal: He remonstrated against the fault of not attending court, hoping they would reform their hearts;
translations.idiomatic: He admonished them for their refusal to submit to the court, hoping they might yet change their ways;

sentences.zh: 數其煮海之饒，聿求利國。

translations.literal: He enumerated the riches of salt-boiling, thereby seeking to benefit the state.
translations.idiomatic: He laid out the wealth to be gained from the salt works, all in the hope of serving the realm.

sentences.zh: 伏奏必陳於逆節，漏師常破其陰謀。

translations.literal: In secret memorials he always set forth their rebellious conduct; leaking military intelligence, he constantly thwarted their hidden plots.
translations.idiomatic: In secret memorials he always exposed their treason, and by passing intelligence to the court he repeatedly foiled their conspiracies.

sentences.zh: 竟以盜憎，遂死王事，歿而不朽，風聲凜然。

translations.literal: In the end, because the thief hated him, he died in service to the throne; though dead, he is imperishable, and his reputation stands austere and shining.
translations.idiomatic: At last the rebel lord's hatred cost him his life in the service of the state; yet death could not extinguish him, and his name endures, stern and bright.

sentences.zh: 式表漏泉之澤，且彰勁草之節。

translations.literal: Let us thereby display the bounty of subterranean springs, and moreover make manifest the integrity of hardy grass.
translations.idiomatic: Let this show forth the reward that flows even from hidden springs, and proclaim the steadfastness of grass that will not bend before the gale.

sentences.zh: 可贈吏部尚書。

translations.literal: He may be posthumously awarded Minister of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Let him be posthumously honored as Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 仍委馬總訪其遺骸，以禮收葬，優恤其家。

translations.literal: Further, Ma Zong is commissioned to search for his remains, bury them with proper rites, and extend generous relief to his family.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Zong is further charged to recover his remains, bury them with full ceremony, and see that his family receives generous support.

sentences.zh: 若有子孫，具名聞奏。

translations.literal: If there are descendants, list their names in a memorial.
translations.idiomatic: If he left descendants, their names are to be reported in a memorial to the throne.

sentences.zh: 賈直言賈直言者，父道沖，以伎術得罪，貶之，賜鴆於路。

translations.literal: Jia Zhiyan — as for Jia Zhiyan, his father Daochong, having offended through occult arts, was demoted, and on the road was granted poisoned wine.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Zhiyan — Jia Zhiyan's father Daochong had run afoul of the court through occult practices and was banished; on the road he was given poisoned wine to drink.

sentences.zh: 直言偽令其父拜四方，辭上下神祗，伺使者視稍怠，即取其鴆以飲，遂迷仆而死。

translations.literal: Zhiyan falsely had his father bow to the four directions, invoking the spirits above and below; when the envoy's attention slackened slightly, he immediately took the poisoned wine and drank it, then collapsed in a stupor and died.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyan had his father pretend to bow to the four quarters and pray to the spirits above and below; when the escort's vigilance wavered, he snatched the poisoned cup and drank it himself, then fell senseless as though dead.

sentences.zh: 明日鴆泄於足而復蘇。

translations.literal: The next day the poison drained through his feet and he revived.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the poison passed out through his feet and he came back to life.

sentences.zh: 代宗聞之，減父死，直言亦自此病蹙。

translations.literal: Emperor Daizong heard of it, reduced his father's sentence from death, and Zhiyan from this point also suffered constricted illness.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Daizong heard the story, he commuted his father's death sentence; Zhiyan himself was left lame from that day forward.

sentences.zh: 後從事於李師道。

translations.literal: Later he served on Li Shidao's staff.
translations.idiomatic: He later entered the service of Li Shidao.

sentences.zh: 師道不恭朝命，直言冒刃說者二，輿櫬說者一。

translations.literal: Shidao was disrespectful to the court's commands; Zhiyan twice risked blades to remonstrate, and once carried his coffin to remonstrate.
translations.idiomatic: Shidao defied the court's orders; Zhiyan remonstrated twice at the point of the sword and once with his coffin borne before him.

sentences.zh: 師道訖不從。

translations.literal: Shidao in the end did not comply.
translations.idiomatic: Shidao never yielded.

sentences.zh: 及劉悟斬師道，節制鄭滑，得直言於禁錮之間，又嘉其所為，因奏置幕中。

translations.literal: When Liu Wu beheaded Shidao and took control of Zheng and Hua, he found Zhiyan in confinement, admired his conduct, and thereupon memorialized to place him on his staff.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Wu killed Shidao and assumed command of Zheng and Hua, he discovered Zhiyan under house arrest, admired his courage, and had him brought onto his staff.

sentences.zh: 後遷於潞，亦與之俱行。

translations.literal: Later when he transferred to Lu, Zhiyan went with him as well.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Wu was later transferred to Lu Prefecture, Zhiyan accompanied him.

sentences.zh: 悟纖微乖失，直言必盡理箴規，以是美譽日聞於朝。

translations.literal: Whenever Wu had even slight lapses, Zhiyan always fully counseled him with reasoned admonition; on this account his good reputation daily reached the court.
translations.idiomatic: At the slightest misstep by Liu Wu, Zhiyan would offer frank and reasoned counsel; on this account his reputation for integrity spread daily at court.

sentences.zh: 穆宗以諫議大夫征之，悟拜章乞留，復授檢校右庶子、兼御史大夫，依前充昭義軍行軍司馬。

translations.literal: Emperor Muzong summoned him as Remonstrance Counselor; Wu submitted a memorial begging to retain him, and he was again appointed Acting Right Cavalry Captain, concurrently Censor-in-Chief, continuing as military adjutant of the Zhaoyi army.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Muzong summoned him to court as Remonstrance Counselor, but Liu Wu petitioned to keep him; he was reappointed Acting Right Cavalry Captain and Censor-in-Chief, and continued as adjutant of the Zhaoyi army.

sentences.zh: 悟用其言，終身不虧臣節。

translations.literal: Wu followed his counsel and never in his life failed in the integrity of a minister.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wu heeded his advice and never once fell short of a loyal subject's duty.

sentences.zh: 後歷太子賓客。

translations.literal: Later he served as Companion to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as Companion to the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 三月卒，廢朝一日，贈工部尚書。

translations.literal: In the third month he died; the court suspended audiences for one day and posthumously awarded him Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third month; the court suspended court for a day and posthumously honored him as Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 庾敬休庾敬休，字順之，其先南陽新野人。

translations.literal: Yu Jingxiu — Yu Jingxiu, style name Shunzhi; his ancestors were men of Xinye in Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jingxiu — Yu Jingxiu, courtesy name Shunzhi, came from a family originally of Xinye in Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 祖光烈，與仲弟光先，祿山迫以偽官，皆潛伏奔竄。

translations.literal: His grandfather Guanglie, together with his second younger brother Guangxian, when Lu Shan compelled them with false appointments, both secretly hid and fled.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Guanglie and Guanglie's second younger brother Guangxian, when An Lushan tried to force them into puppet office, both went into hiding and fled.

sentences.zh: 光烈為大理少卿，光先為吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: Guanglie served as Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review; Guangxian as Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Guanglie rose to Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review; Guangxian became Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 父河，當賊泚盜據宮闕，與季弟倬逃竄山谷。

translations.literal: His father He, when the rebel Zhu Ci seized the palace, fled with his youngest brother Zhuo into the mountain valleys.
translations.idiomatic: His father He, when the rebel Zhu Ci occupied the palace, fled with his youngest brother Zhuo into the mountains.

sentences.zh: 河終兵部郎中。

translations.literal: He ended his career as Director in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: He eventually served as Director in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 敬休舉進士，以宏詞登科，授秘書省校書郎，從事宣州。

translations.literal: Jingxiu passed the jinshi examination, achieved office through the Hongci exam, was appointed proofreader in the Secretariat, and served at Xuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxiu passed the jinshi examination and qualified through the Hongci literary exam; he was made a proofreader in the Secretariat and took a staff post at Xuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 旋授渭南尉、集賢校理。

translations.literal: Soon after he was appointed magistrate of Weinan and collator of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed magistrate of Weinan and collator at the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 遷右拾遺、集賢學士。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Right Remonstrance Official and Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Right Remonstrance Official and Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 歷右補闕，稱職，轉起居舍人，俄遷禮部員外郎。

translations.literal: He served as Right Supplementation Censor, performed his duties well, was transferred to Diarist of the Imperial Bedchamber, and soon promoted to Assistant Director of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He served capably as Right Supplementation Censor, became Diarist of the Imperial Bedchamber, and was soon promoted to Assistant Director of Rites.

sentences.zh: 入為翰林學士，遷禮部郎中，罷職歸官。

translations.literal: He entered service as Hanlin Academician, was promoted to Director in the Ministry of Rites, left his post and returned to his regular office.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the Hanlin Academy, was promoted to Director in the Ministry of Rites, then left that post and returned to his regular appointment.

sentences.zh: 又遷兵部郎中、知制誥。

translations.literal: He was again promoted to Director in the Ministry of War and charged with drafting imperial edicts.
translations.idiomatic: He was later promoted to Director in the Ministry of War and put in charge of drafting imperial edicts.

sentences.zh: 丁憂，服闋，改工部侍郎，權知吏部選事，遷吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: Upon bereavement, after mourning ended, he was made Vice Minister of Works, acting in charge of personnel selections, then promoted to Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: After his period of mourning ended, he was appointed Vice Minister of Works and given charge of personnel selections, then promoted to Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 上將立魯王為太子，慎選師傅，改工部侍郎，兼魯王傅。

translations.literal: When the emperor was about to establish the Prince of Lu as heir apparent and was carefully selecting a tutor, he was changed to Vice Minister of Works and concurrently Tutor to the Prince of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was preparing to install the Prince of Lu as heir apparent and was choosing a tutor with great care, Jingxiu was made Vice Minister of Works and Tutor to the Prince of Lu.

sentences.zh: 奏：「劍南西川、山南西道每年稅茶及除陌錢，舊例委度支巡院勾當，榷稅當司於上都召商人便換。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "Each year the tea tax and chumok money of Jiannan West and Shannan West circuits, by old precedent, were entrusted to the Revenue Commission's inspection offices to manage; the monopoly-tax office at the capital summoned merchants to exchange them.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial: "Under the old system, the annual tea tax and chumok fees from Jiannan West and Shannan West were handled by Revenue Commission inspection offices, with the monopoly bureau at the capital calling in merchants to exchange the proceeds.

sentences.zh: 太和元年，戶部侍郎崔元略與西川節度使商量，取其穩便，遂奏請茶稅事使司自勾當，每年出錢四萬貫送省。

translations.literal: In the first year of the Taihe era, Vice Minister of Revenue Cui Yuanlue consulted with the Jiannan West military governor, chose what was stable and convenient, and memorialized that the tea-tax affairs should be managed by the circuit office itself, remitting forty thousand strings of cash to the central government each year.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Taihe, Vice Minister Cui Yuanlue worked out an arrangement with the Jiannan West governor for a more stable procedure: the circuit would handle the tea tax itself and send forty thousand strings of cash to the capital each year.

sentences.zh: 近年已來，不依元奏，三道諸色錢物，州府逗留，多不送省。

translations.literal: In recent years they have not followed the original memorial; funds and goods of all kinds from the three circuits have been detained by prefectures and never sent to the central government.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years the original plan has not been followed; prefectures across the three circuits have been holding back various revenues and failing to forward them to the capital.

sentences.zh: 請取江西例，於歸州置巡院一所，自勾當收管諸色錢物送省，所冀免有逋懸。

translations.literal: He requested that following the Jiangxi precedent, one inspection office be established at Guizhou to manage and collect funds and goods of all kinds and send them to the central government, hoping thereby to avoid arrears.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed following the Jiangxi model by establishing an inspection office at Guizhou to collect and forward all revenues to the capital, so that nothing would remain in arrears.

sentences.zh: 欲令巡官李濆專往與德裕、遵古商量制置，續具奏聞。」

translations.literal: He wished to have inspection officer Li Fen go specially to consult with Deyu and Zungu on arrangements, and then submit a further memorial."
translations.idiomatic: He asked that inspection officer Li Fen be sent to work out the details with Deyu and Zungu, with a follow-up memorial to follow."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: — it was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 又奏：「兩川米價騰踴，百姓流亡。

translations.literal: He also memorialized: "In the two Sichuan circuits grain prices are soaring, and the common people are fleeing in exile.
translations.idiomatic: He also submitted a memorial: "Grain prices in the two Sichuan circuits have shot up, and the people are fleeing their homes.

sentences.zh: 請糶兩川闕官職田祿米，以救貧人。」

translations.literal: He requested that surplus official salary-grain from the two Sichuan circuits be sold to relieve the poor."
translations.idiomatic: He asked that surplus official salary rice from the two Sichuan circuits be sold off to aid the destitute."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: — it was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 再為尚書左丞。

translations.literal: He again served as Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was again appointed Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 三月，卒於家。

translations.literal: In the third month, he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home in the third month.

sentences.zh: 敬休姿容溫雅，襟抱夷曠，不飲酒茹葷，不邇聲色。

translations.literal: Jingxiu's bearing was warm and refined, his disposition broad and open; he did not drink wine or eat meat, and did not draw near to music and women.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxiu had a gentle, refined bearing and an open, untroubled spirit; he drank no wine, ate no meat, and kept his distance from music and women.

sentences.zh: 著《諭善錄》七卷。

translations.literal: He authored the Record of Instruction in Goodness in seven volumes.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the Record of Instruction in Goodness in seven volumes.

sentences.zh: 贈吏部尚書。

translations.literal: He was posthumously awarded Minister of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 辛讜辛讜，故太原尹雲京之孫，壽州刺史晦之猶子也。

translations.literal: Xin Dan — Xin Dan was the grandson of the former Taiyuan governor Yun Jing and the nephew of Shouzhou prefect Hui Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Dan — Xin Dan was the grandson of the former governor of Taiyuan, Yun Jing, and the nephew of Hui Zhi, prefect of Shouzhou.

sentences.zh: 性慷慨，重然諾，專務賑人之急。

translations.literal: By nature he was generous, valued keeping his word, and devoted himself to relieving others' emergencies.
translations.idiomatic: He was generous by nature, held his promises sacred, and devoted himself to helping others in distress.

sentences.zh: 年五十，不求茍進，有濟時匡難之志。

translations.literal: At fifty years of age he did not seek casual advancement and harbored the ambition to aid the age and redress difficulties.
translations.idiomatic: At fifty he still sought no easy promotion, but nursed the ambition to serve the times and rescue the realm from crisis.

sentences.zh: ，龐勛亂徐泗。

translations.literal: , Pang Xun's rebellion erupted in Xuzhou and Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Then Pang Xun's rebellion broke out in Xuzhou and Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 時杜慆守泗州，賊以郡當江淮要害，極力攻之。

translations.literal: At the time Du Tao defended Sizhou; the rebels, because the commandery stood at a critical point between the Jiang and Huai rivers, attacked with full force.
translations.idiomatic: Du Tao was then defending Sizhou; the rebels, knowing the prefecture commanded the vital junction of the Yangzi and Huai, threw everything they had against it.

sentences.zh: 時兩淮郡縣皆陷。

translations.literal: At the time all commanderies and counties of the two Huai regions had fallen.
translations.idiomatic: By then every prefecture and county on both banks of the Huai had fallen.

sentences.zh: 慆守臨淮久之，援軍雖集，賊未解圍。

translations.literal: Tao held Linhuai for a long time; although relief armies gathered, the rebels did not lift the siege.
translations.idiomatic: Tao held out at Linhuai for a long while; relief forces gathered, yet the rebels would not break off the siege.

sentences.zh: 時讜寓居廣陵，乃仗劍拏小艇趨泗口，貫城柵入城見慆。

translations.literal: At the time Dan was living at Guangling; he took up his sword, seized a small boat and rushed to Sikou, pierced through the stockade and entered the city to see Tao.
translations.idiomatic: Dan was then living at Guangling; he took up his sword, boarded a small boat, and raced to the mouth of the Si River, broke through the stockade, and entered the city to see Tao.

sentences.zh: 慆素聞有義而不相面，喜讜至，握手謝曰：「判官李延樞方話子為人，何遽至耶？

translations.literal: Tao had long heard of his righteousness though they had never met; delighted at Dan's arrival, he clasped his hand and said in thanks: "Judge Li Yan'zhu was just speaking of your character — how did you arrive so quickly?
translations.idiomatic: Tao had long known of his reputation for righteousness though they had never met; overjoyed at Dan's arrival, he took his hand and said, "Judge Li Yan'zhu was just telling me about you — how did you get here so fast?

sentences.zh: 吾無憂矣！」

translations.literal: I need worry no more!"
translations.idiomatic: My worries are over!"

sentences.zh: 時賊三面攻城，王師結壘於洪源驛。

translations.literal: At the time the rebels assaulted the city on three sides; imperial troops had encamped at Hongyuan post station.
translations.idiomatic: By then the rebels were attacking from three sides, while imperial troops had encamped at Hongyuan post station.

sentences.zh: 相顧不前。

translations.literal: They looked at one another and did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: They stared at one another and would not move forward.

sentences.zh: 讜夜以小舟穿賊壘至洪源驛。

translations.literal: Dan by night took a small boat through the rebel camp to Hongyuan post station.
translations.idiomatic: That night Dan slipped through the rebel lines in a small boat and reached Hongyuan post station.

sentences.zh: 見監軍郭厚本，論泗州危急，且宜速救，厚本然之。

translations.literal: He saw military inspector Guo Houben, explained Sizhou's dire crisis and that rescue should be hastened; Houben agreed.
translations.idiomatic: He sought out the army inspector Guo Houben, told him how desperate Sizhou's plight was, and urged immediate relief; Houben agreed.

sentences.zh: 淮南都將王公弁謂厚本曰：「賊眾我寡，無宜輕舉，當俟可行。」

translations.literal: Huainan commander Wang Gongbian told Houben: "The rebels are many and we are few — we should not act lightly; we must wait until action is feasible."
translations.idiomatic: Huainan's chief general Wang Gongbian told Houben, "The enemy outnumber us — we must not move rashly; we should wait until the moment is right."

sentences.zh: 讜坐中拔劍瞋目謂公弁曰：「賊百道攻城，陷在旦夕。

translations.literal: Dan from his seat drew his sword, glared, and told Gongbian: "The rebels assault the city on a hundred paths; it will fall at any moment.
translations.idiomatic: Dan sprang up, drew his sword, and glared at Gongbian. "The rebels are attacking on every front — the city will fall at any moment.

sentences.zh: 公等奉詔赴援，而逗留不進，更欲何為？

translations.literal: You received imperial orders to come to the rescue yet tarry without advancing — what more do you intend?
translations.idiomatic: You were ordered here to relieve the siege, yet you hold back — what do you think you are doing?

sentences.zh: 不唯有負國恩，丈夫氣義，亦宜感發！

translations.literal: Not only do you fail the grace of the state — the righteous spirit of a true man ought to be stirred to action!
translations.idiomatic: You betray not only the emperor's trust — any man of honor ought to be moved to act!

sentences.zh: 假如臨淮陷賊，淮南即是寇場，公何獨存耶！」

translations.literal: If Linhuai should fall to the rebels, Huainan itself would become enemy territory — why would you alone survive!"
translations.idiomatic: If Linhuai falls, Huainan becomes enemy ground — do you imagine you alone will be spared!"

sentences.zh: 即欲揮刃向公弁，厚本持之。

translations.literal: He was about to swing his blade at Gongbian; Houben restrained him.
translations.idiomatic: He was about to strike Gongbian with his sword, but Houben held him back.

sentences.zh: 讜望泗州大哭經日，帳下為之流涕。

translations.literal: Dan gazed toward Sizhou and wept all day; those in the tent wept for him.
translations.idiomatic: Dan turned toward Sizhou and wept all day long; the men in the tent wept with him.

sentences.zh: 厚本義其心，選勇士三百，隨讜入泗州。

translations.literal: Houben was moved by his sincerity, selected three hundred brave warriors, and followed Dan into Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by his devotion, Houben picked three hundred brave men and sent them with Dan into Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 夜半斬賊柵，大呼，由水門而入，賊軍大駭。

translations.literal: At midnight they cut through the rebel stockade, shouted loudly, entered through the water gate, and the rebel army was greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: At midnight they cut through the rebel palisade, raised a great shout, and entered through the water gate; the rebel army was thrown into panic.

sentences.zh: 既知援兵入，賊乃退舍，人心遂固。

translations.literal: Once they knew relief troops had entered, the rebels withdrew their camps, and morale in the city was thereby fortified.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels learned that reinforcements had gotten through, they pulled back, and the city's morale was restored.

sentences.zh: 浙西觀察使杜審權遣大將翟行約率軍三千赴援，屯蓮塘驛。

translations.literal: Zhexi observation commissioner Du Shenquan dispatched great general Zhai Xingyue leading three thousand troops to the rescue, encamped at Liantang post station.
translations.idiomatic: Du Shenquan, observation commissioner of Zhexi, sent his chief general Zhai Xingyue with three thousand men to the relief of Sizhou; they encamped at Liantang post station.

sentences.zh: 慆欲遣人勞之，將吏皆憚其行。

translations.literal: Tao wished to send someone to express gratitude, but officers and clerks all feared making the trip.
translations.idiomatic: Tao wanted to send someone to greet them, but every officer and clerk feared the journey.

sentences.zh: 讜曰：「杜相公以大夫宗盟，急難相赴，安得令使者無言而還！」

translations.literal: Dan said: "Commissioner Du, as a senior kinsman in the clan of great ministers, rushed to aid us in urgent crisis — how could we let the envoy return without a word!"
translations.idiomatic: Dan said, "Commissioner Du, a kinsman of the highest ministerial houses, has come to our aid in our hour of need — how can we let his envoy return without a word of thanks!"

sentences.zh: 即賫慆書幣，犒其使。

translations.literal: He immediately carried Tao's letter and gifts to reward the envoy.
translations.idiomatic: He took Tao's letter and gifts and went himself to welcome the envoy.

sentences.zh: 淮南大將李湘率師五千來援，賊詐降，敗於淮口，湘與郭厚本皆為賊所執，自是無援。

translations.literal: Huainan great general Li Xiang led five thousand troops in relief; the rebels feigned surrender and defeated them at Huaikou; Xiang and Guo Houben were both captured by the rebels — from then on there was no relief.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiang, Huainan's chief general, marched five thousand men to the rescue; the rebels feigned surrender and crushed them at Huaikou. Xiang and Guo Houben were both taken prisoner, and from that point no further aid came.

sentences.zh: 賊並兵急攻，以鐵鎖斷淮流，梯沖雲合，凡周七月，晝夜不息。

translations.literal: The rebels combined forces for urgent assault, used iron chains to block the Huai River current, scaling ladders and siege towers clouded together; for a full seven weeks day and night without cease.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels massed their forces for a furious assault, chained off the Huai River, and piled siege ladders and towers until the sky seemed dark with them; for seven weeks they attacked without pause, day and night.

sentences.zh: 乘城之士，不遑寢寐，面目生瘡，軍儲漸少，分食稀粥。

translations.literal: Soldiers on the walls had no leisure for sleep; faces broke out in sores; military stores gradually diminished; they shared thin porridge.
translations.idiomatic: The men on the walls went without sleep; sores broke out on their faces; stores dwindled, and they subsisted on thin gruel.

sentences.zh: 賴讜犯難仗義，求救於淮北諸軍。

translations.literal: Thanks to Dan, who braved danger upholding righteousness, seeking rescue from armies north of the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Only because Xin Dan risked his life on principle and pleaded for help from the armies north of the Huai did they endure.

sentences.zh: 既而馬舉以大軍至，賊解圍而去。

translations.literal: Before long Ma Ju arrived with a great army and the rebels lifted the siege and left.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Ma Ju arrived with a large army, and the rebels broke off the siege and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 讜無子，猶子山僧、元老等寄在廣陵。

translations.literal: Dan had no sons; his nephews the monk Shanseng, Yuanlao, and others were staying at Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: Dan had no sons of his own; his nephews Shanseng the monk, Yuanlao, and others were living at Guangling.

sentences.zh: 每出城，則書二姓名，謂慆曰：「誌之，得嗣為幸。」

translations.literal: Each time he left the city he would write two names, telling Tao: "Record these — if any survive, it would be my good fortune.
translations.idiomatic: Each time he left the city he would write down two names and tell Tao, "Keep a record of these — if any of them survive, count it my good fortune.

sentences.zh: 慆益感之。

translations.literal: Tao was all the more moved by this.
translations.idiomatic: Tao was deeply moved.

sentences.zh: 賊平，授讜泗州團練判官、侍御史。

translations.literal: When the rebels were pacified, Dan was appointed Registrar of the Sizhou Defense Command and Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels were crushed, Dan was made registrar on the Sizhou defense staff and investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 慆遷鄭滑節度，讜亦從之，為賓佐。

translations.literal: When Tao was transferred to command the Zheng-Hua circuit, Dan followed him as a staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: When Tao was posted as military governor of Zheng-Hua, Dan went with him as a staff officer.

sentences.zh: 慆卒，乃退歸江東，以隱居為事。

translations.literal: When Tao died, Dan retired to the Jiangdong region and made seclusion his occupation.
translations.idiomatic: When Tao died, Dan withdrew to the Jiangdong region and lived in retirement.

sentences.zh: 贊贊曰：獸解觸邪，草能指佞。

translations.literal: Commentary: Beasts can gore the wicked; grass can point out flatterers.
translations.idiomatic: The chronicler comments: Beasts know how to strike down evil; plants can expose the sycophant.

sentences.zh: 烈士徇義，見危致命。

translations.literal: Men of fierce loyalty yield to righteousness; facing danger they give their lives.
translations.idiomatic: Men of fierce loyalty surrender themselves to righteousness and, when peril comes, lay down their lives.

sentences.zh: 國有忠臣，亡而復存。

translations.literal: When a state has loyal ministers, though perished it can live again.
translations.idiomatic: When a state has loyal ministers, though it perish it may yet live again.

sentences.zh: 何以喪邦？

translations.literal: What brings a kingdom to ruin?
translations.idiomatic: What brings a kingdom to ruin?

sentences.zh: 奸邪受恩。

translations.literal: When the treacherous receive favor.
translations.idiomatic: When the treacherous are rewarded with favor.
